body:
# Website plan and publication readiness

There is enough material to define the website’s identity and build its editorial structure. A polished public launch still needs original or licensed media, local review and practical information for the journeys it recommends.

## Current technology plan

The [technology collection](../technology/index.md) records the user-agreed launch architecture and [growth roadmap](../technology/growth-roadmap.md). Use Astro/TypeScript and GitHub Pages, with Git-maintained read-only knowledge and Firebase Spark for private dynamic text. Receive photos through email or a tested free relay; publish approved copies manually through Git. AI chat, Blaze and paid private backups are deferred. These choices supersede earlier unspecified-host and account-free-intake-later proposals; implementation remains pending.

## Broad encyclopedia, connected collections

The latest user direction (30 September 2026) is to expand, relate and classify facts across Odisha. The [subject directory](../subjects/index.md) provides nine entrances spanning geography, history, people, arts, farming, environment, everyday life, economy and governance. The [classification register](../references/data/content-classification.json) assigns a primary subject and optional additional subjects to canonical records; it does not change evidence or publication status.

Tourism, food, handloom and city-experience features remain valuable collections. Health, education, livelihoods, infrastructure and public services have independent reading paths. A public entry should explain what its evidence means, show periods and caveats, and tell readers why related pages are useful. Topic association alone does not establish a causal or historical connection.

The [current PRD](../product/prd.md) retains the Painted Streets pilot and proposes non-tourism health/education and economy explainers to demonstrate breadth. Select complete, reviewed entries; a fixed page count is not the launch gate. Tourism recommendations need checked logistics, while dated statistical explanations need appropriate evidence and comparison review. A podcast and personal ventures do not determine encyclopedia coverage.

## Readiness today

| Component | State |
|---|---|
| Content architecture and editorial direction | Drafted |
| Name, palette, logo and illustration direction | First AI-generated concept kit prepared; production identity and local artist collaboration pending |
| Sourced food, textile, destination and culture nuclei | Available in this KB |
| Existing economic/city evidence and growth calculations | Preserved; calculation checks provided |
| Complete food recipes and Odia-language review | Pending |
| Maker interviews, credited portraits and verified purchase routes | Pending |
| Licensed photography and video library | Pending |
| Current travel logistics and operating information | Pending |
| User’s AI-clone service and production access | Not established in this task |

## Publishing workflow

Select a concept, complete its open research, develop the feature, confirm media rights and participant attribution, check changing facts, then record the final review. Keep the durable knowledge here even if the public copy is shorter. Each public feature should carry its KB concept IDs internally so a source update can identify affected pages.

No public website has been built or published as part of this research edition.

The user has since authorised weekly autonomous updates to the Git repository and website. The [weekly agent](../methods/weekly-data-agent.md) is active for local source monitoring and validated KB updates. Remote publication remains pending the actual GitHub connection, initial project onboarding and website deployment; this is a setup gap, not a recurring approval requirement.

## Maritime layer

Add an optional “Trade & the World” collection using the [evidence map](../history/maritime-evidence.md) and [qualified linked data](../methods/maritime-linked-data.md). Historical and contemporary layers should remain visually distinct. Each edge needs a source reveal; no diagram should imply continuous routes or causation where only an editorial pairing exists.

## Linked visitor indexes

The [visitor index](../visitor-index/index.md) now connects five areas to food, heritage and facility records. Use it for Explore, Taste and Plan your visit. Facility listings are a research seed: current operating checks, named food providers, routes and credited media remain launch requirements. The indexes are directories, not scored state rankings.

## Reader-facing statistics

Use [small, meaningful data stories](statistics-storytelling.md) throughout the website. Present visitor indexes as browsable destination, food and service cards. Keep detailed research tables in an optional evidence view. User comprehension and usefulness guide the design; large data grids are not the default public experience.

## Community encyclopedia direction

The user now wants a public, Git-backed encyclopedia with contributions through GitHub, intended owner `ahimanikya`. The [community model](community-encyclopedia.md) adds contributor review, versioned citations, corrections and explicit publication selection. The local GitHub templates and checks are prepared; the public site, remote settings and release pipeline remain to be implemented. Journalistic and government reference use is an aspiration to measure through actual citations.

## Growth-journey collection

Add four optional story entrances: [Smart cities](../journeys/smart-cities.md), [Rare earths](../journeys/rare-earths.md), [Semiconductors](../journeys/semiconductors.md) and [Investment in Odisha](../journeys/investment.md). Use one lead statistic and a dated timeline or simple chart; retain evidence-state labels. These belong within economy, infrastructure and governance, with links to relevant environmental and livelihood questions.

## Statistical atlas

A broad [source-linked atlas](../statistics/index.md) now supports concise topic stories and a district banking layer. Source conflicts and indexed-only captures are marked for further review. Research depth does not automatically make every observation ready for a public headline.


## Learning from the official tourism portal · 30 September 2026

The [reference study](../about/odisha-tourism-study.md) examines ten sampled pages and proposes place/interest/planning entrances, consistent destination modules and explicit itinerary evidence. The local visitor index now offers those reading paths. The [trip-content template](../methods/trip-planning-content.md) guides research; interactive filters, map planning, route optimisation and booking remain proposals, not additions to the launch requirements. PRD v0.2.0 and its preserved snapshots are unchanged.

## Repository integration · 1 October 2026

This imported research describes the source workspace at its recorded dates. Utkal Project already has a repository and a published preview; current authority, implementation and release status are held in [project records](../../records/index.md) and [the operating dashboard](../../registers/DASHBOARD.md). This sync adds research for review; it does not deploy these additions or replace implemented website addenda. The scheduled research queue continues in its existing workspace pending a separate canonical-workflow handover.

## Baphlimali returns · 2 October2026 UTC

The expanded mining baseline is a research candidate. Baphlimali output/payment wording has original company attribution; complex employment tables and permission/rehabilitation comparisons retain holds. No website pages were deployed by this research run.

## Forest trade follow-up · 2 October 2026 UTC

A dated Van Dhan story candidate and OFDC allocation explanation are available. The national comparison is December 2023 programme reporting, not current leadership. Editorial review remains pending; no website publication.

## Rice, place and food · 2 October 2026 UTC

Rice seed-to-food story candidate available with historical dates and participant attribution. Local/Odia review, current suppliers, tested recipes and portrait rights remain open. No website deployment.

## Rice costs and returns · 2 October 2026 UTC

# Bhubaneswar: city life with cultural depth

Bhubaneswar’s initial research file combines city indicators with cultural experiences. The stored [Ease of Living rank](../evidence/u01.md) belongs to the 2020 edition and its population category. The [Swachh Survekshan result](../evidence/u04.md) belongs to the 2024–25 edition. Neither establishes a current all-purpose “best city” claim.

## Marketing opportunity

Create a resident-hosted day: breakfast, an Old Town encounter, a craft or museum visit, and an evening chosen by an actual resident. [Korakhai](../food/korakhai.md) provides one specific food connection. [The existing visitor-experience record](../evidence/u12.md) offers starting points for further research.

## Planning and infrastructure

The [BDA town-planning mechanism](../evidence/u07.md) documents land pooling and plot readjustment. [Declarations of intention](../evidence/u08.md) are planning stages, not completed infrastructure. The [Gujarat comparator](../evidence/u10.md) prevents a misleading claim of national uniqueness.

## Research still needed

Collect neighbourhood-level transport, current public spaces, representative rents, university and workplace locations, resident interviews, venue choices and measured air-quality data. The research has not established comparative nightlife quality, broad affordability, a youth-friendliness rank or consistently low pollution. Use named experiences until those comparisons exist.

body:
# Global Connections

The Founder’s San Antonio partner-city photograph prompted a question: how can Odisha turn international relationships into useful opportunities? On 3 October 2026 he approved a website section within Utkal Project, with a dedicated initiative considered later.

Existing heritage, migration and maritime research remains relevant but does not establish modern municipal agreements or prove ancestry. This collection reuses the project’s Heritage & Global Connections Atlas ambition and adds a bounded contemporary comparison.

[Canonical comparison data](../references/data/global-connections.json) · [Operating brief](../../specs/global-connections.md)

## What the evidence supports

### Bhubaneswar

1 formal relationship verified in this review. Cupertino, United States. Cupertino records a November 2012 MoU and describes a community nonprofit supporting arts, student programmes and visits.

Limit: Bloemfontein is kept separately as a reported 2017 proposal. This is a verified minimum, not a complete municipal register.

Our interpretation: Build with the existing community bridge. Ask what help would make its next project useful to both cities.

[^global-cupertino] [^global-bloemfontein]

### Mumbai

17 names in a municipal yearbook. Examples include Los Angeles, Yokohama, Stuttgart and Shanghai. The 2025 municipal yearbook names Los Angeles, then 16 further relationships. It illustrates a much broader recorded network.

Limit: A count of names in a historical roster, not 17 programmes confirmed active today. The source uses some historic city and country names.

Our interpretation: Give relationships a durable administrative home and preserve the agreement history.

[^global-mumbai]

### Chennai

At least 3 documented partners in this sample. Denver · San Antonio · Chongqing. Denver describes student exchanges and Taste of India; San Antonio connects its annual Diwali festival to the relationship. MEA records the Chongqing agreement.

Limit: Three individually documented examples, not Chennai’s total. Described programmes do not establish their current scale or impact.

Our interpretation: Let culture create a recurring public meeting point, and connect it to learning.

[^global-denver] [^global-san-antonio] [^global-mea-china]

### Bengaluru

One organising model examined. San Francisco, United States. The SF–Bangalore initiative describes a citizen-diplomacy organisation with committees spanning culture, entrepreneurship, health and urban services.

Limit: This row examines one relationship; it does not count all Bengaluru partners. Published committee descriptions are not verified current outcomes.

Our interpretation: A civic organisation can bring people and institutions together around specific subjects.

[^global-sf-bangalore]

### Hyderabad

At least 3 named foreign municipal partners. Brisbane · Ipswich · Qingdao. Brisbane records a 2010 tripartite agreement with Ipswich and Hyderabad. MEA records a separate Hyderabad–Qingdao agreement in 2015.

Limit: Brisbane and Ipswich count as two municipalities in one agreement. Current programme activity has not been audited.

Our interpretation: A collaboration can involve more than two cities when their institutions have a shared purpose.

[^global-brisbane] [^global-mea-china]

### Pune

One long-standing cooperation examined. Bremen, Germany. Bremen’s 2021 official statement discusses its long-standing cooperation with Pune and wider academic links with India.

Limit: A dated cooperation example, not a total or a claim of a currently active exchange. Do not equate every friendship with a formal sister-city agreement.

Our interpretation: People, universities and civic groups can sustain a relationship beyond an announcement.

[^global-bremen]

## Date and count discipline

Cupertino’s current profile places designation and MoU in 2012; an earlier council report concerns the August 2011 proposal. Store agreement stages separately instead of choosing a single origin date without explanation. Mumbai’s 17 is a derived count of named entries, not a current active total. No numerical ranking is supported by these unequal source bases. No evidence here establishes aggregate Odisha coverage or a statewide total.

## Open research

Obtain BMC’s complete agreement register and dates; confirm Bloemfontein/Mangaung execution or non-execution; identify current coordinators with consent; record recent programmes, participants, costs and published outputs. Extend to Cuttack, Puri, Rourkela, Sambalpur and Berhampur without assuming they have no links. No outreach has been sent.

[^global-cupertino]: [Bhubaneswar sister-city relationship](https://www.cupertino.gov/Your-City/About-Cupertino/Sister-Cities-Friendship-Cities/Bhubaneswar-India). Official city profile; indexed full text reviewed. Reports November 2012 MoU and community programmes; not a current performance audit.
[^global-cupertino-council]: [Bhubaneswar sister-city council proposal, August 2011](https://cupertino.granicus.com/MetaViewer.php?clip_id=1186&meta_id=62504&view_id=18). 2011 council staff report; earlier process date differs from current city profile designation date. Preserve both stages.
[^global-bloemfontein]: [Odisha capital to be linked with South African city, 2017](https://sambadenglish.com/odisha-capital-to-be-linked-with-south-african-city/). News report describes a proposed MoU, not proof of its execution. Formal status unverified.
[^global-mumbai]: [English Year Book 2025: Sister City Relationship](https://portal.mcgm.gov.in/irj/go/km/docs/documents/HomePage%20Data/Whats%20New/English%20Year%20Book%202025%20Portal.pdf). Official indexed excerpt: Los Angeles in preceding paragraph plus 16 names in following list. Historical labels retained by source. Count of 17 named relationships is derived, not a verified total of currently active programmes.
[^global-denver]: [Chennai sister-city programme](https://denversistercities.org/sister-cities/chennai/). Programme body describes 1984 relationship, student exchanges and Taste of India festival. Participation and outcomes not audited.
[^global-san-antonio]: [Chennai, India](https://www.sa.gov/Directory/Departments/EDD/International-Relations/Global-Relationships/Sister-Cities/Chennai). City page lists relationship history 2008 and annual Diwali programme; also links a 2009 ordinance. Do not collapse agreement stages.
[^global-mea-china]: [Parliamentary answer: agreements during May 2015 China visit](https://meacms.mea.gov.in/Images/amb1/ru328.pdf). Official indexed table, page 5, items 20–21: Chennai–Chongqing and Hyderabad–Qingdao. Agreement record, not proof of current delivery.
[^global-sf-bangalore]: [About the San Francisco–Bangalore Sister City Initiative](https://sfbangalore.org/about/). Organisation describes 2009 formation and thematic committees. Current programme outcomes and officeholders not verified.
[^global-brisbane]: [International opportunities: Hyderabad](https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/business/business-support/international-opportunities). Hyderabad section: tripartite agreement with Brisbane and Ipswich on 5 October 2010. Two foreign municipalities in one agreement.
[^global-bremen]: [Bremen and India: cooperation with Pune, 25 November 2021](https://www.senatspressestelle.bremen.de/pressemitteilungen/buergermeister-bovenschulte-bremen-und-indien-verbinden-gute-kooperationen-373292). Dated official statement on long-standing Pune cooperation. Mentions academic links and pandemic pause; not evidence of a current operating programme.
[^global-sci]: [Sister Cities International: frequently asked questions](https://sistercities.org/faq/). Guidance on civic organisation and formal municipal relationships; membership directory is not a complete global census.

# Life in Odisha

What does access to learning, care, work and everyday services look like? Start with one measure at a time, keep the date in view, and follow it to the questions that matter for people’s lives. These are statewide observations, not a city liveability ranking.

## Learning: the scale of the school system

**61,565 schools** — Schools. Academic year 2024–25; Odisha.[^people-udise2025]

The administrative return covers all school management types in the reporting system. Count schools alongside learning outcomes, attendance, staffing and the reliability of facilities; institution counts alone do not measure education quality.

## Health: a broader reach of financial coverage

**47.9% → 82.7% of households** with at least one usual member covered by health insurance or a financing scheme, comparing NFHS-5 (2019–21) as reproduced in the NFHS-6 release with NFHS-6 (2023–24). Odisha’s latter fieldwork ran **18 July–28 November 2024**.[^people-nfhs6]

This is a survey comparison. It does not mean every household member was insured, that every claim was paid or that out-of-pocket costs disappeared. The [health evidence](../statistics/health.md) also retains maternal and child-service measures, including near-flat observations.

## Connection: a dated subscription count

**30.56 million subscriptions** — Internet subscriptions. 2026-03-31; Odisha.[^weekly-trai-mar2026]

Subscriptions are not unique people. This counts wired and wireless, broadband and narrowband connections; it does not measure speed, affordability or reliability. We do not compute an unqualified growth rate against the earlier release because some earlier operator data were carried forward.

## Build out the everyday picture

| Dimension | Evidence to explore | What readers still need |
|---|---|---|
| Work and participation | [Employment](../statistics/employment.md) and [women and inclusion](../statistics/women-and-inclusion.md) | Earnings, hours, job quality and rural–urban differences |
| Health and nutrition | [Health](../statistics/health.md) and [nutrition](../statistics/nutrition.md) | Service quality, affordability and outcomes across groups |
| Essential services | [Rural water](../statistics/rural-water.md) and [digital connectivity](../statistics/digital-connectivity.md) | Reliability and household experience, beyond recorded connections |
| City services | [Smart-city journey](../journeys/smart-cities.md) | Operating services, accessibility, maintenance and resident outcomes |
| Place differences | [Koraput](../places/koraput.md) and [Sambalpur–Bargarh](../places/sambalpur-bargarh.md) | Comparable district measures; statewide averages cannot fill gaps |

## A useful next contribution

Bring a dated district or city source with a defined population, unit and method. We can connect housing costs, commute times, air quality, public spaces, cultural activity and safety once comparable evidence is available. Keep adverse and flat results alongside improvements. Any future composite index needs transparent weights, coverage and missing-data rules; none is claimed here.


[^people-udise2025]: [UDISE+ 2024–25 Report: Existing Structure](https://dashboard.udiseplus.gov.in/report2025/static/media/UDISE%2B2024_25_Booklet_existing.118ba29d4773e6372f72.pdf).

[^people-nfhs6]: [National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6), 2023–2024: Fact Sheets](https://www.nfhsiips.in/nfhsuser/assets/National%20Family%20Health%20Survey%20%28NFHS-6%29%202023-2024%20Fact%20Sheets.pdf).

[^weekly-trai-mar2026]: [TRAI telecom performance indicators, January–March 2026](https://trai.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-06/QPIR_22062026.pdf).


## Connected reading

- [Odisha progress: what the evidence shows](progress.md) — Read infrastructure completion separately from service quality.
- [Education](../statistics/education.md) — Follow school counts to the underlying administrative definitions.
- [Health](../statistics/health.md) — Keep survey periods and household-coverage definitions visible.

# Made in Odisha

Discover the things Odisha grows, weaves and makes—and follow the people and places behind them. This collection joins craft, food and enterprise research. It is an editorial collection, not a certification label or a verified supplier directory.

## The people behind the cloth

**53,472 workers** — Handloom weavers. 2019–20 Handloom Census; Odisha.[^connect-handloom2019]

The same 2019–20 census records **64,364 allied workers**, a separate category. These historical counts make the scale of work visible; they do not establish today’s workforce, wages or growth.[^connect-handloom2019]

## Follow a product back to its place

| Explore | Read next | What to document with contributors |
|---|---|---|
| Kotpad cloth | [Kotpad](../handlooms/kotpad.md) and [Koraput](../places/koraput.md) | Maker, dye process, material, time and attributed design |
| Bandha textiles | [Sambalpuri Bandha](../handlooms/sambalpuri-bandha.md) and [Bargarh weaving](../handlooms/bargarh.md) | Workshop location, technique, product range and route to market |
| Appliqué and painting | [Pipili](../culture/pipili-applique.md) and [Raghurajpur](../culture/raghurajpur-pattachitra.md) | Artist, process, cultural context and image rights |
| Coffee and rice | [Koraput coffee](../food/koraput-coffee.md) and [Kalajeera rice](../food/koraput-kalajeera-rice.md) | Grower or producer, origin, processing, volumes and verified selling channel |
| Markets and institutions | [Boyanika](../handlooms/boyanika.md) | User-selected reference for textile categories, product presentation and buying research; follow the saved reference-use notes |

These links identify research subjects. They do not verify that a particular shop stocks an item, that a producer exports, or that a host serves a regional food.

## Food enterprises deserve their own evidence

A named dish and a named business are different records. Expand the collection with consenting cooks, processors, cooperatives and entrepreneurs. Establish who makes the product, where production occurs, how ingredients are sourced and which claims the business can substantiate. Track dated sales or production only when the units and geographic scope are clear. No verified food-enterprise sales directory is established yet.

## Connect making with the wider economy

Handlooms and food belong alongside manufacturing, logistics, finance and skills. The [industrial production](../statistics/industrial-production.md) and [exports](../trade/merchandise-exports.md) pages provide wider context; company-wide results must not be relabelled as Odisha-only production. [Progress cards](progress.md) separate proposed industrial capacity from realised output.

## The next evidence to seek

Maker income and working conditions, producer ownership, buyer access, production volumes, provenance and a comparable time series. A GI registration history does not certify every seller or establish current registry validity; check the named product and relevant registry before publishing a certification claim.


[^connect-handloom2019]: [Handloom Weavers — Parliament reply, 13 December 2019](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1596372).


## Connected reading

- [Odisha progress: what the evidence shows](progress.md) — Separate new industrial announcements from measured production.
- [Koraput: landscape, makers and everyday enterprise](../places/koraput.md) — Explore coffee and textiles through a regional profile.
- [Sambalpur–Bargarh: cloth, communities and regional enterprise](../places/sambalpur-bargarh.md) — Explore textile-linked places while preserving district boundaries.
- [Craft Livelihoods](../statistics/craft-livelihoods.md) — Read the census definitions behind the weaver and allied-worker counts.

[People and creations](../people/people-and-creations.md), [garments and markets](../handlooms/garments-and-markets.md), and [rasagola economics](../economy/rasagola-and-sweets.md) extend the collection through named contributions and scoped economic questions.

# Odisha in the world: trade, power and connections

**Geopolitics asks how geography, institutions, power and cross-border relationships shape Odisha's opportunities and constraints.** This is a research entrance assembled from saved knowledge, with a new bounded task for the missing synthesis.

## Start with existing evidence

- [Maritime evidence](../history/maritime-evidence.md) and the [connection matrix](../trade/connection-matrix.md): distinguish objects, routes, interpretations and commemorations.
- [Ports](../statistics/ports.md): cargo and connectivity evidence needs dated scope; cargo through a port is not automatically Odisha-origin exports.
- [Mining](../economy/mining.md) and [rare earths](../journeys/rare-earths.md): connect materials and industrial policy while retaining resource, capacity, proposal and output distinctions.
- [Public servants and lawmakers](../people/public-servants-and-lawmakers.md): national roles need person-specific evidence, not assumed state influence.
- [Rulers and royal legacies](../people/rulers-and-royal-legacies.md): distinguish historical boundaries and titles from the modern state.

## Questions for RES-059

How has Odisha's Bay of Bengal position mattered at different times? Which present trade and shipping relationships can be measured? What roles do ports, energy, materials, research and national institutions play? Where does Odisha participate in India's wider regional relationships? How have migration and cultural exchange connected people across borders?

Develop these questions from primary trade data, government policy, institutional records and scholarship. Separate verified events from interpretation, attributed government positions and disputed claims. Historical exchange does not prove uninterrupted modern trade or a present territorial claim. Security-related coverage should use public institutional information; research questions do not imply a particular strategic role has been established.

[Whole encyclopedia scope](../about/encyclopedia-scope.md).

[Related reading](../economy/mining.md) — Links materials research to questions about trade and policy; no strategic outcome is inferred from mineral occurrence.

# Odisha progress: what the evidence shows

A promising project can have several different kinds of evidence. Read the status next to the number. These cards retain the source’s observation date; they are not live dashboards or a claim that every project has passed through every stage.

**Planned** describes an intention or target. **Approved** records an administrative decision. **Operating** needs direct dated evidence of activity. **Measured results** need a defined outcome and period. Installed capacity and reported project completion are additional evidence categories: neither automatically establishes operation or impact.

There is no generic progress percentage or statewide investment total here. “Not established in the saved evidence” means unknown, not zero. Existing observation dates are retained; this collection does not recheck every original release.


## Homestays: an ambition to track

Status: **planned**.

**450 homestay units** — New homestay development target. 2025 scheme; validity through 31 March 2030; Odisha.[^homestay-scheme2025]

The target creates a programme to follow; it is not operating inventory.

Still to establish: Approvals under this scheme; Units open and taking bookings; Room-nights, disbursements and net host income.

[Read the underlying record](../statistics/homestays.md).

## Semiconductors: approval is a dated milestone

Status: **approved**.

**2 projects** — Odisha projects approved in August 2025 ISM decision. 2025-08-12; Odisha.[^legacy-ism]

The August 2025 ISM decision approved two named Odisha projects. Approval does not establish production or hiring.

Still to establish: Commissioning and commercial operations; Realised capital spending; Actual output and employment.

[Read the underlying record](../journeys/semiconductors.md).

## Bhubaneswar: reported project completion

Status: **reported completion**.

**31 projects** — Completed SCM projects. 2026-03-01; Bhubaneswar.[^weekly-smart-mar2026]

**32 projects** — Total SCM projects. 2026-03-01; Bhubaneswar.[^weekly-smart-mar2026]

31 of 32 Smart Cities Mission projects were reported completed at this snapshot. Completion does not establish that every service is operating reliably.

Still to establish: Operating-service verification; Maintenance, usage and resident outcomes.

[Read the underlying record](../journeys/smart-cities.md).

## Rourkela: reported project completion

Status: **reported completion**.

**73 projects** — Completed SCM projects. 2026-03-01; Rourkela.[^weekly-smart-mar2026]

**75 projects** — Total SCM projects. 2026-03-01; Rourkela.[^weekly-smart-mar2026]

73 of 75 Smart Cities Mission projects were reported completed at this snapshot. This is a project-count measure, not a liveability score.

Still to establish: Operating-service verification; Maintenance, usage and resident outcomes.

[Read the underlying record](../journeys/smart-cities.md).

## Rare earths: installed capacity, output still to establish

Status: **installed capacity**.

**11,200 tonnes per annum** — Installed mixed rare-earth chloride capacity. Plant page checked 2026-09-27; capacity effective date unspecified; OSCOM, Odisha.[^journey-irel-reep]

The OSCOM plant page states installed mixed rare-earth chloride capacity. The source does not establish the capacity effective date, current utilisation or actual annual output.

Still to establish: Dated operational status; Production and capacity utilisation; Odisha-attributable sales and jobs.

[Read the underlying record](../journeys/rare-earths.md).

## Debrigarh: reported community participation

Status: **reported activity**.

**More than 150 community members** — Community ecotourism engagement. As reported 20 August 2026; reference date unspecified; Debrigarh Wildlife Sanctuary.[^debrigarh-nie-20260820]

The dated press report attributes community engagement to the local ecotourism programme. It is not a primary payroll roster or a permanent-job count.

Still to establish: Primary dated roster and employment definition; Pay and household net income; Measured conservation outcomes.

[Read the underlying record](../places/debrigarh-hirakud.md).

# Religion and spirituality: traditions, thought and lived practice

**Explore faith as lived practice, intellectual tradition, literature and history.** Explain how people understand their traditions alongside what documentary and archaeological evidence can establish.

## Reuse and deepen

- [Jagannath Temple, Puri](../places/jagannath-temple-puri.md): RES-048 investigates origin traditions and documented temple phases; a village-to-temple account requires its own evidence.
- [Buddhist learning](../history/buddhist-learning.md): RES-045 separates learning-centre identifications, archaeological findings and historical interpretations.
- [Tantric traditions](../culture/tantric-traditions.md): RES-049 covers sites, texts and interpretations with explicit dates and attribution.
- [Mahima Dharma](../culture/mahima-dharma.md): RES-050 connects faith, philosophy, Bhima Bhoi and reading routes.

Religion and spirituality also need household practice, community traditions, sacred landscapes, plural institutions, reform, philosophy and experiences described by participants. Other religious communities and secular interpretations remain part of the wider scope; the current four entrances are a research starting point, not an exhaustive map of Odisha's beliefs.

Tradition, belief, historical inference and verified chronology have different evidence roles. Attribute claims respectfully, retain variant accounts and avoid ranking faiths or treating legend as a dated event. A place of worship may connect to food, literature, music, livelihoods and architecture without being reduced to a visitor attraction or revenue source.

Existing RES-045 and RES-048–050 retain their IDs and completion criteria. Further traditions should receive bounded tasks when the saved coverage-gap review identifies an absent deliverable.

[Whole encyclopedia scope](../about/encyclopedia-scope.md).

[Related reading](../culture/mahima-dharma.md) — Connects a named tradition to the wider faith collection while preserving its own history and literature.

## Yogini architecture and religious contexts

[Hirapur](../places/hirapur-yogini.md) and [Ranipur-Jharial](../places/ranipur-jharial-yogini.md) now have distinct archaeological evidence records. [Read the comparative account](../culture/tantric-traditions.md), including attributed dates, sculpture-count limits and the distinction between Shaiva/Shakta and Buddhist contexts.

## Mahima Dharma and a credited reading route

[Stuti Chintamani](../works/stuti-chintamani.md) now records named English editions and translators. [Mahima Dharma](../culture/mahima-dharma.md) connects them to Joranda, Khaliapali and attributed historical scholarship while reusing the existing Bhima Bhoi literary profile.

# Boita Bandana: honouring the maritime trader

## Sourced knowledge

In Boita Bandana, miniature boats carrying lamps are set afloat in remembrance of maritime journeys. A 2025 Ministry of Culture account connects this practice with Bali Jatra in Cuttack, a festival commemorating trade and cultural exchange between Odisha and Southeast Asia, particularly Bali.[^maritime-culture-2025]

## Editorial interpretation

“A culture that honours its traders” is a defensible contemporary framing of this remembrance. “A celebration of entrepreneurial courage” can be used as our interpretation, rather than as a claim about the festival’s single original purpose.

The ritual carries cultural and devotional meanings as well. Neither participation nor commemoration measures how entrepreneurial all residents are.

## Connect it to action

Use the [Paradip event](../trade/paradip-bridge.md) for a documented institutional connection and [Bali Jatra commerce](../trade/baliyatra-commerce.md) for an attributed present-day sales measure.

[Bali Jatra](bali-yatra.md) · [Campaign](../stories/trading-culture-next-chapter.md)

# Dalkhai

**Dalkhai connects dance, song and festive community life in western Odisha.** Sambalpur district’s cultural account names young women from Binjhal, Soura and Mirdha communities, dancing in a line or semicircle during Dussehra, Bhaijuntia and other occasions. This is the district’s account, not an exclusive list of communities or a claim that every performance follows one format. [District description](https://sambalpur.odisha.gov.in/en/tourism/culture-Heritage).

A Ministry of Culture panel dated **1 March 2024**, entry592, names **Dhyanananda Panda / PRATIVA (A Tribal Folk Akademy), Bhawanipatna**, and links a Dalkhai clip. This connects the tradition to a credited practitioner/group without assigning them authorship of the whole tradition. The duplicate clip link in the register is one route, not two works. [Register, p.255](https://www.indiaculture.gov.in/sites/default/files/pdf/Folk_Dance_as_on_01.03.2024-223-255.pdf).

Performance date, individual dancers, song text, translation, current bookings and video rights remain unverified. No statewide practitioner count or earnings estimate is inferred.

## Viewing route checked · 1 October 2026

The register’s [linked video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1-krCpUX6TE) opens as **TRIBAL INDIA 2017 @ Red Lotus Events ®**, streamed live on **21 July 2017**, on Red Lotus Events’ channel. Muted playback progressed to00:39 in this session. The uploader supplies no description or performer credits: PRATIVA/Dalkhai attribution therefore remains the government register’s, not independently confirmed by the video metadata. Full performance, music and individual identities were not reviewed; no download or reuse permission is implied.

# Odisha through dance, music and their makers

**Follow an art form to its people, a credited work, and a place.** This collection opens several routes through Odisha’s cultural life, without treating every dance as Odissi or every musician with an Odisha career as Odisha-born.

| Start with | Follow the evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Odissi | Mahari, Gotipua, theatre and modern collaborative codification; practitioner testimony kept distinct from archival chronology |
| Mayurbhanj Chhau | An unmasked regional style and a credited 2024 New York programme |
| Dalkhai | Western Odisha community occasions and a named group in the 2024 cultural panel |
| Ghumura | Kalahandi festival practice and a named practitioner/group research route |
| Ranapa | Ganjam stilt performance and a dated 2016 national-festival record |
| Hariprasad Chaurasia | AIR Cuttack, Bhubaneswar teaching and an English biography |

**Editorial story proposal:** “Many rhythms, one Odisha.” A map could lead readers from a tradition to a credited programme and an attributed listening or reading route. This is a proposed presentation, not an audience-tested campaign or a public release.

Current performances, teaching availability, practitioner earnings and media rights are separate research fields. Programme credits do not establish origin, universal practice or commercial success.

[Related reading](odissi.md) — Connects practitioner testimony to the existing account of Odissi development.

[Related reading](mayurbhanj-chhau.md) — Connects a regional tradition to a credited international programme.

[Related reading](dalkhai.md) — Connects a community dance to occasions and a named research route.

[Related reading](ghumura.md) — Connects Kalahandi festival practice to its documented practitioner register.

[Related reading](ranapa.md) — Connects Ganjam performance culture to a dated national-festival record.

[Related reading](../people/hariprasad-chaurasia.md) — Connects Odisha career and teaching evidence to an English reading route.

## Listen with the credits in view

[Chaurasia’s Odia film-music chapter](../people/hariprasad-chaurasia.md) now links three Saregama song chapters and separates singer, lyricist and joint music-director roles. [Dalkhai’s viewing note](dalkhai.md) records a playable register-linked clip while retaining its missing uploader credits. Availability checks are dated and do not grant reuse rights.

body:
# Mahima Dharma and Bhima Bhoi

**Bhima Bhoi provides a connection between faith, literature and concern for human suffering.** In a [2 March 2024 address](https://presidentofindia.nic.in/press_releases/president-india-addresses-meeting-mahima-cult), the President described Mahima Gosein as the movement’s initiator and Bhima Bhoi’s poems, songs and speeches as expressions of equality. This is evidence of a public interpretation, not a complete religious history.

The repository already contains a literary introduction based on Sitakant Mahapatra’s *Bhima Bhoi*, published by Sahitya Akademi. Its saved inspection records uncertainty in biography (pp. 1–2), Khaliapali (pp. 12–13) and compassion (pp. 27–28). We reuse that bounded capture rather than create an independently verified duplicate. [Monograph](https://sahitya-akademi.gov.in/pdf/Bhima-Bhoi.pdf).

The initial research questions concerned the founder’s chronology, Alekha, Joranda and Khaliapali, orders and credited English translations. The sections below address those questions within the inspected sources; exact biographical details and present-day practice remain open.

The canonical website narrative remains in the project’s `kb/research/voices/collection.json`; this page adds the religious-history research scope, rather than replacing that literary entry.

[Related reading](../history/buddhist-learning.md) — Offers comparative reading about distinct religious and learning traditions; no common origin or doctrinal equivalence is asserted.

## A faith expressed through poetry

Mahima Swami, also called Mahima Gosain, is described as the movement’s founder; Bhima Bhoi gave its ideas a widely remembered poetic voice. The existing literary introduction remains the person’s canonical narrative. This extension adds historical context and [credited reading routes](../works/stuti-chintamani.md).

### Alekha and the formless divine

Mahapatra’s monograph explains **Alekha** as indescribable and **nirakara** as formless, alongside other names for the divine. Its discussion of **sunya** belongs to a particular religious and literary interpretation. The use of a shared term does not make Mahima Dharma identical to Buddhist philosophy, nor establish one undisputed origin. [Mahapatra, printed pp. 17–20; PDF pp. 24–27](https://sahitya-akademi.gov.in/pdf/Bhima-Bhoi.pdf). These are descriptions of belief, not scientific claims.

### Joranda and Khaliapali have different roles

| Historical connection | Source and limit |
| --- | --- |
| Mahima Gosain’s death in 1876 and Joranda’s emergence as a major centre | Mahapatra, p.12; historical synthesis, not a death certificate |
| Bhima Bhoi’s move to Khaliapali and the ashram’s activity from 1877 | Mahapatra, pp.12–13; the account also credits Ma Annapurna’s supervision |
| Religious narratives collected at Khaliapali and other western Odisha sites in 2000–2001 | Johannes Beltz, pp.230–232; his fieldwork, not interviews conducted by Utkal |

[Mahapatra](https://sahitya-akademi.gov.in/pdf/Bhima-Bhoi.pdf) · [Beltz’s original chapter](https://publikationen.uni-tuebingen.de/xmlui/bitstream/handle/10900/138250/Beltz_035.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1). Keep the nineteenth-century narrative, the later fieldwork period and present-day visitor conditions separate. The older monograph’s district labels are historical source geography, not a current administrative directory.

### Different orders and remembered lives

Beltz discusses **Balkaladhari** and **Kaupinadhari** orders, their distinctive dress and differences over authority and Bhima Bhoi’s reception. This is evidence of diversity within the tradition; one account cannot stand for every adherent or today’s institutional arrangements. His chapter distinguishes hagiography—stories expressing religious meaning—from a reconstruction of verifiable life events. [Beltz, pp.230–238,244–245; note 29, p. 251](https://publikationen.uni-tuebingen.de/xmlui/bitstream/handle/10900/138250/Beltz_035.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1).

| Biographical question | Reconciled editorial treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Exact birth date and birthplace | Retain nineteenth-century context; do not select one precise date/place from competing narratives |
| Blindness | Preserve differing biographical and hagiographic readings; no medical history inferred |
| Kandha/Kondh background and family stories | Attribute reported community connections; miraculous/adoption stories are not documentary genealogy |
| Accounts linking him to the 1881 Puri incident | Mahapatra contests the claimed personal involvement; original administrative/temple records have not been examined here |

This reconciles how the evidence is presented, not every historical disagreement. The original literary page already preserved uncertainty; the new scholarship strengthens that approach. [Mahapatra, pp.1–2,13–15](https://sahitya-akademi.gov.in/pdf/Bhima-Bhoi.pdf); [Beltz, pp.230–238](https://publikationen.uni-tuebingen.de/xmlui/bitstream/handle/10900/138250/Beltz_035.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1).

### Read in English, with credits

NBT’s 2026 catalogue identifies a 2024 English edition translated by **Satyananda Swain**, 302 pages, ISBN 9789357438629. A separate 2024 anthology edited by **Nishamani Kar** includes selected cantos translated by **Gagan Behari Das**. The [work record](../works/stuti-chintamani.md) keeps those editions distinct and identifies what was actually inspected.

No follower census, present ritual schedule, current site access or newly conducted interview is established. The legal open-access chapter and freely hosted monograph are reading routes; their availability does not grant reuse rights for photographs, complete translations or recordings.

# Odissi

## Sourced knowledge

The tourism profile presents Odissi as a classical dance tradition.[^odissi]

## Story opportunity

*Editorial proposal; audience response has not been measured.*

## Next research

## Connections

[Related knowledge](konark-dance-festival.md) · [Research standards](../about/research-method.md)

[^odissi]: [Odissi Dance](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/experience/themes/odissi-dance.html)

## People, roles and archives

[Kelucharan Mohapatra](../people/kelucharan-mohapatra.md), [Laxmipriya Mohapatra](../people/laxmipriya-mohapatra.md), [Sanjukta Panigrahi](../people/sanjukta-panigrahi.md) and [Raghunath Panigrahi](../people/raghunath-panigrahi.md) offer specific research paths through choreography, performance, teaching and music. Early mixed-style theatre episodes remain distinct from later Odissi repertoire. Archival listings do not establish a current public performance or reusable recording.

## Origins and revival: expanded research · 1 October 2026

[Sujata Mohapatra’s account](https://sujatamohapatra.org/about-guru-kelucharan-mohapatra/) connects Kelucharan’s early Gotipua experience and later research into Mahari and Gotipua traditions with his dance practice and teaching. Retain this as an attributed practitioner account. The existing theatre episodes and Laxmipriya record should remain part of the story.

Ancient sculptural evidence, ritual practice, theatre and twentieth-century reconstruction are different layers of evidence. Do not describe Kelucharan as the sole inventor or imply that the modern repertoire has remained unchanged since antiquity. Odisha Tourism’s early-date wording involving “Udayagiri Monastery” needs identity checking against the Jain caves and separate Buddhist site before reuse.

The wider dance programme will also examine Gotipua, Mahari, Mayurbhanj Chhau and regionally named community dances, with credited practitioners and recorded works. Odisha’s dance culture is broader than this Odissi page.

## Distinct traditions and a modern collaborative repertoire

In an edited **2018 interview**, Mayadhar Raut describes Mahari and Gotipua as different practices: he associates Mahari with temple dancers and explains that Gotipua included acrobatic bandha movements. He recalls theatre training, work with Pankaj Charan Das, and later study at Kalakshetra. His account of Jayantika describes practitioners comparing movement with texts and combining selected elements, rather than simply preserving an unchanged repertoire. [Interview and translation](https://www.sahapedia.org/conversation-guru-mayadhar-raut-odissi).

This supports a story with several contributors: temple practice, boy-performer traditions, theatre, teachers, textual study and twentieth-century collaboration. Raut names Kelucharan Mohapatra among the collaborators. His September 1959 Jayantika date remains attributed oral history, not an inspected founding minute. We have not adopted the interview’s uncorroborated claims of being first to introduce particular elements.

The [existing theatre episodes](../people/kelucharan-mohapatra.md) retain their original dates and role credits. Choreography, performance, music and institutional teaching are distinct contributions.

body:
# Pala and its culture

Pala belongs at the meeting point of performed poetry, musical storytelling and community life. A 2012 festival account connects these ballad traditions with literature, rhythm, humour and epic narratives. [Pala and Daskathia Utsav](https://www.narthaki.com/info/rev12/rev1245.html).

## How to begin listening

Listen for the story, the explanation of a verse and the exchange between the lead voice and accompanying performers. The official 2025 Sammilan account explicitly credits singers and Bayaks for communicating Odia poetry. [48th annual state-level Pala Sammilan at Parklane, Kendujhar](https://cm.odisha.gov.in/en/latest-news/participated-48th-annual-state-level-pala-sammilan-organized-parklane-kendujhar). Detailed roles, instruments and local terminology need an attributed demonstration before becoming a performance manual.

## Forms and history: preserve the source’s vocabulary

Dash’s January 2011 article distinguishes **Pothi Pala** performed seated, **Thia Pala** performed standing, and **Badi Pala**, where singers take turns on a stage. These notes come from the indexed passage at printed page 73; direct PDF access failed. [The Socio-Cultural Value of Odia Folkdance: Pala](https://magazines.odisha.gov.in/Orissareview/2011/Jan/engpdf/72-74.pdf).

A full history needs separately examined evidence for Satyanarayana/Satyapir associations, manuscript dates, teacher lineages and later stage practice. Those are research questions here. A devotional origin account cannot supply a verified founding date; older claims of decline do not measure the present condition.

## Performers and repertoire

The 2009 Sangeet Natak Akademi citation recognises **Jagannath Behera** for Pala theatre and names his teachers. The indexed citation is retained with its full-PDF access gap; its historical age and offices must not become present-day claims. [Jagannath Behera — Akademi Award: Pala (Orissa)](https://sangeetnatak.gov.in/public/uploads/awardees/docs/Jagannath_Behera.pdf).

A contemporary report of the 19–21 July 2012 festival at Rabindra Mandap provides these credited examples:

| Performer | Presentation as reported |
|---|---|
| Santilata Sahu | Hanuman’s meditation in Dwapara Yuga |
| Manorama Panda | Naga Jyoti |
| Kumudini Patel | Sasirekha Parinaya |
| Madanamohana Jena and troupe | Papamochan Yajna |
| Laxman Charan Rout and troupe | Mahadani Ajigarta |

[Pala and Daskathia Utsav](https://www.narthaki.com/info/rev12/rev1245.html). These are dated performance credits, not a complete artist directory. The women performers deserve their own researched biographies. Keep Pala and Daskathia distinct even when a festival presents both.

## A living archive and a dated gathering

The [Shree Jagannath Pala Research Foundation](https://www.sjprf.in/) offers routes to performer material and documentary notices. Its [Pala Kabita catalogue](https://sjprf.in/index.php/pala-kabita) records author attributions, including Bhagabata Bandana by Sarat Chandra Dash. These are useful discovery routes; recordings, editions, translations and rights need item-level checks.

The Chief Minister’s office dates its report of the **48th annual state-level Pala Sammilan in Kendujhar to 28 December 2025**. [48th annual state-level Pala Sammilan at Parklane, Kendujhar](https://cm.odisha.gov.in/en/latest-news/participated-48th-annual-state-level-pala-sammilan-organized-parklane-kendujhar). This establishes a reported gathering and edition number; attendance, artist totals, payments and current booking availability remain unknown.

## Story opportunity

**An evening where poetry becomes performance.** Follow a named artist from choosing a text to explaining it to an audience; credit accompanying artists and the community that hosts the performance. This is an editorial proposal, not a filmed or interviewed story.

## Next research

Recover the two government PDFs; verify performer biographies and women’s participation through independent records; catalogue named texts and legally viewable recordings; document instruments, apprenticeship and community settings. Add dated troupe, funding or earnings statistics only when units and coverage are clear. No local interview, Odia review, verified event calendar or media licence is claimed.

[odissi](odissi.md) — Related reading on Odisha’s performance traditions; no claim that the two forms are identical.

[people and creations](../people/people-and-creations.md) — Connects named performers with the existing people-and-works research framework; performance credit is not a completed biography.

## Source recovery follow-up · 1 October 2026

The Behera award citation has now been retrieved and its one-page text checked. The earlier indexed-only limitation is resolved for that citation alone; see its [updated source record](../sources/pala-sna-behera2009.md). Dash’s 2011 paper remains a full-text gap: direct retrieval encountered an expired TLS certificate, and the search service could not fetch the full issue. No certificate check was disabled. A [feature draft](pala-feature-draft.json) is prepared for editorial development; it is not included in the public website edition.

body:
# Tantric traditions: sites, texts and interpretations

**Odisha’s Yogini temples tell a story through circles, sculpture and the relationship between goddesses and Shiva.** Start with two distinct places: [Hirapur](../places/hirapur-yogini.md) in Khordha and [Ranipur-Jharial](../places/ranipur-jharial-yogini.md) in Balangir. Their open-air architecture gives this heritage collection a strong visual identity without needing claims of national uniqueness.

## Two places, different evidence

| What to notice | Hirapur | Ranipur-Jharial |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Form | Circular sanctuary, eastern projection and central mandapa | Circular sanctuary and central pillared mandapa |
| Divine figures | Yoginis, Bhairavas and exterior Katyayini figures | Yoginis surrounding a central eight-armed dancing Shiva |
| Material or scale recorded | Sandstone structure; black-chlorite interior images | 16.60 m external and 13.60 m internal diameter |
| Dating in the IGNCA inventory | Early tenth century, argued from style; Bhaumakara attribution | Ninth–tenth centuries with early tenth specified; Somavamsi attribution |

Sources: IGNCA’s [Hirapur inventory, pp.1–3](https://ignca.gov.in/asi_reports/orkhurda040.pdf) and [Ranipur-Jharial inventory, pp.1–3](https://ignca.gov.in/asi_reports/orbolangir001.pdf). These are institutional heritage inventories, not original foundation inscriptions. Neither carries a survey/publication date. Their named listers and reviewers are credited in the source records; Utkal has not obtained human review.

## Three contexts to distinguish

**Yogini** names a category of divine figures and associated traditions; it does not identify one uniform religion or modern yoga practice. **Shakta** describes a goddess-centred emphasis, while **Shaiva** refers to Shiva-related traditions. At these sites, Yogini and Bhairava/Nataraja imagery should be read together, without requiring the two emphases to be mutually exclusive.

**Buddhist Vajrayana** has its own Yogini-tantra traditions. Shaman Hatley’s openly available scholarly introduction discusses both Shaiva Bhairava traditions and Buddhist Yogini texts. Shared terminology creates a subject for comparison; it does not establish that either Odisha temple was a Buddhist monastery or that all these traditions followed one lineage. [Hatley, 2020, Introduction](https://academic.oup.com/reference/62357/reference-article-abstract/554513529).

## A textual connection worth investigating

Sabbi Lall’s SOAS report of Hatley’s 2020 lecture describes possible parallels between Hirapur’s images and goddesses in the Devīpurāṇa. The reported argument stops short of asserting that the text inspired the temple. Keep this as an **attributed iconographic hypothesis**, with the text’s date, edition and relevant passages still to examine. The lecture recording and original Sanskrit passages have not been reviewed here. [SOAS report, 14 January 2021](https://blogs.soas.ac.uk/yoga-studies/2021/01/14/in-search-of-yoginis/). The report and Hatley’s Oxford entry share a scholar; they are not independent confirmation.

## What stays open

- **Hirapur’s date and patronage:** Odisha Tourism’s saved account gives the ninth century and Hiradevi; IGNCA argues early tenth century and names the Bhaumakaras generally. Preserve both attributions pending inscription-level or specialist review.
- **Ranipur-Jharial’s image count:** the inventory states 65 niches, but its categories total 66 (48 + 11 + 7). No corrected count is invented, and no current surviving-image total is published.
- **Ritual and access:** IGNCA labels Hirapur living and Ranipur-Jharial non-living, without a survey date. These labels cannot establish present practice, availability or an unbroken ritual tradition. Its brief Kapalika attribution is not enough to reconstruct historical rites.
- **Text and transmission:** direct passage-level links with Buddhist or Jagannath traditions remain unestablished. No secrecy-based promotional claims, supernatural claims as fact, or undocumented origin chain is adopted.

## Editorial story seed

**A circle of goddesses, a sky above.** Explore Odisha’s Yogini heritage through two places whose architecture invites a closer look at sculpture, belief and preservation. This is draft campaign language grounded in form; photographs, visitor details and publication still need their own checks.

[Structured evidence](../references/data/culture-learning.json) retains individual claims, locators and conflict flags. [Related reading](../history/buddhist-learning.md) — Points to questions about Buddhist Vajrayana while keeping Buddhist and Yogini/Shakta histories distinct.

body:
# Odisha’s universities: institutions and evidence

**Compare institutions by their role, legal category and dated evidence.** The [Higher Education Department directory](https://dhe.odisha.gov.in/en/universities/list-of-univerisities-in-odisha) supplies the following starting selection, not a best-university league table or a complete statewide census.

| Directory category | Selected institutions to profile |
| --- | --- |
| State public | Utkal, Ravenshaw, Sambalpur, Berhampur, OUAT, Utkal University of Culture, Odisha State Open University, National Law University Odisha |
| Central | Central University of Odisha |
| State private | Centurion, Sri Sri, Birla Global, ASBM, GIET, Silicon |
| Deemed to be university | KIIT, Siksha ‘O’ Anusandhan, KISS |

Deemed status is a legal category; it does not itself establish government ownership. Directory inclusion does not verify current programme approval, admissions, accreditation or every institutional name change. IIT, NIT, NISER, IISER and AIIMS coverage needs a separate institution-type check.

**One dated finding:** NIRF’s **2025 University category** places **Siksha ‘O’ Anusandhan 15th** (63.14) and **KIIT 17th** (62.87). These are India ranks in that category, not ranks among all institutions or subject-specific outcomes. [Original ranking table](https://www.nirfindia.org/Rankings/2025/UniversityRanking.html).

The attempted 2026 table could not be retrieved. These numbers are explicitly 2025; no latest-ranking claim is made.

The initial research agenda covered UGC identities, establishment dates and comparative performance. The checkpoint below completes selected identity and outcome checks; discipline-specific strengths and broader outcome coverage remain to be expanded. Keep score, rank, category and year together; do not infer growth from rank movements alone.

## Identity check: eighteen existing entries verified

On 2 October 2026 UTC, the UGC public register was checked against all 18 institutions already selected above. The source’s institution IDs, names, state, type and status are retained in the [structured record](../references/data/culture-learning.json). This is our selected directory, not Odisha’s total institution count. [UGC register](https://www.ugc.gov.in/universitydetails/university?type=MuOh4z0uqRaY2k8Ag10I0g==).

### Establishment has several dates

| Institution | What the original record establishes |
| --- | --- |
| Utkal University | State category in UGC; section 3(1)(i) of the 1989 Act continues the identity under the 1966 Act. These dates do not replace its earlier foundation history. |
| Central University of Odisha | Central category; the 2009 Act’s First Schedule names Central University of Orissa. The Act’s commencement 15 January 2009 and assent 20 March 2009 are separate events. |
| Centurion, Odisha | Private category; the 2010 Act describes a self-financed private university. Establishment notification effective 23 December 2010 follows the Act’s August assent/publication. |
| KIIT | UGC deemed-category register date 16 February 2004 |
| SOA | UGC deemed-category register date 17 July 2007 |
| KISS | UGC deemed-category register date 25 August 2017 |

[Utkal Act,p.4](https://utkaluniversity.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/University-Act.pdf) · [Central Act,pp.1,3,17](https://cup.edu.in/sites/default/files/Documents/Gazette.pdf) · [Centurion Act](https://cutm.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/1355.pdf) · [Centurion establishment](https://cutm.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/2160.pdf) · [UGC deemed register](https://deemed.ugc.ac.in/Home/ListOfDeemedToBeUniversity).

These historical Acts establish identity, not a review of all later amendments. Centurion’s 2013 UGC letter approves a compliance report after an expert visit; it is not a blanket present-day programme approval. The Andhra Pradesh Centurion entry is a different UGC identity. Utkal University and Utkal University of Culture also remain distinct. [2013letter,p.1](https://cutm.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/4992496_CenturianUniversity.pdf).

## Read performance through more than one measure

SOA and KIIT have dated national visibility in NIRF’s University category. SOA’s published score moved 62.61→63.14 from 2024 to 2025 while its rank moved 14→15; KIIT’s score moved 62.53→62.87 while its rank moved 15→17. Both rank declines remain visible alongside the score increases. Teaching/resources, research/professional practice, graduation outcomes, inclusion and perception component scores are saved separately. These are ranking measures, not direct learning tests or research-impact estimates.

**Utkal University is in the 101–150 University band in both 2024 and 2025.** Alphabetical order inside the band does not supply an exact rank, and an unchanged band does not establish an unchanged score. [2024band](https://www.nirfindia.org/Rankings/2024/UniversityRanking150.html) · [2025band](https://www.nirfindia.org/Rankings/2025/UniversityRanking150.html).

### Graduate outcomes: optional evidence view

The following are institutional submissions to NIRF 2025, **four-year undergraduate programmes**, grouped by graduation year. Disciplines may differ between universities and cohorts. Pay is nominal annual median among placed graduates only.

| Institution / graduating year | Graduated in minimum time | Placed | Selected for higher study | Median annual pay of placed graduates |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SOA 2021–22 | 1,978 | 1,595 | 207 | ₹4.50 lakh |
| SOA 2022–23 | 2,453 | 2,205 | 235 | ₹5.75 lakh |
| SOA 2023–24 | 2,471 | 2,218 | 237 | ₹6.00 lakh |
| KIIT 2021–22 | 4,162 | 4,021 | 141 | ₹9.00 lakh |
| KIIT 2022–23 | 3,878 | 3,769 | 109 | ₹9.50 lakh |
| KIIT 2023–24 | 3,611 | 3,513 | 98 | ₹9.70 lakh |

[SOA submission,p.2](https://www.nirfindia.org/nirfpdfcdn/2025/pdf/University/IR-O-U-0363.pdf) · [KIIT submission,p.2](https://www.nirfindia.org/nirfpdfcdn/2025/pdf/University/IR-O-U-0356.pdf). KIIT’s reported placed count falls as the graduating cohort shrinks; the rising pay figure should not conceal that. These are different cohorts, not the same individuals’ pay growth. They are not independent job audits, state employment totals or student return-on-investment estimates. KIIT’s first-year admission figures exceed its stated intake for these cohorts; retain that scope question before deriving utilisation or completion rates.

### Connections and next evidence

[Achyuta Samanta](../people/achyuta-samanta.md) connects to KIIT and KISS institution-building; the KISS deemed-status date must not settle an earlier school-founding dispute. [Buddhist learning](../history/buddhist-learning.md) offers a separate historical reading path without claiming institutional continuity. [The public story](../stories/odisha-university-evidence.md) turns selected evidence into a readable card.

Further profiles should add discipline-specific work and comparable public/central/private graduate cohorts. IIT, NIT, NISER, IISER and AIIMS need their own institutional and campus identities. Current programme approvals, admissions, costs, 2026 rankings and independent employment evidence remain open.

[Related reading](../people/achyuta-samanta.md) — Separates institutional legal milestones from a founder’s biography.

## School, university and institutional outcomes · 2 October 2026 UTC

[Samanta’s expanded record](../people/achyuta-samanta.md) adds original KISS university notification evidence, a KIIT continuation instrument, Parliament service and university-only signed financial statements. The KISS school and university are explicitly distinct. Existing KIIT graduate cohorts remain canonical here and are linked, not duplicated.

## KISS student evidence · 2 October 2026 UTC

The [Samanta/KISS record](../people/achyuta-samanta.md) now links postgraduate stock and tuition support, annual doctoral completions, and AQAR pass/placement fields. School populations stay separate. The higher-study count refers to the previous graduating batch, so it cannot be combined with current placements. The canonical observations are in culture-learning.json under kiss_outcomes_checkpoint; they are not duplicated as statewide education totals.

body:
# Kodingamali and Baphlimali: output, processing and accountability

**Two bauxite mines, two different stories.** OMC’s Kodingamali adds a regulator-recorded output series. Baphlimali connects a mine to the Utkal Alumina refinery and an international certification record. Neither capacity nor certification measures mineral revenue or household prosperity.

## Kodingamali: consistent output, a separate expansion plan

IBM’s September 2024 inspection records **3 million tonnes of ROM bauxite in FY2023–24**, against a 6 million-tonne proposal. It explicitly identifies a 3 MTPA environmental-clearance constraint. This is a historical inspection, not confirmation of today’s permission.

| Financial year | Actual ROM tonnes | Proposed tonnes |
|---|---:|---:|
|2019–20|3,000,000|3,000,000|
|2020–21|2,999,500|6,000,000|
|2021–22|3,000,000|6,000,000|
|2022–23|3,000,000|6,000,000|
|2023–24|3,000,000|6,000,000|

Five observations span four elapsed years: this is a broadly flat series. The register identifies OMC, mine code 07ORI09005 and Koraput. Its non-captive classification does not identify a buyer. Rehabilitation-area observations remain held until their annual/cumulative basis is clear. [IBM, PDF pp.1–5](https://ibm.gov.in/writereaddata/files/172965925667188178a68e6MCDR_Inspection_Report_202324_KBM.pdf).

## Baphlimali: a documented mine-to-refinery link

The ASI audit describes bauxite travelling by covered conveyor to Utkal Alumina’s refinery. Its overview reports approximately 1,017 people, including 82 women, and 8.5 MTPA capacity. These are audit-period site figures; local residence and comparable workforce categories remain unverified. The annual-return follow-up below supplies a separate FY2024–25 output measure. The overview describes a lease spanning Rayagada and Kalahandi, so the registered district alone must not become a whole-mine geographic boundary. [Audit, PDF p.4](https://aluminium-stewardship.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ASI-Audit-Report-Utkal-Alumina-International-Limited-Certificate-557-PS.pdf).

**Certificate 557 was issued 19 May 2026**, with an expiry date 18 May 2029 subject to continuing conformance. Its scope covers bauxite mining and related processing/transport; the refinery is expressly excluded. [Certificate and audit, PDF pp.1–4](https://aluminium-stewardship.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ASI-Audit-Report-Utkal-Alumina-International-Limited-Certificate-557-PS.pdf). The issuer’s announcement records **nine minor non-conformances** requiring corrective action. [ASI announcement](https://aluminium-stewardship.org/asi-certifies-baphlimali-bauxite-mines-of-utkal-international-limited-against-performance-standard-v3-1).

Retain the findings alongside the milestone. For example, the audit’s forced-labour criterion finding concerns inadequate statement coverage; the auditors report finding no forced labour. A living-wage assessment was missing, and documented overtime guidance was incomplete. Corrective-action closure is not yet verified. [Audit, PDF pp.17–18](https://aluminium-stewardship.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ASI-Audit-Report-Utkal-Alumina-International-Limited-Certificate-557-PS.pdf).

## Evidence that needs reconciliation

Hindalco’s undated page contains 8.5 MTPA in its header and 7.0 MTPA in its body. Its 18.5 km conveyor description also differs from the audit’s 18 km. Preserve the respective records rather than manufacturing a single precise current value. [Company profile](https://www.hindalco.com/about-us/operations/baphlimali-bauxite-mines).

A compliance-index link retrieved under Baphlimali led to a report whose cover names **Bimarla in Jharkhand**. It is excluded from Odisha observations. The annual return and the actual Baphlimali compliance report have now been read as text; retrieval limits are recorded below.

[Detailed observations, conflicts and next source routes](../references/data/mining-programme.json) · [Koraput](../statistics/districts/koraput.md) · [Rayagada](../statistics/districts/rayagada.md) · [Kalahandi](../statistics/districts/kalahandi.md).

[Mining overview](mining.md): Connects mine identities and reported output to separate work, permissions and community questions.

[Existing NALCO chain](bauxite-to-aluminium.md) supplies a separate processing case; do not combine company or mine totals without boundaries.

## Annual-return follow-up · 2 October 2026 UTC

**Baphlimali reports 7.657 million tonnes of ROM bauxite in FY2024–25.** Its annual return records 7,657,426 tonnes produced and 7,657,000 tonnes dispatched for captive consumption by Utkal Alumina. Opening stock plus production minus dispatch equals closing stock; the 426-tonne difference is preserved.

The mine reports **₹64.22 crore paid to DMF** for that financial year, converted from ₹642,173,879. This is a company payment disclosure, not proof of completed local projects or money received by households. title: From Koraput’s bauxite to Angul’s aluminium
description: From Koraput’s bauxite to Angul’s aluminium — source-linked evidence and limitations.

sources.title: NALCO 45th Annual Report 2025–26
NALCO Alumina Refinery: operations and transport
Pottangi Bauxite Mine: developer project record
NALCO 14th Sustainable Development Report 2024–25

body:
# From Koraput’s bauxite to Angul’s aluminium

**Odisha’s mineral story includes the factories that turn ore into metal.** NALCO’s reported chain joins Panchpatmali in Koraput to the Damanjodi refinery and Angul smelter, with surplus alumina moving to Visakhapatnam for export. [Operating description](https://nalcoindia.com/business/operation/alumina-refinery/).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 P[Panchpatmali bauxite mines · Koraput] --> D[Damanjodi alumina refinery · Koraput]
 D --> A[Angul aluminium smelter]
 D --> V[Visakhapatnam export facility · Andhra Pradesh]
 T[Pottangi · development project] -. Planned supply .-> D
```

The diagram shows reported supply relationships, not mineral conversion ratios, equal quantities or an independently checked logistics map.

## A measurable processing story

NALCO reports **471,701 tonnes of aluminium in 2025–26**, up **2.5%** on 460,137 tonnes in 2024–25. Alumina hydrate output rose from 2,075,500 to 2,300,000 tonnes, **10.8%**. These are company figures; successive material stages must not be added into one production total. Five annual observations from 2021–22 to 2025–26 span four elapsed years.

Markets moved differently. Aluminium domestic sales increased from 323,809 to 461,081 tonnes across those endpoints, while aluminium export sales fell from 133,085 to 13,238 tonnes. Total company export-sales value also fell from ₹5,516.97 crore in 2024–25 to ₹4,701.54 crore in 2025–26. Quantities and rupee values answer different questions. [Annual report, p.296](https://nalcoindia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/45th-Annual-Report-2025-26.pdf).

## What can we say about work?

The company reports 1,715 permanent employees, 3,149 permanent workers and 16,722 other-than-permanent workers at 31 March 2026. The first two categories reconcile to its 4,864 on-roll workforce. These totals include its wider operations and cannot be presented as Odisha-resident jobs created.

A more local connection is the **83% share of wage costs** reported for its semi-urban category in 2025–26, compared with 81% the year before. Its footnote identifies Nalco Nagar Anugola and Damanjodi. This is a wage-cost share, not an employee share or household-income change. [Annual report, pp.14,59,93](https://nalcoindia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/45th-Annual-Report-2025-26.pdf).

## Existing mines and expansion have different timelines

The report identifies Panchpatmali’s Central/North and South blocks separately, with company-reported lease validity to 16 November 2032 and 19 July 2029. Original current permits still need checking.

For **Pottangi**, NALCO reports an MDO appointment on 9 December 2025 and expects production in Q4 FY2026–27, or January–March 2027. Dilip Buildcon names itself as MDO and DBL Pottangi Bauxite Mines Private Limited as the agreement SPV. Its undated project page retains a mid-2026 target. Neither target proves production has started. [Annual report, pp.12–14](https://nalcoindia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/45th-Annual-Report-2025-26.pdf); [developer record](https://dilipbuildcon.com/project/pottangi-bauxite-mine/).

## Community outcomes remain a separate question

Pottangi’s reported conveyor and water-facility components list 415 and 48 affected families separately, with the rehabilitation package awaiting finalisation in that report. Do not add the counts without checking overlap. The report also describes honey and ginger-processing livelihood projects; beneficiary descriptions establish reported programme reach, not increased income.

Safety remains part of the story: the company reports zero worker fatalities in 2025–26 after two at its smelter in 2024–25, and one recordable worker incident each at the smelter and captive power plant in 2025–26. These are own-operation disclosures; the report’s external value-chain partner totals use a different boundary. [Annual report, pp.74,93,97,102](https://nalcoindia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/45th-Annual-Report-2025-26.pdf).

[Detailed evidence and open fields](../references/data/mining-programme.json) · [Mining overview](mining.md) · [Industrial production](../statistics/industrial-production.md) · [Koraput](../statistics/districts/koraput.md) · [Angul](../statistics/districts/angul.md) · [Honey and forest livelihoods](forest-products.md).

[Mining overview](mining.md) — Connects named mineral-processing relationships to separate public revenue, work and community questions.

## Local suppliers: a new reading of the saved report

NALCO reports **₹652.19 crore** of goods/services purchases from Odisha-based MSEs in 2025–26, within₹1,447.94 crore of all-location MSE procurement. This is about45.04% of that MSE total, not a share of all company purchasing. Purchases do not measure supplier profit or employment. [Saved annual report, printed p.56 / PDF p.76, section 19(a)](https://nalcoindia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/45th-Annual-Report-2025-26.pdf).

This extends the inspected scope of the same original report; it is not independent corroboration. [A readable supplier story](../stories/minerals-and-local-suppliers.md).

## Apprenticeship is another route into industrial skills

NALCO reports **925 apprentice trainees engaged during 2025–26**, up to 31 March 2026. This is a company-wide annual engagement figure, not the number appointed to permanent jobs, a placement result, or an Odisha-only count. The report does not allocate it between Damanjodi, Angul and other locations. [Same saved annual report, printed p.49 / PDF p.69, section9.2](https://nalcoindia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/45th-Annual-Report-2025-26.pdf).

This reading extends the existing source; it does not add independent corroboration. The report’s 9,284 employee-training figure also must not replace the 4,864 on-roll workforce: annual training participation and payroll headcount measure different things. Current unit-level payroll and contractor counts remain open.

## Work volume gives a plant view, not a headcount

NALCO’s FY2024–25 injury-statistics table reports these working-day volumes:

| Unit | Employee man-days | Contractor labour man-days |
|---|---:|---:|
| Alumina refinery, Damanjodi | 376,561 | 1,854,408 |
| Aluminium smelter, Angul | 489,800 | 1,308,875 |

Employee rows include executives and non-executives. Do not divide by an assumed working year to invent a count of people. [Report, printed p.79](../sources/mining-nalco-sd2025.md).

The existing **16,722** company-wide non-permanent-worker observation is reused. The annual report’s BRSR calls its table year-end details, while printed p.49 describes the same number as contractor workers engaged during March 2026. Neither passage supplies a plant split or unique-person method. Current unit payroll and local-resident shares remain missing.
