body:
# Indian Metals and Ferro Alloys (IMFA)

IMFA dates its establishment to **1961** and places its beginnings at Therubali, described using historical Koraput geography. Its history credits [Bansidhar Panda](../people/bansidhar-panda.md) alongside Ila Panda; it lists [Subhrakant Panda](../people/subhrakant-panda.md) as managing director. Establishment, plant commissioning, production and installed capacity remain distinct measures.

[Entrepreneur collection](../people/entrepreneurs-and-business-leaders.md).

## From captive ore to ferrochrome · FY2025–26

IMFA identifies captive chromite mines at Sukinda and Mahagiri supplying its smelting operations. Its annual report describes three manufacturing facilities in Odisha, including the acquired Kalinganagar unit alongside Therubali and Choudwar. The company states that its extracted chrome ore is used captively. This establishes a company supply chain, not a mine-to-furnace shipment allocation. [Report pp.4,14–15,40,51](https://www.imfa.in/api/pdf/IMFAAnnualReportFY2526.pdf/IMFA_Annual_Report_FY_2526_10bbee90f9.pdf).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 M[Sukinda and Mahagiri chromite mines] -->|Company captive supply; allocation unknown| F[IMFA Odisha ferrochrome facilities]
 F --> D[Domestic industrial customers]
 F --> E[International industrial customers]
```

| Measure | FY2024–25 | FY2025–26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ferrochrome produced, tonnes | 260,190 | 267,301 |
| Domestic sales, tonnes | 34,066 | 48,769 |
| International sales, tonnes | 225,801 | 221,355 |
| Sukinda ore, tonnes | 285,851 | 273,802 — held for reconciliation |
| Mahagiri ore, tonnes | 416,012 | 536,810 |

Production rose 2.73%; domestic sales rose 43.16%, while international sales fell 1.97%. The earlier Sukinda growth comparison is now held because a mine submission gives a different FY2025–26 value. Mahagiri’s annual-report series rose 29.04%; the later template distinguishes a lower ROM field without explaining the scope. Ore, alloy and sales are different stages and cannot be summed. The acquired plant changes the company perimeter, so output growth is not a like-for-like measure. [Table, p.40 / PDF22](https://www.imfa.in/api/pdf/IMFAAnnualReportFY2526.pdf/IMFA_Annual_Report_FY_2526_10bbee90f9.pdf).

### Acquisition and expansion have different dates

The MD reports completion of the acquired 100,000-tpa Kalinganagar unit transaction in February 2026 and production starting within two weeks. The separate greenfield unit and further furnace construction were still forward-looking in this report. The current-capacity and post-expansion figures belong to different stages; a July publication cannot establish October commissioning. No new investment total is added to the existing tracker. [pp.4,14–15](https://www.imfa.in/api/pdf/IMFAAnnualReportFY2526.pdf/IMFA_Annual_Report_FY_2526_10bbee90f9.pdf).

### People and suppliers: retain the boundary

At 31 March 2026 the standalone BRSR lists 860 permanent employees, 1,327 permanent workers and 5,206 other-than-permanent workers. These are national entity categories, not plant-level Odisha jobs or jobs created during the year. Direct sourcing from MSMEs/small producers represented 15.32% of total input value, up from 7.40%; suppliers within India represented 72.29%, up from 67.29%. The overlapping categories do not disclose an Odisha supplier share. [pp.57–59,97](https://www.imfa.in/api/pdf/IMFAAnnualReportFY2526.pdf/IMFA_Annual_Report_FY_2526_10bbee90f9.pdf).

Plant-specific output, payroll, contractor definitions, named local suppliers and mine despatch allocations remain open. [Trade story](../stories/odisha-ferrochrome-markets.md) · [Mining context](mining.md).

## What the plant and mine records add · 2 October 2026

The ministry’s **4 September 2026 clearance-transfer letter** identifies the acquired Kalinganagar facility as four implemented 16.5-MVA furnaces. Its annexure lists the proposed 33-MVA furnace and 67.5-MW captive power plant as **not implemented**. The transfer covers the implemented furnaces only. This concerns KNR2, not the separate KNR1 greenfield project; it does not establish October operating status. [Letter pp.2–4](https://www.imfa.in/api/pdf/IA_OR_IND1_04092026.pdf/IA_OR_IND_1_04092026_a1432f31b5.pdf).

Choudwar’s Unit-II statement provides furnace-specific input ratios rather than annual production: chrome ore per tonne of HCFC rose from 2.200 to 2.36634 at CCP-2 and from 2.263 to 2.4052 at CCP-3 between FY2024–25 and FY2025–26. Ore grade and operating conditions are not controlled here, so these ratios alone cannot explain efficiency or emissions. [Statement p.3](https://www.imfa.in/api/pdf/EnvironmentalStatementUnitII202526.pdf/Environmental_Statement_Unit_II_202526_4e5b4b9277.pdf).

Mine manpower tables are captured but held for clarification. The template defines local as from the State; it does not split direct and contract employment. Mahagiri’s local categories total 495 against a stated local total of 477. Sukinda’s category denominators total 799 against an overall 1,170. These are company submissions, not independently verified employment counts or awarded star ratings. [Sukinda p.31](https://www.imfa.in/api/pdf/SukindaMinesStarRating202526.pdf/Sukinda_Mines_Star_Rating202526_907f7142d9.pdf) · [Mahagiri p.28](https://www.imfa.in/api/pdf/MahagiriMinesStarRating202526.pdf/Mahagiri_Mines_Star_Rating202526_e5c85f9972.pdf).

Sukinda’s submitted ROM is 269,075 tonnes against 273,802 in the annual report. Both are retained, and the earlier growth calculation is quarantined. Mahagiri’s general field rounds to the annual-report value but differs from its underground ROM field. [Detailed captures and holds](../references/data/mining-programme.json).

Integration review: the annual report’s combined ore figure is also held for reconciliation because it includes the disputed Sukinda component. The reported value remains preserved; no revised total is inferred by mixing the annual report with the mine templates.

Odisha State Finances Audit Report 2024–25 — Chapter 1
Odisha Directorate of Mines and Geology: mineral revenue collected

body:
# From mineral revenues to working community services

A mine can generate revenue, a fund can pay a contractor, and a village can still be waiting for a working service. This research follows the steps between those events. It is a draft evidence account, with dated findings and government replies, not a present-day verdict on a district.

## Follow each rupee without skipping a stage

State mining receipts and DMF contributions are separate financial routes. Within the DMF route, follow sanctioned projects, released funds, expenditure, completed assets, operating services and community outcomes as distinct stages. OMC dividends, mine-level payment returns and DMF interest also need separate labels.

## Actual receipts and estimates

The original CAG State Finances Audit Report 2024–25, Table 1.7 (printed p. 15), gives these rounded figures in ₹ crore:

| Accounting head |2023–24 actual|2024–25 budget estimate|2024–25 revised estimate|2024–25 actual|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|Non-ferrous mining and metallurgical industries|45,046|48,600|46,600|41,052|
|Coal and lignite|1,351|832|2,560|1,015|

The sum of these two actual-receipt heads is 46,397 in 2023–24 and 42,067 in 2024–25. These are our sums of rounded source rows, not newly reported statewide totals. The Directorate’s 2023–24 mining collection series reports 46,396.27. The original comparison differs by 0.73 crore. A higher-precision Finance Accounts check below separates the rounding effect from a remaining 0.20 crore difference; the accounting-head bridge is still unverified. Dividends are excluded. Do not interpret the government’s non-ferrous accounting label as a list of non-ferrous commodities only.

The original [Finance Accounts 2023–24, Volume I](../sources/mining-fa2023-24-vol1.md), Statement 3 (printed p. 10 / PDF p. 28), reports **45,045.55** for non-ferrous mining and metallurgical industries and **1,350.52** for coal/lignite. Their sum is **46,396.07 crore**. Each head rounds to the SFAR figure above. Summing the whole-crore heads adds 0.93 crore relative to this two-decimal sum; the Directorate's 46,396.27 is 0.20 crore above it. That residual requires an accounting reconciliation or scope explanation. It is not evidence of missing funds. Preserve each source edition rather than replacing the rounded historical observations.

The legacy [F05](../evidence/f05.md) figure of 53,000 crore is a 2026–27 **budget estimate**. It remains intact and cannot establish actual collections or a realised increase over 2024–25.

## Six district funds, one explicit audit period

CAG Report 7 of 2026 covers 2015–16 to 2023–24, with later field checks and January 2026 replies. Table 5.1 reports collections **including interest** in this six-DMF sample; do not compare them directly with the existing all 30 DMF leaseholder-contribution total. Amounts below reproduce Table 5.1 in cumulative ₹ crore. **The Dhenkanal/Jajpur expenditure and sample release/expenditure figures conflict with Table 4.1; retain them as source-specific values pending clarification.**

|DMF|Collection incl. interest|Sanctioned|Released|Utilised|Completed / sanctioned projects|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|Dhenkanal|100.28|61.62|56.39|44.14|350 / 623|
|Jajpur|2,395.21|2,848.77|1,514.89|1,164.42|2,994 / 6,414|
|Keonjhar|12,227.12|9,733.37|5,701.34|4,410.10|1,023 / 3,269|
|Mayurbhanj|125.22|109.17|98.64|85.99|208 / 652|
|Nabarangpur|2.47|1.17|1.17|1.17|7 / 7|
|Sundargarh|7,717.87|8,193.42|5,788.32|4,386.71|5,108 / 6,470|

In Table 5.1, collections including interest for these six DMFs were 22,568.17 crore, sanctions 20,947.52 crore, releases 13,160.75 crore and expenditure 10,092.53 crore. Interest included in collections was 1,772.66 crore. These stages must not be summed.

Using Table 5.1 amounts, expenditure is 48.18% of sanctions and 76.69% of releases. These ratios inherit the unresolved cross-table conflict below. The original §5.1 prose says 79.69%, while Table 5.1 says 76.69%; the raw amounts support the latter. This discrepancy is preserved in the structured record. Table 5.2 also carries a rupee heading over project-count columns: use the column labels and accompanying narrative, not that heading, for units.

The sample reports 9,690 completed projects from 17,435 sanctioned (55.58%); 6,551 were ongoing and 1,194 not started/dropped. Completion says nothing by itself about staffing, utilities, sustained use or residents’ welfare. These six districts were audit-selected; neither their spending ratio nor these selected failures estimates all Odisha DMFs.

## The report contains conflicting totals

Original Table 4.1 (printed p. 24 / PDF p. 58), inspected visually, gives different amounts for the same district funds and audit period. We have not established a reason for the differences.

|Measure, ₹ crore|Table 4.1|Table 5.1|
|---|---:|---:|
|Six-DMF funds released|13,160.84|13,160.75|
|Six-DMF funds utilised|10,104.28|10,092.53|
|Dhenkanal released|56.48|56.39|
|Dhenkanal utilised|55.89|44.14|
|Jajpur utilised|1,164.43|1,164.42|

Dhenkanal accounts for the ₹11.75 crore difference between printed expenditure totals. Table 4.1's district expenditure rows sum to ₹10,104.29 crore, ₹0.01 crore above its printed total; rounding or a source error is possible but unconfirmed. Table 5.4 repeats Table 5.1 amounts within the same report and is not independent corroboration. Six affected observations retain their original values and now carry a publication hold; this includes the ratio derived from the disputed expenditure. These differences do not themselves establish missing money.

## A second district series needs its own definitions

The original [Lok Sabha answer of 11 December 2024](../sources/mining-dmf-ls2607-2024.md) supplies annual district collection, **allocation** and expenditure, plus a March 2024 balance table. It does not explain interest coverage or reconcile its figures to CAG. Allocation must not be renamed release, and a balance must not be reconstructed from unrelated totals.

|District expenditure, ₹ crore|FY2021–22|FY2022–23|FY2023–24|Three-year sum|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|Dhenkanal|10.28|4.81|6.10|21.19|
|Sundargarh (source: Sundergarh)|1,449.14|1,989.52|1,052.56|4,491.22|

Dhenkanal's three-year subtotal lacks the earlier years needed to assess either cumulative CAG figure. Sundargarh's subtotal already exceeds CAG's longer FY2015–16 to FY2023–24 figure of 4,386.71 by 104.51 crore. That is a warning against combining unreconciled definitions or vintages, not a finding of cash loss. The original answer's FY2024–25 column ends in October 2024 and must not be compared as a full year. Six selected district extracts and their source labels are retained in the structured programme, separately from the CAG sample.

A bounded official-domain search recovered no matching corrigendum for the CAG table conflict; this does not prove that none exists. The six existing conflict holds remain.

## How the audit selected its sample

Section 1.5 describes risk-stratified random district selection using collections, expenditure and tribal population, with Mayurbhanj additionally selected following media reports of fraud. Block selection combines the highest project counts with random selection; Gram Panchayats were randomly selected. This corrects the earlier structured checkpoint's blanket description as “purposively selected.” The four problem-case bundles below still cannot estimate the prevalence of failure across all projects.

## Four cases: completion, use and the reply

Each case below can include more than one facility. Combined costs must not be repeated as per-facility costs. All four are audit-selected problem cases; they are not a balanced evaluation of the programme.

### Dedicated NICU/PICU at District Headquarters Hospital, Keonjhar

Equipment procured January–February 2022 and installed March 2022 according to CDM&PHO records cited by Audit. Equipment approved and paid during December 2021–June 2022: ₹2.18 crore.

Joint physical verification on 29 April 2025 found units not operational and equipment unused; staff/doctors had not been deployed.

**Government reply:** January 2026: government said the assets strengthened crisis healthcare infrastructure. **Audit response:** CAG said the reply did not address non-use for the purchased purpose, continuing through January 2026.

**Next evidence:** Dated commissioning and duty-roster records, de-identified admission/service aggregates and independent patient/community accounts. Current operation in October 2026 is unverified. Locator: §6.6.3, printed p. 60 / PDF p. 98.

### Boys and girls hostels, Deogan village, Sukinda block

Completion certificate dated 16 July 2022 from R&B Division, Panikoili. Combined construction cost; do not assign the full amount to each hostel: ₹4.34 crore.

Not handed over to Education Department; joint verification 10 December 2024 found non-functional buildings, with water and electricity pending.

**Government reply:** January 2026: handover to BDO Sukinda would occur once critical utilities were in place. **Audit response:** CAG maintained the hostels had remained non-functional since completion.

**Next evidence:** Utility connections, handover/occupation certificates, staffing and anonymised occupancy by term. Current operation in October 2026 is unverified. Locator: §6.6.6, printed p. 62 / PDF p. 100.

### Digital medical records in DHH Sundargarh, SDH Bonai and Government Hospital Rourkela

Installed September 2019 at Bonai and November 2019 at the other two hospitals. Combined payment for system/equipment at three hospitals; sanction 1.52 crore and release 1.33 crore are separate stages: ₹1.32 crore.

Initially operated; audit records end dates 25 February 2020 at Sundargarh/Rourkela and 28 December 2020 at Bonai. Verification 4 March 2025 at Sundargarh found non-functioning system and 24 of 40 tablets stored unused.

**Government reply:** January 2026: acknowledged non-functioning since March 2020 and unsuccessful vendor engagement on compatibility with OeHMIS. **Audit response:** CAG attributed the failure to unresolved compatibility and ineffective use of warranty support; ₹1.32 crore termed infructuous. The general government reply date does not erase the hospital-specific dates.

**Next evidence:** System migration/asset redeployment records and dated evidence of records successfully used in care; do not infer all healthcare at these hospitals stopped. Current operation in October 2026 is unverified. Locator: §6.6.4, printed pp. 60–61 / PDF pp. 98–99.

### Wholesale market complex and Mission Shakti Café, Vyasanagar/Jajpur Road

Sanctioned in 2021–22/2022–23; audit describes completion and handovers in February/November 2023. Combined completed cost of two facilities; not separate per-facility amounts: ₹6.39 crore.

Joint verification November 2024 found intended beneficiary allotments absent and facilities not in use.

**Government reply:** January 2026: construction completed and facility handed to KNDA on 25 November 2023 for operation/management. **Audit response:** CAG retained its finding of defunct facilities; the handover reply does not establish operation.

**Next evidence:** Allotment and opening records, dated activity, tenant/SHG revenue and beneficiary testimony, with costs split by facility. Current operation in October 2026 is unverified. Locator: §6.6.9, printed p. 66 / PDF p. 104.

## Follow-up search: what remains unverified

A bounded public-record search on 2 October 2026 did not recover a later, facility-matched operating record for any of the four bundles. This means current status is unknown; it does not mean the facilities are still closed.

|Case|What the follow-up established|Evidence still needed|
|---|---|---|
|Keonjhar NICU/PICU|An official medical-college bed-listing lead appeared in search, but its page could not be retrieved and the units were not matched to the DMF equipment. Bed counts alone would not establish care delivered.|Commissioning, staff deployment and de-identified service counts tied to those units.|
|Deogan hostels|No matched later utility, handover or occupancy record recovered. Same-named villages and older hostel stories cannot safely be substituted.|Utility connections, handover and anonymised term occupancy for the Sukinda buildings.|
|Sundargarh digital records|An old annual-report lead and a general PMU tender do not establish restoration or migration of the three-hospital system.|Dated migration/redeployment record and evidence of routine use in care.|
|Vyasanagar market/café|The original [27 March 2023 Parliament reply](../sources/mining-npcc-rs2970-2023.md) lists **scheduled** completion of the market on 27 April 2023 and café on 25 November 2023. These are not opening dates.|Facility identifiers, allotments, trading activity and beneficiary evidence after the audit.|

The parliamentary list supports a candidate match by name, locality and client; a shared project identifier remains unverified. The café's scheduled date happens to match the later government handover date, but those are different claims. The market's schedule must not overwrite the audit's earlier handover account. Direct district-portal retrievals also failed; search snippets and recent crawl dates were not promoted to current facts. The structured follow-up preserves these retrieval limits.

### Next records, rather than another identical search

Further attempts to retrieve the Jajpur 2023–24 accounts, its 2022–23 annual report and the Keonjhar infrastructure page failed. A general hospital-service description and an old OeHMIS navigation link do not verify the audited equipment or digital system. None of the four case bundles has newly established current operation or beneficiary outcomes.

The structured programme now has six **unsent** record questions: the receipt-head reconciliation; the conflicting DMF tables and Parliament accounting basis; and one request for each facility bundle. They identify the relevant record holders and the exact documents needed—asset/project identifiers, actual commissioning/handover dates, staff and utilities, and de-identified service or occupancy counts. No outreach or application has been sent. Revisit a case when one of these records, a dated operating update or a restored source endpoint becomes available; repeated search failure is not new evidence of closure.

## An operating asset can still raise a different question

In §6.5.1 (printed p. 46 / PDF p. 84), CAG records Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium as functional during January 2025 verification, while separately questioning DMF funding eligibility and benefit to mining-affected residents. Government's January 2026 reply cited larger public interest and Sports and Youth Services permission; CAG said that department could not authorize this use of DMF funds.

This is useful context, not a control group: **operation, funding eligibility, beneficiary access and community impact are separate questions.** A service can operate while its funding is disputed; a completed building can have eligible funding while still awaiting staff or utilities.

## What would establish benefit?

A completed hostel needs functioning water/electricity, staff and evidence of occupation. An ICU needs staff and evidence of care delivered. A market needs occupied stalls and trading activity. A digital system needs evidence of use in care. These are proposed verification fields, not findings that the evidence already supplies.

For each case retain: stable identity and geography; funding source; sanction/release/expenditure dates; completion and handover records; operation dates; maintenance/staffing; de-identified service counts; intended and actual beneficiary scope; and attributed community accounts. An outcome claim needs an appropriate baseline/comparison and cannot be inferred solely from use. Never collect identifiable patient or student records for this research.

Chapter VII records weak public disclosure and absent asset registers in the audited sample. January 2026 replies describe training and progressive asset-register compilation; these are reported responses, not independently verified remediation. The cumulative reading now covers §1.5 and Chapters III–VIII (collection, planning, fund management, implementation, monitoring, conclusions and recommendations). Appendices have not been exhaustively reviewed; this is source reading, not an independent re-audit.

## Sources and connected knowledge

- [CAG DMF audit](../sources/mining-cag-dmf2026.md): §1.5 and Chapters III–VIII; Tables 4.1 and 5.1–5.2 retain their discrepancies.
- [Parliament construction schedule](../sources/mining-npcc-rs2970-2023.md): Annexure IV, rows 193/213; planned dates only.
- [CAG State Finances](../sources/macro-cag-fy2025.md): original PDF Table 1.7.
- [Directorate revenue table](../sources/mining-directorate-revenue.md): collection-series scope.
- [Finance Accounts 2023–24](../sources/mining-fa2023-24-vol1.md): higher-precision receipt heads.
- [Lok Sabha DMF reply](../sources/mining-dmf-ls2607-2024.md): annual district figures and dated balances.
- [Mining research](mining.md) · [Minerals and mining statistics](../statistics/minerals-and-mining.md) · [Public finance audit](../statistics/public-finance-audit.md).
- [Structured cases, amounts and follow-ups](../references/data/mining-programme.json) · [Observation atlas](../references/data/statistics-atlas.json).

Research checkpoint only. No independent human review, local testimony, full accounting reconciliation or website story publication is claimed.

body:
# Forest products: household use, markets and livelihoods

**The central question is how forest knowledge and produce support everyday life and paid work.** Keep foods connected to the wider non-timber forest-products economy without calling every product food.

| Research group | What to document |
| --- | --- |
| Fruits, kernels, flowers and honey | Identity, use, season, preservation, supply origin and food-processing evidence |
| Leaves and leaf products | Sal-leaf collection, plate-making, labour, local buyers and processing; examine other leaf identities separately |
| Oilseeds, gums, resins and lac | Product and grade, actual end uses, processing yields and prices |
| Bamboo, cane, fibres and brooms | Material, maker, end product and commercial channel |
| Kendu leaves | A non-food commodity used as bidi wrappers; separate leaf trade from any fruit entry |

These groups define research coverage. Inclusion does not establish present procurement, sustainable supply, exports or proven medicinal effects. The TDCCOL product page is currently a partially captured discovery lead, not a verified current buying list.

## Follow value through each transaction

A proposed reporting chain is **collection → household use or local sale → aggregation → processing → retail or export**. Verify actual buyers before claiming a product follows that chain. Record procurement separately from sales, and collector receipts separately from turnover and net earnings. Prices require date, place, grade, moisture and unit. Published support prices do not prove procurement at that price.

[The first market checkpoint](../statistics/forest-products.md) saves a kendu series and one honey-processing capacity observation. It is not an estimate of Odisha's entire forest-food market. [Forest foods](../food/forest-foods.md) retains household and culinary context; [history](../history/forest-livelihoods.md) provides dated evidence rather than invented ancient origins.

## Next evidence to obtain

Product-level TDCCOL/Van Dhan procurement and realised sales; collector payments and costs; women-led groups and named community enterprises; seasonal haat prices; storage loss and processing yields; state-origin export quantities. Export promotion, an online listing or an overseas buyer mention alone does not establish measured shipments. For land, collection rights and ecological effects, use current primary decisions and location-specific studies.

[Structured research register](../references/data/forest-products.json).

[Related reading](../food/forest-foods.md) — Connects commodity research to household uses and ingredient identities; forest origin requires its own evidence.

[Related reading](../history/forest-livelihoods.md) — Adds dated institutional and community-study context without dating the origin of traditions.

[Related reading](../statistics/forests.md) — Provides land-cover context; forest area does not estimate product yields or household income.

[Related reading](../economy/mining.md) — Connects research on land and livelihoods; no causal effect of a named mine is asserted.

## Named products · 1 October 2026

Start with [kendu patra](kendu-patra.md), [Mohu/honey](../food/mohu-honey.md) and [mahua/mohula](../food/mahua-mohula.md). The structured register now separates flowers, seeds and leaf products rather than treating one tree as one market commodity.

Vasundhara's own livelihood account names sal leaves, siali leaves, sal seeds, char seeds, mahua and honey among products sold through the collectives it supports. It describes women-member producer groups and business unions. The page is undated; we use it to identify products and research routes, not a current count of enterprises or an independent income-impact claim. [Organisation account](https://vasundharaodisha.org/Welcome/page/Livelihood).

Tamarind, harida, bahada, karanja seed, kusum seed, lac and hill brooms are additional leads from the previously saved, indexed TDCCOL list. Each needs direct product-level verification; inclusion is not evidence of current buying, a market size or exports. Bamboo, cane, gums and other materials remain in the broader research groups.


[Related reading](../economy/kendu-patra.md) — Connects the leaf commodity to the saved market series; leaf sales do not describe edible fruit.

[Related reading](../food/mohu-honey.md) — Connects honey processing and collector questions while preserving forest-collected versus managed-hive origin.

[Related reading](../food/mahua-mohula.md) — Connects separate flower and seed uses with botanical identity and attributed cultural research.

[Siali: leaves and fibre](siali-products.md) — separates a climber’s identity and community-attributed fibre uses from sal and mahua. Its named product records inherit no statewide market totals.

[Mahua preparation and processing](../food/mahua-mohula.md) now connects local historical food practice, qualitative market constraints and a university-developed processing unit. A plant design or batch rating does not establish enterprise sales or collector earnings.

## Leaves are a material economy too

[Sal](sal-products.md) and [siali](siali-products.md) now distinguish tree and climber, leaf and seed/fibre, maker processes and local seasonal accounts. Collection, stitching, pressing and selling need separate measures. Current market totals and exports remain open; the historical craft evidence does not fill those gaps.

## Fruit and kernel value chains

[Tentuli](../food/tentuli-tamarind.md) distinguishes pulp, seeds and sale grades. [Chara/chironji](../food/chara-chironji.md) distinguishes fruit, hard nut and kernel. Historical community-market accounts are saved; processing yields, current prices, realised procurement and exports remain open.

## From sale proceeds to worker support

[The payment evidence](../statistics/forest-products.md) adds dated kendu welfare statements and a separately labelled compassionate-grant table. These belong to the non-food forest economy. TDCCOL product procurement and actual collector payments still need accessible original statements; tenders, targets and indexed tables are not realised purchases.

## Mine-to-processing checkpoint · 1 October 2026

[Mining and livelihood links](bauxite-to-aluminium.md) preserves NALCO’s reported honey/ginger project descriptions. Beneficiary counts do not measure collector earnings or market sales.

## Named enterprise leads and reported sales · 2 October 2026 UTC

[The Van Dhan story](../stories/van-dhan-enterprises.md) now has a dated parliamentary sales comparison. To connect it to people and products, the [ministry's 2021 account](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1715921) supplies these leads:

| Named cluster or group | Place stated | Activity described in the historical plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Luguburu, Maa Dharithri and Bhimakund | Mayurbhanj | Collectively: sal-leaf plates/cups, kusum oil and processed wild honey |
| Anchalika Khandadhar | Keonjhar | Mango preparations, turmeric powder and mustard oil |
| Ban Durga | Not specified in the cited paragraph | Tamarind processing, sal shampoo and packed char seeds |

Do not distribute the collective product list to each Mayurbhanj cluster. Current operation, women ownership, product sales and collector payments are unknown. These five named leads are a research list, not a census. Programme aggregate sales cannot be assigned to them.

The next evidence sought is a dated procurement ledger, completed-sale statement and actual collector-payment record for the same product, grade and period. Recent departmental PDFs and TDCC pages failed retrieval; index snippets and auction notices remain leads. Retry on 8 October, retaining the accessible historical evidence.

description: Odisha’s GDP story: scale, momentum and meaning — research and reuse notes.
body:
# Odisha’s GDP story: scale, momentum and meaning

The most useful economic narrative connects the size of the economy to visible sectors and places. Lead with a clear, dated number and then show what it represents.

## Opening evidence

The preserved survey records give **₹9.88 lakh crore nominal GSDP** and **7.9% real GSDP growth** for FY2025–26, both advance estimates. These are two different measures: [economic size](../evidence/e02.md) and [inflation-adjusted annual growth](../evidence/e01.md). They can sit side by side if labelled properly.

## Suggested message

“Odisha’s next chapter is taking shape.” Follow it with the economic-size number, its estimate label, and a sequence covering ports, production, food, services and people. Treat the phrase as campaign language rather than a statistical finding.

## A richer proof sequence

Use [construction’s five-year real growth](construction.md), [fisheries production](comparison-01-fisheries.md) and [Paradip cargo](comparison-05-port-logistics.md) as distinct stories. Their measures must stay separate: economic value added, physical output and port throughput. They cannot be added into a single “growth” total.

The [industry growth collection](index.md) retains complete six-year sector series so the campaign can use both the positive endpoint comparison and a truthful chart. A changing trajectory is more informative than an invented uninterrupted boom.

## Publication controls

Use a common vintage and price basis for any India comparison. The state survey’s national comparator and later national estimates are not automatically comparable: see [survey comparator](../evidence/e04.md) and [later national estimate](../evidence/e05.md). Do not call nominal expansion real growth. Do not turn per-capita income into a claim about every household. Announced investments and jobs remain announcements until completion is established.

The nominal ten-year tripling angle from earlier work needs its historical starting value added as an independently locatable record before it becomes a website headline.

## Fresh series expansion

The [economic-size and income atlas](../statistics/economic-size-and-income.md) records the current-price 2018–19 to 2025–26 series with revision/advance-estimate labels and explicit lakh-to-crore conversion. It supports the saved five-year nominal comparison, not a real-growth or ten-year claim.

body:
# Homestays: government support and policy history

A hosted home can connect accommodation spending with local food, crafts and work. Odisha’s support programme creates an opportunity to develop those connections; household income and benefits to makers still need measurement.

## What the 2025 scheme provides

The Gazette defines family-hosted accommodation around the owner’s residence. Its financial route supports selected new units in notified rural areas; other units have a separate non-financial route. The notified framework offers up to **50% of eligible fixed capital investment excluding land**, limited to **₹2.5 lakh per lettable room**, four rooms and **₹10 lakh per unit**. Payment is conditional and staged: 50%, 15%, 15% and 20%, with later booking-night thresholds of 15, 30 and 45 per room. These are historical source provisions, not amounts already paid.[^homestay-scheme2025]

Support also includes promotion, training, mentoring and digital visitor management. The budget window ends FY2028–29, while scheme validity runs to 31 March 2030 unless changed. The programme supersedes the 2021 scheme.[^homestay-scheme2025]

## Policy sequence and currentness

| Date | What is established | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| 24/29 November 2025 | Notification/Gazette publication of the 2025 scheme | Later amendments must be read with it |
| 5 March 2026 | Go Homestay launch reported on 6 March | Event report; not adoption figures[^homestay-launch-mar2026] |
| April–May 2026 | Official guidelines index lists an amendment and Cycle-1 targets | Linked PDFs could not be retrieved in this run[^homestay-guideline-index] |
| 19 May 2026 | First-cycle targets described in reporting | Target, not achievement[^homestay-cycle1-may2026] |
| 5 August 2026 | New Homestay Scheme entry in official Gazette archive | Metadata checked; underlying text unavailable[^homestay-gazette-aug2026] |

A regulatory publisher reports a July amendment concerning residency within the Block and a Rayagada GP correction. This remains a **discovery lead**, because the Gazette text was not obtained. Do not use the original GP-residence clause or this secondary summary as definitive current application guidance.[^homestay-amendment-lead]

## Digital support: what exists versus what is measured

The public Go Homestay address is saved, but its page returned no readable dashboard data in this run.[^homestay-go-portal] OCAC’s app listing describes application tracking, inspections, incentives, visitor records and reporting. These advertised functions are useful source leads; they were not tested in an authenticated account. App downloads are not counts of hosts, bookings or approved units.[^homestay-go-app]

## National programmes are a separate layer

The national parliamentary reply describes a 1,000-homestay tribal-development intervention and national credit support. Those are India-level programmes, not an Odisha allocation. National classification, state registration, marketing-platform listings and financial-benefit selection need separate labels.[^homestay-nidhi2025]

## Connections to document next

Record host consent, a stable property ID, operating status, room count and date before recommending a stay. A regional food tradition does not prove that a host serves it; a nearby craft centre does not prove a commercial relationship. Research actual meals, guide services, maker visits and purchases through attributed local accounts. No booking recommendation follows from scheme eligibility alone.

- [Homestay data](../statistics/homestays.md) — Read targets, registries and market listings with their distinct meanings.
- [Food collection](../food/index.md) and [handlooms](../handlooms/index.md) — Potential local experiences to investigate with hosts and makers.
- [Classification](../methods/content-classification.md) — Keep topic association separate from demonstrated commercial links.

[Economy](../subjects/economy.md) · [Governance](../subjects/governance.md) · [People](../subjects/people.md)

[^homestay-guideline-index]: [Odisha Tourism guidelines: amendments and Cycle 1 targets](https://dot.odisha.gov.in/en/guidelines).

[^homestay-gazette-aug2026]: [Tourism Gazette archive: Homestay Scheme entry, 5 August 2026](https://egazette.odisha.gov.in/extraordinary_archival_dept/70/1).

[^homestay-nidhi2025]: [One India, One Registration Initiative under NIDHI Portal](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2155162&lang=2&reg=48).

[^homestay-go-portal]: [Go Homestay official portal](https://gohomestay.odisha.gov.in/).

[^homestay-go-app]: [Go Homestay Portal — OCAC app listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?hl=en_IN&id=com.aashdit.gohomestay).

[^homestay-launch-mar2026]: [State launches Go Homestay portal](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bhubaneswar/state-launches-go-homestay-portal/articleshow/129108175.cms).

[^homestay-market-jan2025]: [Homestay count grows manifold in Odisha but local experience missing](https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/odisha/2025/Jan/04/homestay-count-grows-manifold-in-odisha-but-local-experience-missing).

[^homestay-amendment-lead]: [Reported July 2026 homestay eligibility amendment](https://teamleaseregtech.com/updates/article/59065/odisha-tourism-amendment-to-homestay-establishment-scheme-2025/).

## Policy reconciliation checkpoint · 1 October 2026

The [official portal](https://gohomestay.odisha.gov.in/) now supplies a readable area table and notice list. Seven distinct titles include “11436”, “Ammendment 17.08.26”, an application-deadline extension and a Rayagada correction. The title date is not independently verified as the notification or effective date. The carousel repeats notices; repeats are not new releases.

The April amendment and Cycle-1 official PDF downloads timed out. Portal document buttons did not produce readable originals in this session. RES-008 therefore remains blocked for text retrieval, with retry on 8 October. Its policy and geographic conflicts are not resolved by the availability of a portal table. The portal still displays GP-residence wording; the July secondary lead reports broader Block residency. Do not give definitive applicant guidance from either alone.

### From a place list to livelihood evidence

RES-009 begins with the 2025 scheme’s own reporting route: printed pp. 27–28 describe programme monitoring; the blank annual declaration at p. 49 asks for operation/closure status, rooms and beds, guest-nights, revenue, occupancy, family/local staff and subsidy received. This establishes potential administrative evidence, not that returns were filed or outcomes achieved. Parsed text was read; no new visual PDF verification is claimed.

Next retrieve aggregate completed returns or departmental progress reports with their reporting period, responding-property denominator, cancellations/closures and revision dates. Guest-nights cannot silently become room-nights; gross revenue cannot become net household income. The [monitoring record](../references/data/homestay-research.json) keeps every unavailable outcome null. The nine missing outcome measures remain open.

## Operating evidence checkpoint · 1 October 2026

World Tourism Day coverage supplies a new lead but conflicting quantities: [Odisha Connect](https://odishaconnect.com/odisha-celebrates-world-tourism-day-2026-with-digital-innovation-and-community-led-tourism/) reports 176 provisional-registration beneficiaries in an indexed passage; [OdishaBytes](https://odishabytes.com/odisha-signs-pacts-to-promote-homestay-heritage-adventure-tourism/amp/) says 17 in its directly read closing paragraph. The event is 27 September 2026. Both counts are held pending an original departmental release/register, outside the headline statistics. The reports may draw on the same event announcement.

OdishaBytes also reports an SBI financing MoU. Its signed terms, loan approvals and disbursements were not obtained. An agreement is not realised lending. No active-property census, completed compliance returns, occupancy or host-income data was recovered in this bounded search. Unknown remains unknown.

[Community ecotourism evidence](../statistics/ecotourism.md) now supplies a separately scoped programme income/visitor series; it does not fill homestay operating gaps.

# Kendu patra: a leaf, skilled work and trade

**Kendu patra means the leaf product in this collection.** OFDC identifies kendu as *Diospyros melanoxylon* and describes the leaves' use as bidi wrappers. Leaf grading, bundling and trade are distinct from any fruit or food entry. [OFDC](https://www.odishafdc.com/kenduleaf.php).

## The story to document

Follow collection, sorting, drying, grading, storage and sale through named places and workers. OFDC's institutional account describes processed and phal leaf forms and the organisation of marketing following nationalisation in 1973. Further research needs worker-attributed accounts, seasonal calendars and dated collection and payment records. Do not infer every household's practice from an agency description.

[The existing market series](../statistics/forest-products.md) owns the sales figures. Reuse it instead of creating a competing kendu total. Gross sale value, working funds, collector payments and net household income have different meanings; the 2019–20 source discrepancy remains held.

## Evidence to add

District and division collection volumes; quality grades; dates and units of payments; plucker and binder earnings; seasonal employment; cooperatives and women workers; storage losses; actual export shipments. Identify whether a measure counts people, worker-days, bundles or weight. Keep tobacco-wrapper commerce clearly classified as non-food.

[Forest products](forest-products.md) · [Forest livelihood history](../history/forest-livelihoods.md).

## Payment evidence added

[Worker welfare and compassionate grants](../statistics/forest-products.md) now separate distribution year, crop year and financial year. Historical payment statements, a newer portal table and the original OFDC comparative sales quantity are retained with their scope conflicts. Procurement prices and bonus announcements do not prove what each worker received.

body:
# Mining, land and people

**A mine is also a neighbour.** Its story follows water beyond a lease boundary, workers along a haul road, communities making decisions about land, and the life that returns after excavation. Production figures alone cannot answer those questions.

These are four bounded research studies, not current safety assurances or completed public stories. Each separates the place, evidence period, source role, reported finding and next record. [Structured cases](../references/data/mining-programme.json) retain the follow-up fields under `environment_rights_safety_checkpoint`.

## Sukurangi: read the sample before the conclusion

OMC's expansion summary describes a March–May 2022 baseline: air monitoring at ten locations and water sampling from three surface and six groundwater sources. It reports ambient-air compliance, but also surface-water chromium and groundwater aluminium exceedances. Its broad groundwater-compliance conclusion therefore needs reconciliation. This is a proponent's assessment hosted by OSPCB, not an independent regulator finding. The underlying laboratory tables remain unchecked. [EIA summary, pp.8–10](../sources/mining-sukurangi-eia-summary.md).

Do not turn a seasonal study into a present-day drinking-water guarantee. Keep pollutant species, source type, sampling point, detection limit and applicable standard together. The existing [city air-quality series](../statistics/air-quality.md) has different geography and coverage and cannot establish this mine's contribution to pollution.

A [reproduced July 2026 NGT order](https://www.casemine.com/judgement/in/6a844d3b979ea4201d807c32) is a follow-up lead for wider Sukinda monitoring and remedial action. Its original judgment and study annexures still need retrieval. No numerical table from the mirror enters the atlas. Keep residents' allegations, medical evidence, regulator measurements and tribunal findings distinct.

## Niyamgiri: rights are part of the decision

The Supreme Court's 18 April 2013 judgment required Gram Sabhas to examine affected forest and cultural/religious claims, including worship rights. MoEF was then to decide Stage-II clearance in light of their decisions. A District-Judge-rank observer was to certify independent proceedings. This is a specific rights process, not an automatic approval or a blanket statewide veto. [Official SCR edition, paragraphs 58–63](../sources/mining-niyamgiri-scr2013.md).

The OMC proposal in this case is distinct from Baphlimali/Utkal Alumina. Signed village resolutions, observer certifications and the subsequent ministry decision are still needed to complete this historical decision chain. A judgment describing a process does not prove how every later step occurred.

## Bharatpur: follow the recommendation into action

DGMS's May 2024 alert concerns a 14 March 2023 accident at MCL's Bharatpur coal mine in Angul. A contractual tipper operator died after a collision with an abandoned building at a road curve; the alert reports excessive speed. Its prevention recommendations cover transport checks, contractor training, road obstructions and signage. [DGMS, pp.1–2](../sources/mining-dgms-bharatpur-2024.md).

The next question is whether the site implemented those measures. The alert alone cannot answer it. Nor can one incident supply an annual total or accident rate without a complete register and exposure denominator. The study records the worker's role without reproducing unnecessary personal details or accident photographs.

## Baphlimali: planted land is not yet a recovery trend

Reuse the [existing mine and annual-return studies](bauxite-mine-identities.md). They preserve different dated measures of reclaimed, backfilled, afforested and rehabilitated land; these cannot form one trend.

The January 2026 ASI audit rates rehabilitation criterion 8.7 as conforming, while air criterion 6.1 records a monitoring gap for mine vehicles. Neither the mine-scoped certificate nor its rehabilitation finding establishes final closure or ecological recovery. The refinery is outside its scope. [Audit, pp.10–11,13–14](../sources/mining-asi-baphlimali2026.md).

The planting-count wording is ambiguous, and the reported survival percentage lacks a cohort/sampling basis in the public summary. Do not relabel the count as independently verified species or seedlings. Obtain the underlying rehabilitation audit, map comparable areas, and examine survival, soil, water, biodiversity and post-mining use before describing recovery. Corrective-action closure remains unverified.

## A reusable case-study model

|Question|Record to retain|What it cannot establish alone|
|---|---|---|
|Which site and people?|Mine identity, operator, affected settlements, dated boundary|All nearby mines have the same impact|
|What was required?|Permit condition or exact decision paragraph and date|Compliance or present permission|
|What was measured?|Station/sample, medium, method, units, season, denominator|Exposure or health causation|
|Whose finding is it?|Company disclosure, regulator measurement, court finding, community testimony|Independent corroboration merely because a government site hosts a file|
|What changed?|Matched before/after observations and corrective-action evidence|Recovery from a plan, expense or planting count|
|What remains unresolved?|Named missing record, scope conflict and next check|Failure or success from the absence of a record|

A future public narrative should connect these records to consented local voices. It should not invent testimony, collapse communities into a single opinion or use a celebratory industrial image as evidence of an outcome. No outreach or interviews were performed for this batch.

[Mining programme](mining.md) · [DMF community outcomes](dmf-community-outcomes.md) · [Research source method](../methods/source-reliability.md).

## Evidence follow-up · 3 October 2026

### Sukinda: an annexed study, with a denominator conflict

A scan of CGWB's June 2025 study was recovered as Annex 7 of a 2026 applicant filing, Kailash Chandra Nayak v State of Odisha. This is a different proceeding from the Mantu Das judgment lead. The scan supplies the study's own pages; NGT hosting does not turn the petition's allegations into tribunal findings or certify the annex. [Capture and provenance](../sources/mining-cgwb-sukinda2025-annex.md).

Report p. 3 describes 183 pre-monsoon and 50 post-monsoon samples collected in 2024. Follow-up sites were selected mainly because earlier chromium(VI) readings were elevated, with some nearby additions. These are not comparable representative seasonal samples. The study includes groundwater, rivers, ponds, mine pits and treatment plants.

Table 4 (report p. 8 / PDF p. 65) is transcribed below. Above-threshold counts refer to Cr(VI)>0.05 mg/L as used in the report, not a finding of discharge-permit violation.

|Source|Pre samples|Pre above threshold|Post samples|Post above threshold|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|DW|28|0|1|0|
|BW|11|0|5|0|
|HP|99|20|31|18|
|Damsala Nala|23|9|4|2|
|Mine pit|2|2|2|2|
|Pond|5|0|0|0|
|ETP-inlet|6|6|6|6|
|ETP-outlet|6|0|6|0|
|WTP|1|0|0|0|
|Spring|2|0|1|0|
|Printed total|183|37|50|28|
|Sum of component rows|183|37|56|28|

**Numerical interpretation is held.** Post-monsoon rows sum to 56, not the printed 50. Table 1 also uses different hand-pump, river and ETP-outlet totals from the seasonal sums in Table 4. Preserve the printed data; request clarification rather than silently adjust a cell. Table 3's 39 location rows include repeat seasonal readings and different water types, not 39 affected people. No prevalence percentage or contamination trend is calculated, and no figures enter the statistics atlas.

The report's suggested geogenic explanation is its interpretation, not proof that all contamination has one cause or that every operator is exonerated. Its recommendations include alternative safe-water supply, closure of contaminated wells, periodic testing and treatment-system maintenance. Completion remains unverified. Below detection is not zero, and a dated sampled result is not a current drinking-water assurance. The original Sukurangi EIA laboratory-table gap remains separate.

### Baphlimali: a regulator inspection adds a dated work record

IBM inspected the mine on 10 September 2024. The document identifies Utkal Alumina International Ltd and mine code 07ORI27001, despite a filename containing NALCO. Read the document identity, not the filename. [IBM report, pp.1,5–6](../sources/mining-ibm-baphlimali2024.md).

|Measure|Proposed FY2023–24|Actual FY2023–24|
|---|---:|---:|
|Backfilled area, row 5b|17.28 ha|17.45 ha|
|Afforestation, row 6b|29.51 ha|30.20 ha|

Row 5d separately reports total reclaimed area 141.204 ha and rehabilitated area 88.75 ha. These may overlap and must not be added. This is regulator-reported work, not proof of native ecological recovery or final closure. The inspection is not established as the exact later government audit mentioned by ASI. Later company and certification area figures retain their original dates and definitions.

### Niyamgiri: a government committee records the village decisions

The 2014 Xaxa Committee report says all twelve Palli Sabhas, held 18 July–19 August 2013, rejected the proposed mining. Footnote 356 cites state-provided English translations of resolutions held by the committee. This is a government committee's account; we have not inspected the signed village originals. Retrieval is limited to an indexed excerpt of the official PDF. [Report p. 353 and capture limits](../sources/mining-xaxa-niyamgiri2014.md).

The signed resolutions, observer certifications and original final ministry decision remain the next records; no current permission conclusion is drawn.

### Bharatpur: the same incident appears in the ministry agenda

The 49th coal-safety committee agenda lists Bharatpur OC/MCL, 14 March 2023, a tipper incident and one fatality. This matches the existing DGMS case; it adds no new death to any total. [Agenda IV(a), p.59, row 5](../sources/mining-coal-safety49-agenda.md).

The agenda's general company-level action summaries do not verify that the specific roadside hazard was removed. The mine-specific action-taken or inspection-closure record remains missing; absence from this search does not establish that no action occurred.

# Odisha mining: minerals, industry and people

**Mining needs a connected encyclopedia section.** The editorial question is: how does mineral wealth become lasting value for Odisha? Answer it through production, processing, public money, working lives and the places affected.

| Angle | Question to answer |
| --- | --- |
| Minerals and geology | Which minerals occur where, with what dated reserve/resource classifications? |
| Production and national position | How have coal, iron ore, bauxite, chromite, manganese and other minerals changed over five and ten years? |
| Processing and manufacturing | How much ore is beneficiated, refined or made into metal and finished products inside Odisha? |
| Revenue and public finances | What do royalties, auction premiums and other receipts contribute, and how volatile are they? |
| Mining-area development | What do DMF projects deliver in health, water, schooling and livelihoods? |
| Jobs, skills and small businesses | Who works in mines, plants, transport and supplier firms, under what employment conditions? |
| Trade and transport | Where do minerals and metals go through railways, ports and domestic supply chains? |
| Land, rights and communities | How do acquisition, resettlement, consent, forest rights and local livelihoods affect mining communities? |
| Air, water, forests and health | What do site monitoring records show about dust, water, waste, forests and exposure? |
| Safety and mine closure | What happens during operation, closure and restoration, and what liabilities remain? |
| Ownership and accountability | Who owns and operates each lease; what is its current stage and compliance history? |
| Industrial history and future materials | How did mining towns develop, and what could recycling, research and critical minerals change? |

## Start with the evidence already saved

Reuse the existing [real mining value-added series](mining-and-quarrying.md), [bauxite](comparison-06-mining.md), [coal](comparison-07-mining.md) and [iron-ore comparisons](comparison-08-mining.md). These are imported records with stated vintages, not freshly verified by their inclusion here. Reconcile future captures alongside them without rewriting the frozen ledger.

[The first statistical checkpoint](../statistics/minerals-and-mining.md) adds dated national production shares and mining-area fund evidence. The [rare-earth journey](../journeys/rare-earths.md) already separates OSCOM capacity from proposed expansion.

## District and value-chain research

Build profiles around mineral, mine, operator, district, processing plant and transport route. Candidate geographies for verification include Keonjhar/Kendujhar and Sundargarh, the Sukinda/Jajpur area, Angul–Talcher and the Ib Valley, and bauxite-linked areas of Koraput, Rayagada and Kalahandi. This is a research selection, not a verified deposit or active-mine map. Preserve historical and administrative aliases.

Begin with iron ore → beneficiation/pellets → iron and steel; bauxite → alumina → aluminium → fabrication; chromite → ferrochrome → stainless steel; coal → power and industrial uses. These are research pathways, not verified supplier relationships between particular companies. Link plant-level evidence before drawing arrows on a public map.

## What readers should see

Short mineral explainers, district portraits, credited worker and scientist profiles, five- or ten-year charts, and plant-stage timelines. A public card should carry one takeaway, its year/unit and a source reveal. A mine profile should state whether it is proposed, auctioned, leased, operating, suspended or closed, with an observation date.

Keep useful positive achievements alongside setbacks and unresolved questions. More ore extracted does not on its own establish higher local incomes or better services. Green-mining claims need measured outcomes.

[Structured coverage and evidence pointers](../references/data/mining-programme.json).

[Related reading](../statistics/minerals-and-mining.md) — Connects the broad mining questions to dated national contribution and fund-use measures, without claiming causal local benefits.

[Related reading](../journeys/rare-earths.md) — Reuses the rare-earth processing record while keeping capacity, actual output and proposals separate.

[Related reading](../statistics/industrial-production.md) — Links ore extraction to plant-level output research; mineral and processed-metal quantities must not be summed.

## Coal series checkpoint · 1 October 2026

[Coal’s full timeline](../statistics/coal-production.md) now preserves ten annual observations, a five-year comparison, two coalfields’ resource classes and six selected block identities. Ore reconciliation and wider district mapping remain open.

## Ore reconciliation checkpoint · 1 October2026

[Ore series and district links](../statistics/ore-production.md) now distinguish annual production, despatch and dated resources. Disputed IBM/state values remain held; no merged national-share measure.

## Mine-to-processing checkpoint · 1 October 2026

[Bauxite to aluminium](bauxite-to-aluminium.md) now joins selected named mines, processing and transport links to dated work and community evidence. Company totals, targets and unresolved fields remain explicit.

## Bauxite-site checkpoint · 1 October 2026

[Kodingamali and Baphlimali](bauxite-mine-identities.md) adds regulator-recorded output and a separate mine-to-refinery certification case. Capacity and audit findings retain their scope.

## Baphlimali returns · 2 October2026 UTC

[Baphlimali’s annual return](bauxite-mine-identities.md) adds realised output, captive dispatch, payments and employment denominators. Permission layers and rehabilitation scopes remain separate.

## Processing and supplier checkpoint · 2 October 2026

[Rourkela’s steel chain](rourkela-steel-chain.md) adds plant-specific financial and historical production-table evidence with work-count limits. [NALCO’s supplier story](../stories/minerals-and-local-suppliers.md) uses a newly read section of the saved annual report. RES-052 remains incomplete: chromite-to-ferrochrome is the next chain, with plant payroll and local-supplier evidence still open.

## Chromite-to-ferrochrome checkpoint · 2 October 2026

[IMFA’s existing company entry](company-imfa.md) now connects two named mines, Odisha processing and domestic/international sales. Company-wide workforce and supplier shares remain separate from plant-local measures. The three-chain research is still incomplete for plant jobs and suppliers.

## Plant-record checkpoint

[IMFA’s reconciled record](company-imfa.md) distinguishes Kalinganagar clearance transfer, Choudwar furnace input ratios and held mine workforce/output data. No employment total or expanded capacity is inferred from these records.

## Industrial work: dates and categories

[Rourkela’s historical employment record](rourkela-steel-chain.md) now distinguishes manpower, project contract workers and other contract work at 1 April 2015. This strengthens the historical record without supplying a current plant employment total.

## Mining and community services · 2026-10-02

[From mineral revenues to working community services](dmf-community-outcomes.md) links actual state receipts, six audited DMF districts and four named case bundles. Construction completion, operating service and community benefit remain distinct. Government replies and original-table discrepancies are retained; current operation and resident outcomes remain open.

## Land, rights, safety and restoration · 3 October 2026

[Four scoped cases](mining-land-and-people.md) connect Sukurangi monitoring, Niyamgiri rights, Bharatpur haul-road safety and Baphlimali rehabilitation. Reported findings, decisions and actual outcomes remain separate; original monitoring and implementation/recovery records still need follow-up.

body:
# Rasagola economics and Odisha’s sweets

**Follow a sweet from milk to market.** Rasagola economics can connect dairy farmers, chhena makers, sweet shops, packaging, cold storage, transport, festivals and overseas buyers. This is our research framework; a statewide revenue total has not yet been established.

## Build on the existing sweet records

- [Odisha Rasagola](../food/odisha-rasagola.md): retain the historical GI certificate and distinguish Pahala/Salepur business clusters from the protected product’s statewide geography.
- [Chhena poda](../food/chhena-poda.md): deepen local history, preparation and producer evidence.
- [Chhena jhili](../food/chhena-jhili.md): place-linked Nimapada research.
- [Kendrapara Rasabali](../food/kendrapara-rasabali.md): separate GI record, cultural context and enterprise data.
- [Dhenkanal Magji](../food/dhenkanal-magji.md): names, ingredients, historical record and producer verification.
- [Korakhai](../food/korakhai.md): ritual and place context; commercial output remains to research.

These are existing research records, not a complete sweet inventory. Khaja, chhena gaja, chhena murki and region-specific variants are follow-up candidates whose product descriptions need sources.

## What export evidence currently says

APEDA and the Odisha government displayed **Salepur Rasagolla, Kendrapada Rasabali and Dhenkanal Magaji Ladoo** at their Bhubaneswar agri-export workshop on 25 April 2025. The 27 April release discusses processing, logistics and cold-chain opportunities. This establishes export promotion, **not completed sweet shipments or export revenue**.

## The numbers to collect

| Measure | Required scope |
|---|---|
| Milk and chhena input; sweet output | Producer, period, kg/litres, yield and wastage |
| Sales | Named business or representative survey; domestic and export revenue separate |
| Work and income | Paid workers, family work, seasonality, wages and net income |
| Export shipments | Actual shipment date, producer origin, quantity, value, destination and product identity |
| Costs | Milk, sugar, labour, fuel, packaging, transport and spoilage on the same batch basis |
| Cluster scale | Counted enterprises and sampling method; avoid multiplying a few popular shops by an invented statewide total |

All sweet-specific export quantities, values and destination counts remain unknown in this batch. Overseas online availability is a lead, not proof of an Odisha-origin shipment. Customs categories may aggregate many sweets, and shipments via another state may obscure manufacturing origin. Reconcile these before claiming a global rasagola market size.

A future margin calculator can use explicit user inputs; scenario estimates must remain separate from observed industry statistics. Research lawful shelf-life and packaging evidence from responsible food-science authorities before publishing operational guidance.

[Export-promotion source](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2124747) · [Structured open measures](../references/data/creative-economy.json).

[Odisha Rasagola](../food/odisha-rasagola.md) — Read product identity alongside economic questions; a GI record does not measure industry revenue.

## Rasabali evidence lead · 1 October 2026

The [Rasabali preparation follow-up](../food/kendrapara-rasabali.md) captures the original 2023 GI applicant’s seller/maker claims and the correction that repeats them. Their reference period and method are absent; they remain held leads in [the preparation register](../references/data/food-preparations.json), owned by RES-031. No current employment total, revenue or export estimate has been added.

## A supply chain we can actually trace · 2 October 2026

**Niali’s chhena connects dairy work with Pahala’s sweet market.** A December 2023 case study interviewed 10 retailers and 200 consumers. It describes supply from Niali and sales reaching other Odisha markets and West Bengal. These are the authors’ study findings; fieldwork dates and shipment quantities are not given. [Original study, pp.2306–2307](https://ndpublisher.in/admin/issues/EAv68n5z11.pdf).

The study’s ingredient table totals ₹2,000 for a described 20 kg batch. This is an ingredient bill, not the full cost of production or profit. Its consumer table ranks short shelf life as the leading concern. That gives us a grounded research direction: packaging, product consistency and distribution, alongside the sweet’s cultural appeal. [Tables 1–2](https://ndpublisher.in/admin/issues/EAv68n5z11.pdf).

### Numbers that need correction or more evidence

The paper says 10 kg yields ₹3,000–₹4,000 at a stated ₹150–₹200/kg. Those inputs produce ₹1,500–₹2,000. We preserve the discrepancy and withhold its extrapolated cluster revenue. Retailer percentages also lack a denominator consistent with its ten-person sample. Neither these figures nor the undated ₹5,500-crore claim on a [government-hosted news page](https://industries.odisha.gov.in/news/rasagola-makers-odisha-seek-government-support-wider-reach) becomes a statewide market-size statistic.

### One promising enterprise lead

The January 2026 SDG volume’s indexed p.26 describes **Kamadhenu Utpadaka Gosthi**, a women-led chhenapoda enterprise at Tendabadi in Daspalla. Its membership, production and financial figures remain in the provisional register: the complete PDF could not be retrieved and the observation period is unclear. [Government case-study lead](https://sdg.odisha.gov.in/uploads/6052f16a-22b0-4ee3-9d98-0e6672b77ba3_1e128a94-3ef5-4bc8-80dc-fce54e1db29e.pdf). No current revenue, profit per member or verified growth headline is claimed.

### Six sweets, different economic questions

| Existing entry | Next useful evidence |
| --- | --- |
| [Rasagola](../food/odisha-rasagola.md) | Resolve study arithmetic; obtain dated maker accounts and shipment records |
| [Chhena poda](../food/chhena-poda.md) | Recover the enterprise case study and establish its accounting period |
| [Chhena jhili](../food/chhena-jhili.md) | Credit a Nimapada maker and document enterprise history |
| [Rasabali](../food/kendrapara-rasabali.md) | Date the applicant’s seller/maker claims and obtain production or sales records |
| [Magji](../food/dhenkanal-magji.md) | Follow the named association and original historical references |
| [Korakhai](../food/korakhai.md) | Establish named confectioners, ritual roles and rice-based production economics |

The [APEDA directory](https://apeda.gov.in/exporter-directory) and [commodity filter](https://agriexchange.apeda.gov.in/IndiaExport/Home/SearchFilters) provide routes for further work, but this run recovered no sweet-specific shipment rows. This means **unknown exports**, not zero exports. The 2025 exhibition remains export promotion.

[Structured evidence, calculations and held claims](../references/data/sweets-economy.json). RES-031 remains in progress; six-sweet maker/history and market depth is not yet complete.

## Makers and a historical trade trail · 2 October 2026

The [Chhena jhili](../food/chhena-jhili.md) entry now credits a maker through a university reference. [Korakhai](../food/korakhai.md) adds named confectioners from dated reporting and a stronger economic-history anchor: Bhubaneswar’s 1999 town commodity listing records the sweet in both manufacturing and outward trade. [Census handbook, Statement VI, p.499](https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/44136/download/47792/DH_21_2001_KHO.pdf). The directory offers a research trail into local commerce, without establishing foreign exports or a sales ranking.

These are extensions of existing food identities. Three maker credits live within the [shared evidence register](../references/data/sweets-economy.json); full biographies and current venue listings await stronger evidence. Six-sweet research continues with Magji’s original historical references and Rasabali’s undated producer claims.

## From recognition to a market: what is documented

**A dated selling venue is a useful step toward a market story.** January 2026 reporting places [Rasabali](../food/kendrapara-rasabali.md) at Sisir Saras in Bhubaneswar. It supports an event connection, without quantifying this sweet’s sales. [Market report](https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/bhubaneswar/2026/Jan/16/stalls-selling-gi-tagged-products-major-crowd-puller-at-sisir-saras). The earlier maker comments express hopes for better prices; they do not supply a before-and-after series.

For [Magji](../food/dhenkanal-magji.md), a named maker’s family account adds credit to inherited skill. The original district-history books remain unread; a launch report now supplies a bibliographic lead. The collection keeps these evidence classes separate from dated accounts and shipment records.

This pass recovered no product-level production, employment, sales or completed export series for these two sweets. The NABARD document fetches failed; their indexed support figures remain excluded. Existing Rasabali seller/maker claims lack periods and methods. These gaps are unknowns, not zero activity. RES-031 has a saved continuation for 9 October; handloom research can proceed independently.

body:
# Odisha’s rice economy: from paddy to value

**Rice is both a staple and a chain of livelihoods.** Start with production, then distinguish what farmers sell, what mills process and what consumers buy.

## The scale of the crop

Odisha Agriculture Statistics 2023–24 reports **115.39 lakh tonnes of rice**, across **40.87 lakh crop-hectares**, with average rice yield **2,823 kg/ha**. The same table reports **174.83 lakh tonnes of paddy**. These are two product bases for the crop, not quantities to add together. Seasonal crop area is not unique land or a farmer count. [Printed p.65](https://agri.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2025-05/OAS%20A4.pdf).

The existing [agriculture series](../statistics/agriculture.md) retains the separately sourced 2024–25 rice estimate of 118.6 lakh tonnes. No growth rate has been spliced across these publications in this edition.

## Procurement is one part of the market

The department’s 2024–25 report lists **70.89 lakh tonnes of paddy procured in KMS 2023–24**, including **12.36 lakh tonnes in Bargarh**, and **1,372 participating millers**. Millers participating in procurement are not a census of every rice business. [Annexure I, p.12; milling, p.27](https://www.foododisha.in/Download/annual-activity-glance-24-25.pdf).

For **KMS 2024–25**, that report gives common-paddy MSP of ₹2,300/quintal, Grade-A MSP of ₹2,320, and additional state assistance of ₹800/quintal. The common-paddy combination is ₹3,100/quintal for the applicable scheme: a historical policy rate, not a current retail quote or net profit. Registration, quality and scheme conditions matter. [Report p.9](https://www.foododisha.in/Download/annual-activity-glance-24-25.pdf).

## Where value can be measured next

| Part of the chain | Evidence to collect |
|---|---|
| Seed keeping and seed sale | Named varieties, growers, volumes, seed prices and benefit sharing |
| Farming | District/season yield, paid costs, family labour, land costs and actual sale receipts |
| Procurement | Marketing year, accepted quantity, farmers paid and payment timing |
| Milling | Paddy input, rice recovery, broken grain, bran and husk; processing and transport costs |
| Distinctive rice | Traceable origin, actual farmgate and retail transactions for the same product/date |
| Trade | Odisha-origin shipments, destination, quantity and realised value |

A retail premium is not the farmer’s premium. Farm receipts minus clearly defined costs are needed before claiming profitability. Production multiplied by MSP is not measured statewide revenue. Shipments through an Odisha port do not by themselves establish Odisha-grown rice exports.

## Open evidence checks

The earlier report’s partial KMS 2024–25 payment/quantity snapshot remains held. Its KMS 2023–24 aggregate is now contextualised by the later report recovered on 2 October 2026 UTC; see the reconciliation below. Earlier values remain in the [register](../references/data/rice-economy.json).

Comparable production series and district snapshots are saved below. Next work: matched procurement settlements, dated farmer cost evidence, premium-variety transactions and attributable exports. [Rice identities and seed keepers](../food/rice-varieties.md) provide the cultural and agricultural context.

## Comparable trends: growth with setbacks

[The rice productivity story](../stories/rice-productivity.md) provides a chart and five-/ten-year comparisons from the same historical table. Every intervening year is preserved. Detailed 2023–24 figures above and whole-thousand historical-table values remain separately labelled precision variants from one publication.

## Yield and profit can move differently

Samant and colleagues report a coastal Odisha experiment in 2019–20 and 2020–21: transplanted rice had higher yield, but direct-seeded rice had higher reported net return. Transplanting’s mean cost was ₹77,816/ha and gross return ₹112,353/ha; direct seeding’s reported net return was ₹39,121/ha. [Original ORYZA abstract, published 30 June 2023](https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/OIJR/article/view/138554).

This is a study-period experimental comparison. The full itemised cost basis and price schedule are still needed before interpreting it as an all-cost profit comparison, a representative household outcome or a current budget. It does not justify choosing a farming method without local agronomic advice.

## Procurement payment reconciliation: later report recovered

The earlier report gave ₹16,883.03 crore for KMS 2023–24 MSP payments. The **2025–26 report instead gives ₹15,475.18 crore** for that same category and year (p.29). Multiplying the saved 7,088,950 tonnes by 10 quintals/tonne and ₹2,183/quintal gives ₹15,475.17785 crore, which rounds to the later amount. We use the later report with this provenance. No formal correction notice or independently audited settlement record was recovered; the earlier claim remains preserved.

For **KMS 2024–25**, the newer report gives **₹28,718 crore paid as MSP plus input assistance**. Its detailed seasonal quantities sum to 9,264,235 tonnes. At the common-paddy combined rate, this implies ₹28,719.1285 crore—a small difference that still needs settlement detail. We retain the reported amount and do not label the calculation as an audited payment total. [Newer report, pp.10,26,29](https://foododisha.in/Download/annual-activity-glance-25-26.pdf).

The report also gives 86.30 lakh tonnes for **FY 2024–25**, a different window from **KMS 2024–25**. A marketing year runs October–September; a financial year runs April–March. Page 8 contains an internally inconsistent partial-snapshot date and seasonal wording; neither is used for a fresh public headline. The earlier partial 2024–25 payment snapshot remains unresolved.

[The public story draft](../stories/rice-procurement-payments.md) keeps combined payments separate from MSP-only payments and from farm profit.

## Seed production is its own market

[The Kalahandi seed-enterprise case](../food/rice-varieties.md) adds dated collective production and named seed classes. Seed output does not establish completed sales or member earnings. Variety-specific output, processing costs, realised seed prices and payment records remain the next economic questions.

## What remains after growing the rice?

A regional study published in March 2023 reports **₹79,050/ha gross income** and **₹14,141.58/ha net income after C2 costs** for its paddy case. C2 includes valued family labour, land and owned-capital costs. Its A2 cost of ₹41,013.10/ha also includes depreciation and owned inputs; it is not simply cash spending. [Sahoo and colleagues, Tables 5–7](https://ndpublisher.in/countpdfdownload.php?id=5788&pdf=EAv68n1p.pdf).

The full study sampled 120 farmers across six clusters; the paddy-specific sample and survey year are unclear. Context tables use 2018–19, which we have not assigned to the paddy case. These nominal historical values cannot be extrapolated to statewide farmer profit or compared with current MSP as a margin.

[The short cost story](../stories/rice-income-after-costs.md) explains the difference between gross value and net income. The [structured case](../references/data/rice-economy.json) retains rounding differences and conflicting definitions. The existing Samant experimental case remains separately identified.
