body:
# Rourkela: ore, steel and the evidence for work

**A mine-to-metal story needs more than an expansion announcement.** Rourkela gives us a named processing plant, dated output and financial records, and a historical ore route from Sundargarh.

## The route we can document

SAIL’s June 2021 pre-feasibility report describes the Barsua valley railway connection through Bondamunda as established to carry iron ore to Rourkela. It also proposes larger Barsua–Taldih–Kalta mining and processing facilities to supply Rourkela and other SAIL plants. The existing transport description and future expansion are different claims. [Report, printed p.28 and pp.1–3](https://environmentclearance.nic.in/writereaddata/Online/TOR/28_Jun_2021_17124567022642313PFRjune2021.pdf).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 B[Barsua valley iron ore] -->|Route described in June 2021 report| R[Rourkela integrated steel plant]
 R --> F[Flat steel products]
 T[Barsua–Taldih–Kalta expansion proposal] -. Planned supply increase .-> R
```

The arrows do not establish present shipment quantities or exclusive supply. Exact mine-to-plant despatch records remain missing.

## Production: keep the flat year visible

The May 2026 compliance report’s carbon-budget table gives these historical crude-steel values:

| Financial year | Reported historical output, million tonnes |
|---|---:|
|2023–24|4.161|
|2024–25|4.045|
|2025–26|4.046|

That is a **2.8% decline**, followed by a **near-flat year** (about 0.02% higher). The table mixes historical values with future targets; only completed-year columns are used here. Its 4.850 MTPA clearance figure is capacity. Exact annual tonnage still needs reconciliation with production returns. [Compliance report, PDF p.27](https://sail.co.in/sites/default/files/steel-plants/2026-06/5_%20RSPs%20implementation%20status%20of%20conditions%20of%20EC%20received%20for%20HM%204.855%20MTPA%20Proejct%20other%20new%20projects%20Oct.%2C2025%20-%20March%2C%202026.pdf).

## Financial recovery is a separate story

SAIL reports **₹888.25 crore profit before tax for the Rourkela unit in 2025–26**, versus ₹20.24 crore in 2024–25. Present both figures rather than a dramatic percentage from the small base. Profit, output and benefits to local households are different measures. [Annual report, printed p.66](https://www.sail.co.in/sites/default/files/2026-09/Annual%20Report%20-%202025-26.pdf).

## What the work evidence does—and does not—show

The compliance report lists 9,872 permanent-employee and 10,803 contractual-worker entries for 2025–26 in a **health-check-up table** (PDF p.15). It reports 100% coverage but does not establish a payroll snapshot date, unique-person methodology or local residence. These numbers are retained as health-service context, not new jobs or a verified workforce total. SAIL’s 49,752 employees at 1 April 2026 are company-wide and likewise cannot be assigned to Rourkela.

Direct/contract employment, local-supplier purchases and shipment quantities remain the next plant-level evidence needs. Neither the 2021 proposal’s additional 1,133 positions nor its ₹2,740.88 crore estimated cost is treated as a realised outcome.

[Mining programme](mining.md) · [Existing bauxite chain](bauxite-to-aluminium.md) · [Detailed observations and boundaries](../references/data/mining-programme.json) · [Sundargarh](../statistics/districts/sundargarh.md).

[Mining research](mining.md) — Connects plant and supplier evidence to the broader mining programme without equating company results with household benefits.

## The people behind an expansion: a historical snapshot

**Rourkela reported 9,067 contract workers on 1 April 2015.** Of these, 5,346 were assigned to projects and 3,721 to other works and non-works activities. The same table separately lists 16,939 under manpower. These categories show why an industrial employment story needs to distinguish building projects from other plant work. [Ministry of Steel, parliamentary answer 6 May 2015, p.2](https://steel.gov.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ru1184.pdf).

| Source category | People at 1 April 2015 |
|---|---:|
| Manpower |16,939|
| Contract workers: projects |5,346|
| Contract workers: others |3,721|
| Contract workers: total |9,067|

The two contract components sum to the contract total; they must not be added again. This is a historical snapshot, not current employment or 9,067 newly created jobs. It gives no local-resident share. The 2026 health-check table has a different purpose and cannot provide a valid employment trend from this baseline. Current plant workforce, contractor definitions and local supplier spending remain unresolved.

## A supplier trail—and a limited employment claim

The RSP account’s July 2026 meeting report places orders to Odisha-based LSSIs at **₹133.46 crore for FY2025–26**. It also cites ₹12.23 crore for FY1984–85. These are nominal order values; payments and a consistent four-decade definition are not established. [Source and limits](../sources/mining-rsp-subplac2026.md).

A separate June communication reports **73 contractual placements** for a relocation cohort. This does not measure plant employment or confirm wages and continued retention. The 2 June date belongs to compensation disbursement, not explicitly the placement count. [Source and limits](../sources/mining-rsp-relocation2026.md).

Both are account-attributed statements awaiting underlying records and independent community evidence. Current RSP payroll and contractor headcount remain open. The next useful source would identify the plant/mine boundary, snapshot date and whether people appearing under multiple contractors are counted once.

body:
# Sal: leaf craft, seeds and seasonal care

**Sal (*Shorea robusta*) is a tree with several distinct product streams.** Its leaves support plates, bowls and wrapping; its seeds belong to a separate oilseed chain. Keep it distinct from the siali climber and from edible forest-food ingredients.

The Balliguda working plan for **2021–22 to 2030–31** names **September–January** as an ideal leaf-collection window. It cautions against stripping plants and collecting tender foliage. This is a local management prescription, not an observed annual collection series or present statewide permission to harvest. Its botanical account places fruit maturity in **May–June**; fruiting, collection and sale are different events. [Printed pp.199–200](https://odishaforest.in/admin/data/documents/div_working_plan_file_831468672.pdf).

The [siali profile](siali-products.md) retains a named Nayagarh maker's historical account of sal hand stitching alongside machine-sewn siali. That testimony connects material knowledge and household work without treating every maker's practice as identical.

[Mahua preparation](../food/mahua-mohula.md) also records sal leaves as a cooking wrapper in a separate Santhal field account. A wrapper is not an edible ingredient; a seed-oil use description is not a home extraction or food-safety recipe.

Current collectors, volumes, prices, realised earnings and product-specific exports remain unknown. Follow these in the [forest-products market research](forest-products.md), preserving season, plant part, origin and evidence date.

[Related reading](siali-products.md) — Distinguishes leaf-plate materials and connects shared processing questions; does not imply identical seasons, makers or economic outcomes.

body:
# Siali: leaves, fibre and a distinct plant identity

**Siali needs a separate identity from sal.** IISc's Eastern Ghats flora places Siali and Sialpatra under *Phanera vahlii*, retaining *Bauhinia vahlii* as another taxonomic name. It describes a liana and records Odisha localities including Koraput and the Similipal hills. This is a botanical locality reference, not a harvest or enterprise census. [IISc](https://indiaflora-ces.iisc.ac.in/EasternGhats/herbsheet.php?cat=4&id=1830).

## Separate material and use

- **Leaves:** Vasundhara's previously saved livelihood account lists siali leaves among traded products. Record leaf collection, stitching, processing and sales as separate questions; current output and prices remain unknown.
- **Fibre:** SCSTRTI's historical Mankirdia account describes siali-fibre ropes, slings, nets, bags and small baskets (printed p.32). Attribute this account to that community and source, not every Odisha household.
- **Seeds:** IISc notes food use, but does not establish a local recipe, present market or safe identification procedure for a reader. Keep seeds distinct from leaf and fibre commodities.

## Names prevent misleading stories

The flora also lists “Mahul” among Hindi names for siali. A similar-looking name must not merge it with [mahua/mohula](../food/mahua-mohula.md), whose botanical reference is *Madhuca*. Likewise, [Mohu](../food/mohu-honey.md) means honey in the user's clarification. Local names need language and plant-part fields.

The local accounts below begin to document leaf-plate manufacture, maker attribution and seasonality. Present operations, wider raw-material sourcing and environmental comparisons remain research questions. Material being plant-based alone does not prove sustainable harvesting, a particular life-cycle footprint or measured exports.

[Forest-product collection](forest-products.md) · [Food and seasonal knowledge](../food/forest-foods.md).

[Related reading](../food/mahua-mohula.md) — Disambiguates siali names from the separate Madhuca tree and its flower/seed products.

[Related reading](../food/mohu-honey.md) — Connects forest livelihood research without merging honey with similarly transliterated plant names.

## From leaf collection to a finished plate

The Balliguda working plan for **2021–22 to 2030–31** describes siali leaves being sun-dried for **two to three days**, then joined with bamboo slivers: **five to six leaves per plate**, packed in bundles of **80 plates**. These are a division account's process and packing conventions, not a universal standard or measured factory output. It identifies **October–February** as the local peak for leaf quality and availability. [Plan, printed pp.198–199](https://odishaforest.in/admin/data/documents/div_working_plan_file_831468672.pdf).

## A named maker and a different local calendar

CYSD's February–April **2002** fieldwork records **Rajani Majhi of Satajhari, Nayagarh**, collecting forest leaves with other women. Her case describes machine sewing for siali and bamboo-stick hand stitching for sal. Its account places abundant leaf supply in **May–January**, poor sewing suitability in **February–April**, and greater priority for agriculture in **July–September**. The seasonal paragraph follows the siali production account, but the household handles both leaves; its exact species scope remains qualified. Forest degradation is reported as a concern. This is published testimony, not a new interview. [NRI Report 2714, printed p.26](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/57a08d48e5274a31e0001784/cysd-orissa-2714.pdf).

Do not average the Nayagarh and Balliguda windows into an Odisha calendar: they differ in place, period, species precision and whether they describe broad availability or peak quality.

## The skills between forest and dining table

JICA's **February 2017** survey describes a Kandhamal chain from collection and stitching through drying, bundling, trading and further trimming or pressing. It distinguishes hand, sewing-machine and press-moulded products. This gives us a useful editorial connection between forest knowledge, women's work, craft and food service. It supplies no current statewide employment or export total here. [Attachment 6.9.3-13–14](https://openjicareport.jica.go.jp/pdf/12284139_02.pdf).

[Sal leaves and seeds](sal-products.md) explains the separate tree, material uses and local collection prescription. The leaf-plate story deserves its own craft and livelihood context; environmental superiority still needs a measured comparison.

Ethnobotanical exploration of wild edible fruits of Balasore district in Odisha, India

body:
# Bela pana: a summer drink and an Odia New Year connection

Bela pana brings ripe bael fruit into Odisha’s summer-drink repertoire. The ingredient is **bela, *Aegle marmelos***. The saved [Balasore fruit study](../sources/food-koli-balasore2020.md), Table 1 row 1, records its pulp in sherbet and squash; row 42 separately identifies kaitha as *Limonia acidissima*. English “wood apple” labels alone should not merge these fruits.

## How one home version is made

[Sasmita Sahoo’s 2021 account](https://rosheighara.wordpress.com/2021/04/16/4-traditional-healthy-drinks-of-odisha/) places Bela pana among summer drinks. Her version uses one bael fruit, five glasses of water, sugar or mishri, and black pepper.

1. Dissolve the sweetener in water.
2. Open the fruit and scoop out its pulp.
3. Work the pulp into the water and separate the seeds.
4. Strain; finish each serving with pepper. Ice is optional in this account.

**Quantity gaps:** glass size and sweetener amount are unspecified. The ingredient list gives a “small tablespoon” of pepper, while the method says a pinch per serving. Keep that discrepancy visible: this is an attributed method, not a calibrated or kitchen-tested Utkal recipe.

## More than one preparation

[Chef Reetu Uday Kugaji’s account](https://chefreetuudaykugaji.com/blog/2023/03/06/bael-ka-sharbat-bel-ka-sharbatwood-apple-sharbat%EF%BF%BC/) describes an Odisha version with pepper, grated coconut, mashed banana and chhena alongside strained bael, water and sugar or jaggery. This is a credited variation, not a rule for every household. Her separate measured sharbat-concentrate recipe is not relabelled as this Bela pana version.

## Summer and Odia New Year

[Fakir Mohan University’s report](https://fmuniversity.nic.in/getdata?dir=InstituteNews&rid=inewsEvent75_15420231681554279989.pdf) documents Bela pana at its **14 April 2023 Odia New Year / Maha Bishuba Sankranti celebration** in Nuapadhi, Balasore. This establishes a specific cultural example, not participation totals or one obligatory festival recipe.

The Balasore field study reports May–June for Bela fruiting within its January 2018–February 2020 survey of five blocks. That source-specific season is not a statewide retail calendar, and an April festival serving does not establish an April local harvest. A government-hosted Odisha Review article on Bela and Pana Sankranti remains a follow-up: its full PDF exceeded the browser fetch limit in this run.

## What to collect next

Record household and district variations, reviewed Odia spelling, fruit size or pulp weight, measured water and sweetness, and an actually tested preparation. A dated vendor sample could document fruit prices, servings per fruit and sales; **current prices, statewide production, drink revenue and exports remain unknown**. No health-treatment or shelf-life claims from the recipe sources are adopted.

## Proposed story treatment

**Odisha’s Best-Kept Secret · A summer glass of bela pana.** Follow the fruit from a tree or market to an attributed household recipe and an evidenced festival setting. This is an editorial proposal; photographs, interviews and market observations have not been produced.


[Everyday food culture](everyday-food-culture.md) — Connects a seasonal fruit drink with household food knowledge and documented preparations.

[Koli fruits](koli-fruits.md) — Connects Bela ingredient identification with source-specific local fruit names; this does not classify Bela as a koli cultivar.

sources.title: Ethnobotanical exploration of wild edible fruits of Balasore district in Odisha, India

body:
# Chara koli and chironji: fruit, seed and kernel

**A fruit name and a traded kernel can tell different parts of the same plant's story.** Odisha's existing Koli register identifies chara koli as *Buchanania lanzan*. ICAR-CIAH uses that botanical name for chironji. This links the names through their reported plant identity; it does not establish that every lot sold as “char seed” is a shelled kernel.

## A seasonal food account

Noor and Satapathy's **2018–2020 Balasore survey** gives **April–May** as the fruiting period. It records kernels eaten raw or roasted and used in sweet preparations. No specific Odisha sweet recipe, proportions or roasting endpoint is supplied. [Table 1, row 15, printed p.451](https://www.botanyjournals.com/assets/archives/2020/vol5issue3/5-3-106-999.pdf).

## Community knowledge and trade

SCSTRTI's study lists **Char Seed / Char Manji, Buchanania lanzan**, among market products for **Juang communities in Hatisila, Nadam and Sarai** (Table 2.16, printed p.49). It also records summer chara fruit/seed use in its Hill Kharia–Mankirdia food table (Table 3.7, printed p.63). The study date remains unresolved; these accounts establish attributed historical uses, not present sales, income or universal practice. [Source](https://repository.tribal.gov.in/bitstream/123456789/74427/1/SCST_2014_research_0338.pdf).

Keep **whole fruit → hard seed/nut → separated kernel** distinct when collecting weights and prices. Shelling yield, breakage, labour and grade would explain value addition, but no Odisha measurements have yet been established.

## Cultivars and processing research

ICAR-CIAH lists **Thar Priya** under chironji. This is a documented cultivar, not evidence that it grows commercially in Odisha. The field-study wild-food classification likewise cannot certify the origin of purchased nuts. [SVRC row 3](https://www.icar-ciah.org/index.php?do=veriti_relese_svrc&mod=veriti).

A **2012 processing paper** is bibliographically located, but the original page and PDF were unavailable. Its indexed abstract is retained as a follow-up lead; its machinery, oil-content and market claims are not adopted as current local facts. [Publisher record](https://nopr.niscpr.res.in/handle/123456789/13445).

[Koli collection](koli-fruits.md) preserves the original identity record. Local Odia spellings, community-attributed recipes, dated collector prices, shelling yields and actual shipments remain next fields to verify.

[Related reading](../economy/forest-products.md) — Connects a named ingredient to plant-part, season and collector-market questions; does not establish current income or exports.

## Preparation and variations · 1 October 2026

The specification uses pressed buffalo-milk cheese, sugar and cardamom, cooked in a pan and hand-shaped. It identifies Mandar–Sadangi and the wider Dhenkanal production area. [Dhenkanal Magji — GI Journal 178 specification](https://search.ipindia.gov.in/IPOJournal/Journal/GIR), Printed/PDF pp.45–50; description, geographical area and method. Applicant specification published by the GI Registry; historical production description, not a tested household recipe or independent economic evaluation.

The same journal gives sugar quantities of 400–500 g per kg cheese on pp.45/48, 400 g on p.46, and 300–400 g on p.47. No single recipe quantity is adopted.

**Still to verify:** Reconcile internal sugar proportions with an original clarification and a credited producer; distinguish documented process from origin legends, comparative nutrition and shelf-life claims. Odia and local review remain pending.

[Preparation collection](preparation-and-variation.md) — Compare techniques and attributed versions across the existing food entries.

## Makers and historical references

The saved 2023 specification names **Dhenkanal Sweets Association** as applicant and OUAT as facilitator (p.45). It links production to Mandar–Sadangi in Gondia and cites Pramod Kumar Mishra’s *Adhunika Dhenkanal Itihas* p.230 and *Abibhakta Dhenkanal Itihas* p.291 (p.47). Those books have not been inspected here. The accompanying saint-origin story is an attributed tradition, not verified chronology. [Original specification](../sources/food-magji-gi178.md).

This gives the [economic research](../economy/rasagola-and-sweets.md) a named institutional lead without treating association membership, GI status or historical descriptions as measured production or sales.

## A family craft, with an open history trail

A January 2024 report quotes **Hrushikesh Sahoo of Sadangi** describing Magji making by his grandfather, father and himself. This is a credited family account, not an independently dated origin history. [Interview Times, 4 January 2024](https://interviewtimes.net/dhenkanal-magji-gets-gi-tag/).

A [14 August 2021 Odia report](https://www.localnewsodia.com/35485dhenkanal-district-history-book-launch/) describes the launch of a Pramod Kumar Mishra history of undivided Dhenkanal. It offers a route toward the books cited by the GI applicant, but does not establish an edition match or verify their cited pages. The saint-origin story and a claimed Fakir Mohan Senapati–John Beams gift remain unverified accounts in that specification. No original book scan was located in this bounded search.

Current shop operation, sales and international shipments remain unknown. [Research gaps and retry plan](../references/data/sweets-economy.json).

[Related economic research](../economy/rasagola-and-sweets.md) — A named family account connects sweet-making knowledge with livelihood research; its economic value remains unmeasured.

# Odisha’s everyday food culture

A meal can tell a large story through its smallest accompaniments. This collection follows drying, crushing, leaf cooking, seasonal fruit and rice-water preparations, giving everyday knowledge its own place in Utkal. This framing is editorial; the accounts below identify their contributors and limits.

| Food | What the evidence lets us explore |
|---|---|
| [Badi chura](badi-chura.md) | Condiment; preserving and crushing. |
| [Sukhua](sukhua.md) | Preserved ingredient family; drying and cooking. |
| [Tala pitha](tala-pitha.md) | Seasonal preparation family; ripe palm fruit preparations. |
| [Torani and torani pani](torani.md) | Rice-water food and drink terminology; meal liquids. |
| [Torani kanji](torani-kanji.md) | Cooked dish; boiling and tempering. |
| [Patra poda chatu](chatu-patrapoda.md) | Reuse the existing mushroom entry: leaf wrapping and mustard-seasoned cooking. |

## Tala khaja: a seed-food lead

Ahimanikya clarified on 1 October 2026 that “khaja is seed produce.” Preserve **tala khaja** as the supplied palm-seed food name. The user subsequently clarified the intended later/final seed-food stage, distinct from ice apple; preparation, precise botanical anatomy and local/Odia spelling remain to be documented. Do not merge it with the khaja pastry or automatically equate it to tala gaja or tala saja. A Commons photograph labelled tala gaja in Baleswar remains an indexed discovery lead; direct page access failed again on 1 October. No image reuse or identity decision follows from that caption.

## A useful way to tell the story

Begin with the ingredient and the hands that prepare it, then show its place in a meal. Add the local name, season, district or community only when evidenced. Producer livelihoods belong beside culinary practice; state totals, exports and nutrition claims need their own evidence.

Next collection candidates are saga preparations, ambula and other souring ingredients, chutneys, seasonal greens and household preservation. Search existing records before creating identities. Local participation and Odia review remain pending.


[badi chura](badi-chura.md) — Connects badi chura with the collection’s documented meal practices; this is editorial context, not a claim of uniform statewide custom.

[sukhua](sukhua.md) — Connects sukhua with the collection’s documented meal practices; this is editorial context, not a claim of uniform statewide custom.

[tala pitha](tala-pitha.md) — Connects tala pitha with the collection’s documented meal practices; this is editorial context, not a claim of uniform statewide custom.

[torani](torani.md) — Connects torani with the collection’s documented meal practices; this is editorial context, not a claim of uniform statewide custom.

[torani kanji](torani-kanji.md) — Connects torani kanji with the collection’s documented meal practices; this is editorial context, not a claim of uniform statewide custom.

[chatu patrapoda](chatu-patrapoda.md) — Connects chatu patrapoda with the collection’s documented meal practices; this is editorial context, not a claim of uniform statewide custom.

[pakhala](pakhala.md) — Connects pakhala with the collection’s documented meal practices; this is editorial context, not a claim of uniform statewide custom.

[Koli: local fruit names and varieties](koli-fruits.md) — source-specific plant names, seasons and unresolved local-name overlap.

[Bela pana](bela-pana.md) — summer preparation, credited variations and a documented Odia New Year serving.

## Germinated-seed comparison documented

[Talagaja](talagaja.md) now has an original Odisha field-study account distinguishing germinated seed food from young-fruit endosperm and ripe-fruit pitha. This narrows the research question but does not establish that tala khaja is the same local name. Exact spelling, documentary name equivalence and recipe remain open; the user’s intended distinction from ice apple is now explicit.

## User-supplied visual reference · 1 October 2026

An image supplied in this discussion shows a split dark fibrous covering and a white interior. Ahimanikya then clarified that this is the later/final food stage and is different from ice apple. Record that as the user’s identification of the intended food. Species, precise botanical anatomy and documentary khaja/gaja equivalence still require independent evidence. The image is retained in the local research workspace; its creator and public reuse rights are unverified.

## Stage distinction clarified by the user

**Tala khaja refers here to the later/final seed-food stage shown in the supplied image, not ice apple.** This identification is attributed to Ahimanikya’s clarification on 1 October 2026. Keep it separate from young-fruit food in the index. The documented Talagaja germinated-seed account remains the comparison for further name and anatomy research.

## Palm-seed research deepened

[The Talagaja comparison](talagaja.md) now explains the haustorium using primary seed-development research, separates young fruit from ripe pulp and seedling foods, and records experimental flour work. Regional words are attributed leads; the user’s tala khaja name remains intact. No current Odisha trade or household nutrition figures established.

# Forest foods: knowledge, seasons and everyday life

**Build this collection around ingredients, the people who know them and the seasons in which they are used.** Household food, local exchange and commercial trade deserve separate evidence.

## Reuse the food identities already documented

[Koli fruits](koli-fruits.md) already records botanical and local-name distinctions, including chara, jammu and several kinds of bara. That collection is a starting point for location-specific forest-food research, not proof that every market fruit is wild harvested. [Ou khatta](ou-khatta.md) and [bela pana](bela-pana.md) preserve attributed preparations; record cultivated, garden and wild origins separately when known. [Chatu patrapoda](chatu-patrapoda.md) connects food with leaf cooking, but a recipe does not establish a mushroom's wild origin or edible species identity.

## What households keep matters too

Mishra and Pradhan's 2018 publication describes 120 households in six villages of Patana and Bansapal, Kendujhar. Its abstract reports that **38.09% of collected non-timber forest products were consumed and 61.91% sold**. This includes edible and non-edible materials; it is not a diet share. The fieldwork year is unspecified in the abstract, and the sample cannot represent all Odisha. [Study abstract](https://ideas.repec.org/a/ags/injagm/399613.html).

## Product stories to build

Document fruits and kernels, flowers, honey, edible leaves and shoots, tubers and identified edible fungi. These are research groups, not a verified list of edible Odisha species. Each entry needs the local name and language, identified species and plant part, place, season, community-attributed uses, preservation or preparation account, and whether supply is wild, cultivated or mixed. Do not collapse one community's knowledge into a single statewide tradition.

[Preparation and variation](preparation-and-variation.md) remains the recipe home. Add reliable, attributed versions there when available; do not publish identification-dependent wild-food instructions from a common name alone. Monetary sales cannot capture every food's household or cultural value.

[Markets and non-food products](../economy/forest-products.md) · [Historical evidence](../history/forest-livelihoods.md).

## Named profiles

[Mohu/honey](mohu-honey.md) and [mahua/mohula](mahua-mohula.md) are separate entries. The user confirmed Mohu means honey; mahua flowers and seeds remain distinct product forms. [Kendu patra](../economy/kendu-patra.md) belongs to the related non-food economy.

[Siali products](../economy/siali-products.md) connects plant identity with distinct leaf, fibre and seed uses. The mahua profile now includes attributed food-development research, while the honey profile contains a source-specific historical seasonal account.

[Mahua’s local seasonal and cake account](mahua-mohula.md) now distinguishes a documented food preparation from later university product-development work. Historical collection includes both private and forest land.

[Sal](../economy/sal-products.md) and [siali](../economy/siali-products.md) extend the food story to the materials used for wrapping and serving it. Named historical testimony and a local working plan document different practices and seasons; neither establishes present availability.

[Tentuli](tentuli-tamarind.md) and [chara/chironji](chara-chironji.md) now connect local seasons, plant parts, attributed food uses and market questions. Market-lot origin and current income remain unknown.

[^gi-rasabali]: [Kendrapara Rasabali — GI application 802](https://search.ipindia.gov.in/GIRPublicSearch/Application/Details/802)

## Preparation and variations · 1 October 2026

The reference links Rasabali to Kendrapara and describes a thick-milk/cardamom finish. [Regional Cuisine of India, BHM-602AT](https://uou.ac.in/sites/default/files/slm/BHM-602AT.pdf), Printed p.121 / PDF p.121, item 25. University teaching reference; one described version, not a definitive formula.

The 2019 menu serves fried chhena in sweetened condensed milk. [Chef TZac: Odia cuisine is an evolved cuisine](https://apps.odishatourism.gov.in/blog-detail/chef-tzac-odia-cuisine-is-an-evolved-cuisine), Odia Experience menu, dessert. Mansita Mishra’s 27 November 2019 account of a chef and restaurant menu; contemporary interpretation, not a universal or current menu.

**Still to verify:** Obtain the original GI method and a credited Kendrapara preparation; restaurant wording is not the GI standard. Odia and local review remain pending.

[Preparation collection](preparation-and-variation.md) — Compare techniques and attributed versions across the existing food entries.

## Primary-source follow-up · 1 October 2026

The May 2023 specification describes ghee-fried chhena in reduced sweetened milk; its early method includes semolina and a central hole. [Kendrapara Rasabali — GI Journal 175 advertised specification](https://search.ipindia.gov.in/IPOJournal/Journal/GIR), Printed/PDF pp.42–43,46–48. Historical applicant specification; read with September correction, not as the final sole recipe.

The September correction replaces lemon juice with chhena water in the opening method, removes semolina there, and describes round tikkis without a hole instruction. Its later method still says vinegar. [Kendrapara Rasabali — corrigendum of 29 September 2023](https://search.ipindia.gov.in/GIRPublicSearch/Application/Details/802), PDF pp.1–2,5–6. Same applicant/registry source family; unresolved internal discrepancy is held separately. No inference that a hole is legally prohibited.

**Remaining question:** Seek an original clarification of chhena-water versus vinegar instructions and a credited maker account; do not silently harmonise the correction. Local/Odia review remains pending.

## Sweets-economy research lead

The 2023 applicant specification reports nearly 300 sweet shopkeepers selling Rasabali and more than 600 people making it in Kendrapara district (Journal 175 p.49; repeated in the September correction, PDF p.8). The reference period and method are absent. These are held historical applicant claims, not current employment totals; seller and maker counts must not be added. [Original documents](../sources/food-rasabali-corrigendum2023.md). Revenue and exports remain unknown; [RES-031](../economy/rasagola-and-sweets.md) owns follow-up.

## Ritual and livelihood context

The already retrieved September 2023 applicant correction associates Rasabali with offerings to Baladevjew in Kendrapara (PDF p.2). This is an applicant’s cultural account; the page does not independently date the sweet’s origin. Its district seller/maker claims on p.8 still lack a reference period and method. [Saved correction](../sources/food-rasabali-corrigendum2023.md). The [sweets-economy register](../references/data/sweets-economy.json) keeps these distinctions visible.

## Makers and a dated market connection

An October 2023 report names **Souri Sahoo** as a Rasabali maker and **Baishava Panda** as the makers’ association president. Their comments describe expectations following GI recognition; they provide no measured price rise or export growth. [Dated report](https://www.newindianexpress.com/odisha/2023/Oct/04/kendraparas-famous-rasabali-gets-gi-tag-2620736.html).

In January 2026, Rasabali stalls were listed among featured products at **Sisir Saras in Bhubaneswar**, in reporting attributed to ORMAS officials. [16 January report](https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/bhubaneswar/2026/Jan/16/stalls-selling-gi-tagged-products-major-crowd-puller-at-sisir-saras). body:
# Koli: Odisha’s local fruit names and varieties

Koli is a useful local-language doorway into Odisha’s fruit diversity. The names below span several botanical groups; they are not cultivars of a single fruit. Preserve the place and source behind each name.

## A first selection

| Local name in the source | Botanical name as reported |
|---|---|
| Bara koli | *Ziziphus mauritiana* |
| Jangli bara koli | *Ziziphus nummularia* |
| Kantai / Kana koli | *Ziziphus oenoplia* |
| Tina koli | *Ziziphus rugosa* |
| Jammu koli | *Syzygium cumini* |
| Nara koli | *Phyllanthus acidus* |
| Karanda / Anku koli | *Carissa carandas* |
| Bhaincha koli | *Flacourtia indica* |
| Chara koli | *Buchanania lanzan* |
| Pharsa koli | *Grewia asiatica* |
| Guala koli | *Cordia dichotoma* |
| Lakhan koli | *Uvaria hamiltonii* |

Most mappings come from Noor and Satapathy’s [Balasore field study](https://www.botanyjournals.com/assets/archives/2020/vol5issue3/5-3-106-999.pdf), Table 1. Lakhan comes from [RPRC’s garden account](https://rprcbbsr.in/researchanddevelopment/conservation/wildediblefruitgarden). Botanical names retain the publications’ usage. The [structured register](../references/data/koli-fruits.json) keeps row locations and source-specific seasons.

## One local name can point to different plants

RPRC uses **Khirakoli** for *Carissa spinarum*. The Balasore table labels *Manilkara hexandra* **Khira-koli** and calls *Carissa spinarum* **Anka-koli**. This overlap needs local spelling and specimen checks; the records remain separate.

## Food, markets and conservation

RPRC connects wild fruits with village markets and maintains a conservation collection. Its institutional holdings do not establish how many koli varieties Odisha has. The Balasore study records pickle uses for bara, pharsa and guala; exact preparations require credited recipe evidence.

[Patra and Basak’s 2020 pectin study](https://www.foodandnutritionjournal.org/volume8number2/physicochemical-characterization-of-pectin-extracted-from-six-wild-edible-fruits-in-odisha-india/) supplies another Karanda koli account and a possible processing-research connection. Laboratory findings are not evidence of sales or exports.

## Next evidence

Add reviewed Odia spellings, locality, fruit photographs with rights, taste descriptions, food uses and attributed recipes. Verify named cultivars separately from species. Collect dated market observations before describing availability or prices. This is a cultural research index, not a guide for identifying something picked in the wild. No medicinal claims or general fermentation/storage advice are adopted.

## Story opportunity

**The small fruits that mark the seasons.** A proposed series could follow a verified fruit from its local name and harvest to a household preparation and village market. Photographs, interviews and recipes have not yet been produced.

[Everyday food culture](everyday-food-culture.md) — Connects fruit names and seasonal food knowledge with the existing everyday-food collection; local names do not establish identical botanical species.

[Ekamra Kanan](../places/ekamra-kanan.md) — RPRC’s botanical collections, cactus-claim scope and connections to wild fruits.

[Chara koli and chironji](chara-chironji.md) deepens the existing chara identity with product-form and community-use evidence; it is not an additional fruit species. [Tentuli](tentuli-tamarind.md) adds a separate ingredient profile from the same Balasore publication.

body:
# Mahua and mohula: flowers, seeds and changing uses

**Mahua is more than a beverage story.** Record the tree, its flowers and its seed products separately, then connect them through attributed household knowledge and trade evidence.

## Names and identity

IISc's Herbarium JCB records *Madhuca longifolia* var. *latifolia*, with *Madhuca indica* and *Madhuca latifolia* among its synonyms. Its Odia-name field includes Mahula and Mahua and lists occurrence in Odisha districts. This supplies a botanical reference, not a census of productive trees. [IISc flora](https://indiaflora-ces.iisc.ac.in/FloraPeninsular/herbsheet.php?cat=7&id=8868).

The user's spelling **Mohua** is retained as a search alias. Mohula/mahula (ମହୁଲ, editorial script pending language review) belongs here; **Mohu (ମହୁ)** means honey in the user's clarification and has a [separate profile](mohu-honey.md).

## Follow each product

| Part or product | Evidence and research boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Flowers | The saved 2001 Vasundhara study discusses mahua collection and locally brewed beverages. Food preparations and preservation need community-specific accounts. |
| Seeds and seed oil | TNAU describes oil uses including cooking and soap manufacture. This is general extension information, not evidence of a named Odisha processor's output or a home-processing instruction. |
| Beverages | Document credited cultural accounts and production histories; distinguish the flower from the finished drink and its market. |
| Other materials | Research fodder and other uses individually; do not infer every part is edible or medicinally effective. |

TNAU describes both forest occurrence and cultivation near villages. Consequently, mahua supplied to a market must not automatically be labelled wild harvested. Its broad March–April flowering account is a lead for local calendars, not a verified season for every Odisha district. [TNAU](https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/bio-fuels/Biofuel_Mahua.html).

## Culture and economics to deepen

Seek attributed harvesting and drying practices, preservation, songs, festivals and household histories by community and place. Compare flowers, seeds, oil and finished-product transactions using dated units, grades, procurement quantities and collector receipts. Odisha-wide turnover and export volumes remain unknown in this profile. [Dated history](../history/forest-livelihoods.md) keeps 2001 publication evidence separate from the age of a tradition.

[Forest foods](forest-foods.md) · [Markets and livelihoods](../economy/forest-products.md).

## Odisha food-processing research · 2016 issue

Bakhara, Bal, Pal, Sahoo and Panda reported surveying mahua post-harvest practices in Odisha and developing foods including candied and glazed flowers, a bar, drinks, squash, jam, laddu and cake. Their affiliations include OUAT's agricultural processing and food-engineering department. The paper appeared in *Agricultural Engineering Today*40(4), pp.22–28; the publisher dates its online release to24 February2017. [Publisher abstract](https://indianjournals.com/article/aet-40-4-004).

This supports a research-and-food-diversity story. It does not establish that these formulations are ancestral recipes, widely sold products or profitable businesses. The abstract supplies no usable recipe quantities or consumer-panel methods; those remain full-text questions. Connect [preparation and variation](preparation-and-variation.md) only when a complete attributed formulation is available.

## A documented sal-leaf cake and local harvest season

Behera and colleagues' 2016 paper reports 2009 fieldwork among Santhal residents around Chandbill, Bangiriposi, Mayurbhanj. Its collection account places the flower season in **March–April** and includes **private as well as forest land**. This is a local historical account, not a present statewide calendar.

Under “Cake” (printed p.98), it describes **250 g mahua flowers and 500 g rice**, separately soaked for **one hour**, then ground together. The paste is enclosed between sal leaves and fire-cooked. The paper mentions alternative starch ingredients but gives no cooking time or temperature. This is an attributed preparation description, not a kitchen-tested recipe; flower moisture state and practical cooking endpoints remain unclear. [Original paper](https://atr.vsu.edu.ph/article/download/212/202/390).

Its marketing discussion describes sales to local intermediaries under storage and cash constraints. It supplies no usable collector-price series here. Do not translate that qualitative account into present earnings or assume identical conditions across communities.

## Later university research

OUAT's 2020–21 report records development of a **10 kg-per-batch unit** for mahua candy and nectar/syrup, and a cookie experiment using mahua powder. These are research outputs, not verified commercial production or deployed businesses. [Annual report, printed p.23](https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/annual_report_2020-21_3.pdf).

The earlier Agricultural Engineering Today abstract and this field paper are different publications. Their food accounts must not be collapsed into one study or one recipe tradition.

[Related reading](poda-and-fire-cooking.md) — Connects one attributed leaf-and-fire preparation to the broader technique collection; does not establish a shared origin or universal method.

# Mohu: honey, collectors and processing

**Mohu (ମହୁ) means honey here.** The user explicitly confirmed that meaning on 1 October 2026. This records the intended name; it does not constitute a linguistic survey or identify the source of a particular honey.

Honey needs its own entry, distinct from [mahua/mohula](mahua-mohula.md). For each producer or lot, establish whether it is forest-collected, from managed hives, mixed, or unknown. Keep floral-origin labels as claims until supported by suitable traceability or analysis.

## What is already documented

The 2025 Odisha forestry report describes OFDC honey processing at Jashipur, Mayurbhanj. The [existing capacity observation](../statistics/forest-products.md) is reused: rated capacity is not actual output, and the report does not establish that all input honey is wild collected. Vasundhara lists honey among products in its producer-group livelihood work; this is the organisation's account, not measured statewide sales.

## Follow the value and the knowledge

Document named collectors or beekeepers, seasons and places, attributed collection history, aggregation, processing, testing, packaging and sales. Household uses and preparations require credited accounts. Beeswax should be a related non-food product record when Odisha-specific evidence is obtained, rather than being counted as honey.

The next market fields are dated collector prices, quantities purchased, processing throughput, quality tests, realised sales and Odisha-origin exports. Product listings and the presence of a processing plant cannot establish these outcomes. No current statewide honey market value or named producer certification has been verified here.

[Forest foods](forest-foods.md) · [Forest-product markets](../economy/forest-products.md).

## A historical, community-specific seasonal account

SCSTRTI's Hill Kharia account in the Similipal context describes honey collection and sale in **March–June** and **October–November** (printed p.28, PDF p.42). It records local distinctions rendered as bada/bhagua mahu and sana mahu; these are not verified bee-species identifications. [SCSTRTI report](https://repository.tribal.gov.in/bitstream/123456789/74427/1/SCST_2014_research_0338.pdf).

The file carries a2014 label, but exact publication and fieldwork dates remain unconfirmed. Preserve this as a historical account, not a current Odisha-wide availability calendar. Utkal has not interviewed collectors or verified present collection conditions.

body:
# Odisha Rasagola

**A sweet can carry a place’s memory.** Follow rasagola through Odisha’s ritual life, literary references and sweet-making communities.

## A homecoming in Puri

OSIC describes rasagola’s offering to Lakshmi on Jagannath’s behalf at Niladri Bije and cites the temple’s 1955 Record of Rights. The ritual belongs to devotional tradition; it is not a dated account of invention.[^rasagola-osic]

## A thread through Odia literature

The same publication identifies a rasagola reference in Balaram Das’s Dandi Ramayana. We have inspected OSIC’s account, not independently collated the original passage or dated its earliest manuscript witness.[^rasagola-osic]

## Meet the places that keep making it

A travelogue hosted by Odisha Tourism describes Pahala’s roadside sweet market between Bhubaneswar and Cuttack and mentions Salepur’s rasagola tradition. These are connections for future maker-led stories; the account concerns a 2019 visit, not verified present-day hours, prices or vendor quality.[^rasagola-market-travelogue]

Ask a maker what they learned, who taught them, and what they want the next generation to remember. Photograph the making with permission. Record their account as testimony, with their name and date, rather than treating one shop’s story as the history of every rasagola.

## A named Odisha identity

The GI Registry lists Odisha Rasagola under application 612, with a certificate dated 29 July 2019. Odisha’s named product and cultural connections deserve explicit recognition. Registration alone does not settle every competing account of the sweet’s first invention.[^gi-rasagola]

## The filed historical statement

The registry’s GI Journal 116, dated 27 March 2019, was retrieved and its page 10 visually inspected on 1 October 2026. It cites the temple Record of Rights, Part III, under the Law Department notification of 12 October 1955, and identifies the Ayodhya Kanda hospitality episode in Dandi Ramayana. This is the application’s statement of evidence, not an inspection of the original record or a critical literary edition. The journal is available through “612 - GI - Journal Copy - 27-03-2019” in the registry document list.[^gi-rasagola]

A separately sourced, author-released public-domain Pahala rasagola photograph now supports the website feature. Its image metadata is recorded in [the food collection](collection.json); a photograph does not establish an origin claim.

## Research still to do

Inspect the cited temple record and a critical edition of Dandi Ramayana; record editions, page references and dates. Add consented maker interviews from Pahala and Salepur, with properly licensed images. Keep ritual, documentary evidence and oral testimony distinct.

## Connections

[Mahaprasad](mahaprasad.md) · [Rasagola economics](../economy/rasagola-and-sweets.md) · [Research standards](../about/research-method.md)

[^gi-rasagola]: [Odisha Rasagola — GI application 612](https://search.ipindia.gov.in/GIRPublicSearch/Application/Details/612)
[^rasagola-osic]: [OSIC E-News, July 2019, pp. 3–4](https://admin.osicltd.in/Siteupdate/Event/AUG19.pdf)
[^rasagola-market-travelogue]: [A short trip to a Sweets Wonderland in Odisha](https://apps.odishatourism.gov.in/blog-detail/a-short-trip-to-a-sweets-wonderland-in-odisha)

## From milk to market

A 2023 original study links Niali’s chhena supply to Pahala’s sweet shops and describes markets within Odisha and in West Bengal. Its ten retailer interviews are a sample, not an enterprise census. The [economic record](../economy/rasagola-and-sweets.md) retains the study’s limits and arithmetic conflicts. [Original study, pp.2306–2308](https://ndpublisher.in/admin/issues/EAv68n5z11.pdf). No current sales or export total established.

## A cook’s two versions and a remembered meal · 1 October 2026

Sasmita identifies Odisha as her home state and documents two versions. Her 2017 sweet preparation uses boiled fruit, jaggery or sugar, seed tempering, ginger and coconut.[^food-ou-sasmita2017] Her 2019 version uses mustard–cumin paste and panch phoron with jaggery; it omits onion and garlic.[^food-ou-sasmita2019] These are two accounts from one author, not independent surveys or district recipes.

Julie Acharya Ray’s 2014 family memoir remembers ou khatta in her mother’s Kartik meal.[^food-ou-ray2014] This connects the dish to one household’s seasonal memory without claiming uniform observance across Odisha. Compare [Dalma](dalma.md). The attributed relish account offers rice and dalma as a serving combination; meal context, not universal ritual prescription.

The university’s Assam-labelled passage remains unresolved. These attributed Odisha accounts do not establish exclusive origin or make that other label an error. Recipe testing, local/Odia review, precise district distribution, current availability and economic totals remain unknown.


[^food-ou-sasmita2017]: [Meetha Oou Khatta | Sweet Elephant Apple Relish](https://www.firsttimercook.com/meetha-oou-khatta-sweet-elephant-apple-relish/) — Sasmita, First Timer Cook, 2017-12-10.

[^food-ou-sasmita2019]: [Khata Meetha Oou | Sweet & Sour Elephant Apple Relish](https://www.firsttimercook.com/khata-meetha-oou-sweet-sour-elephant-apple-relish/) — Sasmita, First Timer Cook, 2019-01-04.

[^food-ou-ray2014]: [The Month of Kartik in my Mother’s Kitchen](https://www.saveur.com/article/travels/kartik-holy-month/) — Julie Acharya Ray, Saveur, 2014-10-09.

# Pakhala

## Sourced knowledge

Pakhala brings rice and water to the centre of an Odia meal. Odisha Tourism describes a fermented version served with fried vegetables and fish, especially in summer. This account provides a starting point for understanding the dish; it is not a prescription for how every household prepares or serves it.[^food-tourism]

## Story opportunity

A table built around simplicity: photograph rice, accompaniments and the person serving it.

*Editorial proposal; audience response has not been measured.*

## Next research

Document fresh and fermented variants with cooks; identify every accompaniment.

## Connections

[Related knowledge](dalma.md) · [Research standards](../about/research-method.md)

[^food-tourism]: [The Taste of Odisha](https://apps.odishatourism.gov.in/the-taste-of-odisha)

## Preparation and variations · 1 October 2026

The overview describes rice fermented in water and served with accompaniments. [The Taste of Odisha](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/the-taste-of-odisha.html), Pakhala heading. Odisha Tourism institutional overview; no household or regional prevalence established.

The 2019 menu adds curd and a ginger–mustard tempering. [Chef TZac: Odia cuisine is an evolved cuisine](https://apps.odishatourism.gov.in/blog-detail/chef-tzac-odia-cuisine-is-an-evolved-cuisine), Odia Experience menu, third course. Mansita Mishra’s 27 November 2019 account of a chef and restaurant menu; contemporary interpretation, not a universal or current menu.

**Still to verify:** Research fresh versus fermented naming and regional versions; do not adopt the tourism page’s heat-stroke or nerve-vitamin claims. Odia and local review remain pending.

[Preparation collection](preparation-and-variation.md) — Compare techniques and attributed versions across the existing food entries.

[Poda and fire cooking](poda-and-fire-cooking.md) — Compare attributed food preparations and method boundaries; no common origin, culinary ranking or venue availability inferred.

[Odisha’s everyday food culture](everyday-food-culture.md) — badi chura, sukhua, palm-fruit pitha, rice-water preparations and the existing leaf-cooked mushroom entry.

## Rice preferences reported by farmers

A 2026 participatory study records Bahal, Bojni, Bhajna and Kalahans in relation to pakhala among its selected western Odisha participants. [Table6](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/sustainable-food-systems/articles/10.3389/fsufs.2026.1769950/full). These are attributed preferences, not a single compulsory rice variety or a statewide recipe rule. The [rice collection](rice-varieties.md) preserves the sample scope and unresolved seed identities.

# Pitha: a collection, not one dish

Odisha’s pitha repertoire includes pan-cooked, boiled, baked and fried preparations.[^food-tourism]

For the website, make this a browsable collection. Begin with [chakuli](chakuli.md), [poda](poda-pitha.md), [enduri](enduri-pitha.md), [sijha manda](manda-pitha.md), [kakara](kakara-pitha.md) and [arisa](arisa-pitha.md). These are examples, not an inventory of all Odia pitha.

## Editorial proposal

“How many ways can a home say welcome?” is a stronger opening than a large unverified dish count. Each page should show a whole serving, a texture close-up and the maker’s hands. Let the cook identify the occasion, ingredients and variation. A six-part series can introduce one preparation at a time and end with a tasting spread.

## Recipe research template

Capture local name and approved spelling; place; contributor credit and consent; ingredient quantities; preparation method; household variation; occasion; serving context; photography rights; and dietary/allergen information verified from that recipe. Do not infer that every version of a dish has the same ingredients.

No complete recipe has yet been established in this KB.

# Odisha’s poda and fire-cooking traditions

**Odisha’s Best-Kept Secret — The Art of Cooking with Fire** is the user-selected campaign wording. The evidence supports a varied poda repertoire; it does not establish an official title, national ranking, exclusive origin or one cooking technique. “Best-kept secret” is a creative tag, not a measured awareness finding.

## A menu connected by heat

This selection brings together nine food identities, not a statewide count. Ingredients cross vegetables, mushrooms, fish, prawns, chicken, meat, rice and cheese. Evidence ranges from contributors’ recipes to institutional descriptions and historical menu specifications.

| Food | Method in the cited account | Source scope |
|---|---|---|
| [Baigana poda](baigana-poda.md) | direct roasting | Contributor recipe; pakhala accompaniment. |
| [Tomato / bilati baigana poda](tomato-poda.md) | direct roasting | Contributor recipe; no district attribution. |
| [Chatu patrapoda](chatu-patrapoda.md) | leaf parcel | Contributor home version; distinct from the saved 2019 restaurant account. |
| [Machha patrapoda](machha-patrapoda.md) | leaf parcel | Contributor home version; not evidence of a unique Odisha invention. |
| [Chingudi patrapoda](chingudi-patrapoda.md) | leaf parcel | Historical restaurant interpretation reported by Mansita Mishra. |
| [Kukuda patrapoda](kukuda-patrapoda.md) | leaf parcel | Proposed/specification menu, not proof of current restaurant availability. |
| [Baunsa poda mansa](baunsa-poda-mansa.md) | bamboo cooking | Attributed reporting; detailed Araku recipe is not transferred to Odisha. |
| [Poda pitha](poda-pitha.md) | slow baking | Reuse of saved attributed regional accounts; versions are not universal rules. |
| [Chhena poda](chhena-poda.md) | slow baking | Reuse of institutional overview; modern oven versions need no direct flame. |

## What the connection means

Direct roasting exposes vegetables to heat before peeling/mashing. Leaf parcels enclose food and can combine surface charring with moisture retained inside. Bamboo is a cooking vessel in the meat account. Baking gives rice cakes and cheese sweets another route to a browned surface. These are related for this editorial collection; they are not interchangeable definitions of barbecue.

[Pakhala](pakhala.md) supplies an everyday meal connection through Sasmita’s baigana recipe. [Poda pitha](poda-pitha.md) supplies festival context through the saved Raja account. [Chhena poda](chhena-poda.md) lets the story finish with a sweet. This is an editorial tasting sequence, not a documented traditional set meal or bookable tour.

[Enduri pitha](enduri-pitha.md) is a useful boundary: it is leaf-wrapped and steamed. Leaves alone do not make a dish barbecue. Lopa’s account also describes a modern enclosed daba-poda adaptation; the name alone does not prove charring. The food traditions shared with neighbouring regions must retain their own credits; resemblance does not establish migration or historical influence.

## Evidence limits and next work

- Obtain named Odisha community and cook accounts for bamboo-cooked meat and chicken parcels; broad “tribal” attribution is insufficient for an origin claim.
- Deepen sukhua poda, alu poda, bhendi/janhi/potala poda and leaf choice only after source verification. These are leads, not confirmed additions to the nine-entry selection.
- Keep the Nimantran procurement menu separate from operating/serving evidence. Its steamed chhena-poda description conflicts with the baking account, and is held unresolved.
- The CCRT-hosted folklore PDF failed direct retrieval and a 50-second network retry. Indexed bamboo references are discovery leads only; retry 8 October 2026 if needed.
- Recipe quantities, smoke chemistry, nutritional benefits, origin dates, comparative state rankings and economic impact are not established here. No new revenue, export or popularity numbers.

[Structured evidence](../references/data/poda-traditions.json) · [Story and video draft](../stories/odisha-poda-country.md) · [Preparation collection](preparation-and-variation.md).

## Website candidate · 1 October 2026

The [fire-cooking collection](fire-cooking-stories.json) selects vegetable roasting and mushroom, fish and prawn leaf-parcel accounts for the first illustrated website batch, connected to existing baked-food stories. [Page data](collection.json) retains named sources and accurate photo captions. The wider nine-entry research scope remains separate; unresolved chicken and bamboo accounts are not promoted into verified visit or menu suggestions.

[Mahua and rice cooked between sal leaves](mahua-mohula.md) offers a source-attributed connection to fire cooking. The paper calls it cake; no unsupported local name, national uniqueness or universal cooking method is inferred.

## Sourced knowledge

A slow-baked rice-batter pitha associated with Raja.[^food-tourism]

## Story opportunity

Make patience the story: preparation, waiting, cutting and sharing.

*Editorial proposal; audience response has not been measured.*

Record a household’s Raja practice and its recipe; dates vary each year.

## Connections

[Related knowledge](pitha.md) · [Research standards](../about/research-method.md)

[^food-tourism]: [The Taste of Odisha](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/the-taste-of-odisha.html)

## Preparation and variations · 1 October 2026

Fermented rice batter is cooked slowly with sal leaves in an earthen pot; Raja is the festival association. [The Taste of Odisha](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/the-taste-of-odisha.html), Poda Pitha heading. Odisha Tourism institutional overview; no household or regional prevalence established.

**Still to verify:** Document a second attributed preparation and its location; do not infer a standard oven temperature. Odia and local review remain pending.

[Preparation collection](preparation-and-variation.md) — Compare techniques and attributed versions across the existing food entries.

## Primary-source follow-up · 1 October 2026

Named entries distinguish milk-based khira poda, rice-flour/jaggery poda and sweetened rice–black-gram biri chaula poda. [Traditional Rice Foods: The Rich Heritage of India — Lipi Das](https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/final_book_ldas.pdf), Printed pp.23,26,29 / PDF pp.34,37,40. Lipi Das, ICAR-CRRI, 2015 compilation; an Odisha-labelled version, not a tested recipe or district prevalence measure.

Sujata Dehury describes coastal rice-flour/jaggery dough in banana leaves; Sweta Biswal describes lightly seasoned western rice–black-gram batter in sal-leaf parcels. [In Odisha, ‘podo pitha’ is a sentiment — regional accounts](https://www.livemint.com/mint-lounge/food/odisha-podo-pitha-burnt-cake-111686847809768.html), Coastal and western Odisha paragraphs, 16 June 2023. Accounts reported by Priyadarshini Chatterjee; regional descriptions are attributed, not universal rules or surveyed distribution.

**Remaining question:** Regional accounts are now attributed; confirm finer locality and household differences without equating every rice–black-gram version with western Odisha. Local/Odia review remains pending.

## Poda story connection · 1 October 2026

Coastal and western accounts distinguish banana-leaf rice-flour/jaggery dough from sal-leaf rice–black-gram parcels. [In Odisha, ‘podo pitha’ is a sentiment — regional accounts](https://www.livemint.com/mint-lounge/food/odisha-podo-pitha-burnt-cake-111686847809768.html), Sujata Dehury and Sweta Biswal regional accounts.

Reuse of saved attributed regional accounts; versions are not universal rules.

**To establish:** Local variants remain open; CRRI book versions already captured separately.

[Odisha’s poda and fire-cooking traditions](poda-and-fire-cooking.md) connects this account to other ingredients and cooking methods.

# How Odisha cooks: preparations and variations

Fourteen entries now connect names to preparation accounts: six pitha, four everyday dishes and four place-linked sweets. These are the bounds of this research batch, not a count of Odisha’s foods. Explore the linked entries for ingredients, sources and differences; their versions are attributed rather than prescribed as one authentic recipe.

## Pitha: follow the cooking method

- [Chakuli pitha](chakuli.md) — pan cooking, fermentation.
- [Poda pitha](poda-pitha.md) — slow cooking, leaf assisted cooking.
- [Enduri pitha](enduri-pitha.md) — steaming, leaf wrapping.
- [Sijha manda pitha](manda-pitha.md) — boiling, steaming, filled dumpling.
- [Kakara pitha](kakara-pitha.md) — frying, filled dough.
- [Arisa pitha](arisa-pitha.md) — frying.

## Everyday dishes and sweets

- [Pakhala](pakhala.md) — soaking, fermentation.
- [Dalma](dalma.md) — boiling, tempering.
- [Chatu patrapoda](chatu-patrapoda.md) — leaf wrapping, fire cooking.
- [Ou khatta](ou-khatta.md) — boiling, tempering and simmering.
- [Chhena poda](chhena-poda.md) — baking, leaf assisted cooking.
- [Chhena jhili](chhena-jhili.md) — frying, syrup soaking.
- [Kendrapara Rasabali](kendrapara-rasabali.md) — frying, milk soaking.
- [Dhenkanal Magji](dhenkanal-magji.md) — pressing, pan cooking, hand shaping.

## What still needs a cook’s voice

Regional distribution, household measurements, preferred Odia names and demonstrated variations remain open. A contributor recipe hosted by a government portal retains its author’s scope. A restaurant interpretation does not establish temple practice. No field interview, recipe test or human language review has been invented.

Magji’s original specification is now available, but its internal sugar proportions differ. Enduri’s new steaming detail remains indexed-only because the hospitality PDF could not be retrieved. The collection retains those limits rather than silently turning them into recipe instructions.

[Structured preparation register](../references/data/food-preparations.json) keeps each account, locator, scope and unresolved question together. [Rasagola and sweets economics](../economy/rasagola-and-sweets.md) owns the separate sales/export questions. No commercial totals, health claims or serving venues were added here.

## Follow-up: original records and regional voices · 1 October 2026

Seven of the existing entries now have additional evidence. The [2015 rice-food book](../sources/food-crri-rice2015.md) supplies full preparation passages for six pitha, including Enduri; its new capture resolves the earlier reliance on an indexed-only steaming description without claiming that the unavailable NCHM PDF was recovered. [Poda pitha](poda-pitha.md) now separates named book versions and attributed coastal/western accounts.

[Rasabali](kendrapara-rasabali.md) now preserves both the original GI specification and September correction. Conflicting curdling instructions remain visible. Undated seller/maker claims are held as economics leads, with no sales or exports inferred. Earlier checkpoints above describe the evidence available at that time.

Next: independent local preparations for chatu patrapoda and ou khatta; finer regional attribution where supported. Recipe testing and local/Odia review remain pending.

## Poda story extension · 1 October 2026

[Poda and fire cooking](poda-and-fire-cooking.md) connects existing pitha, cheese and mushroom entries with six new scoped food nuclei. Chatu now has Lopa’s own home preparation alongside the chef-menu account; locality review remains open. Ou khatta remains the next distinct preparation gap.

## Fourteen-food research set complete · 1 October 2026

[Ou khatta](ou-khatta.md) now distinguishes two preparations by Sasmita and a family meal memory by Julie Acharya Ray. This closes the last attributed-preparation gap in the bounded RES-011 set of six pitha, four everyday dishes and four place-linked sweets. It does not complete statewide coverage, recipe testing, local language review or the resolution of every source conflict. Further poda and locality questions remain in the existing records. Next sequential task: sweets economics (RES-031).

## Mahua food-development reference

[Mahua/mohula](mahua-mohula.md) now links to a2016-issue Odisha study reporting laddu, cake, jam and other formulations. Only the abstract was read; ingredient quantities and procedures remain unavailable here. Do not turn a product list into an invented recipe or describe research formulations as established community traditions.

## Mahua preparation account recovered

The [mahua profile](mahua-mohula.md) now records a separate field-study cake description, its source quantities and missing cooking endpoints. This adds an attributed preparation account; it does not fill the unread methods of the earlier food-development paper. The original fourteen-food research set remains preserved.

## Tentuli and chara preparation leads

The [tentuli](tentuli-tamarind.md) and [chara](chara-chironji.md) profiles now hold attributed ingredient-use descriptions. These are not complete recipes. Tamarind-seed gruel tables need local review and clarified cooking endpoints; chara roasting needs a named local account and quantities.

## Palm stages and preparation

[Talagaja](talagaja.md) adds a brief field-study use description. The original article separates germinated seed, young-fruit endosperm and ripe-fruit pitha; this is useful ingredient classification, not a tested recipe or verified name equivalence.

## Germinated palm interior

The [Talagaja entry](talagaja.md) distinguishes reported fresh consumption from experimental drying/milling. Laboratory powder results and sprout/tuber recipes cannot be transferred to the fresh seed interior without evidence. Full local recipe and storage validation remain open.

body:
# Odisha’s rice: varieties, seed keepers and food

Rice connects Odisha’s farms, kitchens, plant science and trade. This collection begins with **21 named entries**, not a count of all varieties grown in the state. The [structured register](../references/data/rice-economy.json) records whether evidence concerns cultivation, conservation or release.

## Heritage kept alive by farmers

MSSRF describes **Tulasa Ghiuria of Nuaguda, Kundura, Koraput**, conserving more than 70 indigenous rice seeds. It names Kalajeera, Dangarbasumti, Machakanta, Tikkichudi, Haldichudi and Muktabali. Its account specifically mentions cultivating the first three; the page credits original publication to 26 July 2022 and cannot establish 2026 acreage. [Institutional profile](https://www.mssrf.org/our-stories/more-than-70-landraces-of-paddy-varieties-have-been-conserved-by-tulasa).

Reuse the existing [Koraput Kalajeera profile](koraput-kalajeera-rice.md) for the saved GI record. Similar names alone do not prove a seed lot’s identity, geographical certification or entitlement to use a GI.

## Rice for different fields

NRRI’s release list connects these varieties with Odisha:

| Growing environment in the source | Examples |
|---|---|
| Irrigated | Naveen, Tapaswini, Geetanjali; hybrids Ajay and Rajalaxmi |
| Shallow lowlands | Pooja, Savitri/Ponmani, Samalei |
| Medium-deep water | Utkalprabha |
| Coastal saline | Lunishree |
| Flood-prone lowlands | Swarna Sub1 |
| Rainfed uplands | Sahbhagidhan |

[NRRI list](https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/). These are release/ecology records. District planting, present seed supply, market share and realised farm yields require separate evidence. This is not a current planting recommendation.

## A heritage variety and its improved selection are different entries

NRRI identifies **Nua Kalajeera, Nua Dhusara and Nua Chinikamini** as pureline selections from Kalajeera, Dhusara and Chinikamini respectively. The parent landrace and selected variety must retain separate identities. [Research Bulletin 39, printed p.4](https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/NRRI-Research-Bulletin-39.pdf).

The same bulletin separates Geetanjali’s 2005 release from its 2006 notification; the HTML list labels 2006 as release. Both statements are retained in the register, with a notification check still open. No single harmonised date is asserted.

## From seed to plate

Follow existing food and preparation records before creating new dishes. Rice variety, grain colour, polishing, parboiling and food preparation are separate dimensions. Selected source-attributed food-use links are added below. Local spellings, accession identities and preparation accounts from named cooks remain open. An aromatic label alone does not establish suitability for every pitha, pakhala or puffed-rice product.

[Seed deployment and women farmers](../works/odisha-rice-seed-deployment.md) connects this collection to existing plant-science research. [Rice economics](../economy/rice-economy.md) follows production, procurement and the evidence needed for farmer returns.

[Related economics](../economy/rice-economy.md) — Connects variety identity and seed keeping to economic measures without assuming a price premium or causal income gain.

## A farmer, a place and a dated cultivation account

Tulasa Ghiuria's account reports **one acre of Kalajeera, two of Dangarbasumati and two of Machhakanta** at Nuaguda in Kundura, Koraput. The original article is credited to **26 July 2022**; the cropping season is unstated. These are personal cultivation areas, not district acreage or current supply. Spelling variants remain attached to the source. [MSSRF account](https://www.mssrf.org/our-stories/more-than-70-landraces-of-paddy-varieties-have-been-conserved-by-tulasa).

## What farmers keep rice for

The following are farmers' reported preferences in a study published **19 February 2026**. They are food-use leads, not tested recipes or verified genetic identities.

| Reported rice name | Reported food use | Study scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bahal, Bojni, Bhajna | Pakhala | Selected western Odisha villages |
| Kalahans | Kanika and pakhala | Selected western Odisha villages |
| Machhakanta | Rice pudding | Selected western Odisha villages |
| Umuriachundi | Popped rice; Chaitaparab ritual use | Koraput sample |
| Sapuri | Popped rice at weddings | Koraput sample |
| Para dhan, Mati Dhan | Rice flakes | Koraput sample |

[Yadav and colleagues, Tables6–7](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/sustainable-food-systems/articles/10.3389/fsufs.2026.1769950/full). Western sites cover Bargarh, Sundargarh and Jharsuguda; the tables do not allocate every rice name to a particular village. Fieldwork dates remain unverified. The paper's health claims are excluded. A name appearing in both this study and the existing register does not prove seed-lot equivalence.

## Women producing seed in Kalahandi

IRRI's 2020 account reports around **180 women producing about 350 tons of paddy seed (source wording) in 2019** through Adarsh Dharmagarh Women Farmers Services Producer Company. **Pooja foundation seed** was among the supplied varieties. The report separates kharif and rabi production areas; it does not split output by variety. [IRRI](https://news.irri.org/2020/05/women-farmers-take-significant-step.html).

This documents a seed enterprise, with no assumption about current sales or farmer profit. It complements landrace conservation and the existing [seed-deployment record](../works/odisha-rice-seed-deployment.md).

# Sukhua

Sukhua belongs in the encyclopedia as a dried-fish family with named preparations. Tanuja Tripathy’s Kokali Sukhua Rai combines dried fish with mustard and garlic paste, onion, tomato and mustard oil. [Traditional Odia Recipe - Kokali Sukhua Rai](https://odiarecipes.com/details.php?htid=76). The vernacular fish name is retained; a biological species has not been confirmed.

The food also connects to work. WorldFish’s 8 October 2025 Dalimbapur case credits Premalata Behera and the Maa women’s group, describing solar drying and training in processing, packaging, labelling and pricing. [From Traditions to Triumph: Premalata’s Success with Solar-Dried Fish in Odisha](https://worldfishcenter.org/impact-story/traditions-triumph-premalatas-success-solar-dried-fish-odisha). This is a project case, not a statewide industry total.

## Next evidence

Verify local fish names and species, coastal/inland variations, producer groups, dated prices and actual shipments. Recipes and online listings do not establish exports.

[Everyday food culture](everyday-food-culture.md) connects this entry to ingredients, meal relationships and makers.

body:
# Tala pitha

The Gapu Photography account credits Manaswini Sahoo / Soul Of Odisha with a tala poda pitha made from ripe palm fruit and places it in a monsoon setting. [Sugar Palm Rice Cake - ତାଳ ପୋଡ଼ପିଠା](https://www.gapuphotography.com/2018/06/Tala-Pitha.html). This is one credited example within the broader tala-pitha name; it does not establish that every version uses the same cooking method.

Ripe fruit pulp and palm-seed foods require separate records. The user identified tala khaja as seed produce; its exact seed stage and equivalence to other local names remain open in the collection.

## Next evidence

Obtain directly documented recipes, grain/fibre ingredients, local names and season windows. Embedded video was not inspected.

[Everyday food culture](everyday-food-culture.md) connects this entry to ingredients, meal relationships and makers.

## Ripe-fruit and rice-flour evidence

[Panda and colleagues, printed p.67](https://reference-global.com/download/article/10.2478/arls-2021-0031.pdf) document ripe palm-fruit material mixed with rice flour for pitha in their 2015–2018 study. This extends the ingredient evidence but supplies no measured recipe. [Talagaja](talagaja.md) is the separate germinated-seed food in that account; the user’s tala khaja name remains unresolved.
