# Odisha’s people and creations

Explore people through what they made, discovered or achieved. Record statewide, national and international significance through specific evidence—an award, performance, competition result, publication or institutional contribution—rather than a single subjective fame score.

## First source-backed entries

- [Gopinath Mohanty](gopinath-mohanty.md) — Jnanpith laureate
- [Satchidananda Rautroy](satchidananda-rautroy.md) — Jnanpith laureate
- [Sitakant Mahapatra](sitakant-mahapatra.md) — Jnanpith laureate
- [Pratibha Ray](pratibha-ray.md) — Jnanpith laureate
- [Fakir Mohan Senapati](fakir-mohan-senapati.md) — English edition with University of California Press; not sales or readership measurement
- [Prafulla Kar](prafulla-kar.md) — 2015 Sangeet Natak Akademi award citation, Sugam Sangeet
- [Dilip Tirkey](dilip-tirkey.md) — India representation and three Olympic appearances recorded by Hockey India
- [Bedangadas Mohanty](bedangadas-mohanty.md) — Infosys Prize in Physical Sciences 2021
- [Sudarsan Pattnaik](sudarsan-pattnaik.md) — Named installation at the 55th IFFI in Goa, 2024

## Read, hear and examine their work

The [works catalogue](../works/index.md) connects authors with books and English editions, a composer with film music, an artist with an installation, and a scientist with a paper. Author, translator, editor, composer, lyricist, performer, team contributor and maker are separate credits.

The initial records establish selected facts, not finished biographies or an exhaustive canon. International publication or archival inclusion proves a route of circulation, not global popularity. Odisha association may mean language, birthplace, education, residence or work; each must be stated explicitly rather than inferred from a surname.

## Broaden whose work is represented

Research candidates include Sarala Das, Balaram Das, Gangadhar Meher, Radhanath Ray, Jayanta Mahapatra, Manoj Das, Ramakanta Rath and contemporary writers; Bhima Bhoi and oral-literature traditions; Sanjukta Panigrahi, Kelucharan Mohapatra, Akshaya Mohanty, Sikandar Alam and Sunanda Patnaik; Dutee Chand, Srabani Nanda, Pramod Bhagat, Rachita Mistry, Padmini Rout, Debashish Das, and Odisha hockey players; Pathani Samanta, Prana Krushna Parija, Subrat Kumar Acharya and other scientists. These are discovery candidates, not established profiles or endorsements.

Prioritise women, disabled achievers, tribal and minority communities, less-covered districts, regional languages and diaspora connections. Omit uncertain candidates when identity or Odisha association cannot be established. Living-person profiles should focus on public professional work and retain relevant record changes; never collect private contact details.

## Connected production stories

[Sand art](../culture/sand-art.md), [Cuttack Tarakasi](../culture/cuttack-tarakasi.md), [garments and markets](../handlooms/garments-and-markets.md) and [rasagola economics](../economy/rasagola-and-sweets.md) connect creativity with craft communities, materials and measurable economic activity. No livelihood benefit is inferred from fame alone.

## Other Odisha subjects to add

Cinema and theatre; Odia-language printing and journalism; manuscripts and libraries; instruments and instrument makers; community oral histories; architecture and public art; boats and maritime skills; sports coaching and academies; scientific institutions and inventions; rice, spices, coffee and processed foods; biodiversity knowledge and conservation practitioners. Start each with named people, places and works, then add comparable quantities where evidence exists.

[Research queue](../methods/research-pipeline.md) · [People and works register](../references/data/people-creations.json).

[Sand art](../culture/sand-art.md) — Read an art form with its named practitioners and dated works; shared subject matter alone does not establish influence.

[Women writers and English reading](../works/spark-of-light.md) connects five selected stories with authors and edition-specific translators. Four new profiles cover Reba Ray, Suprabha Kar, Basanta Kumari Patnaik and Binapani Mohanty; Pratibha Ray’s profile is expanded.

## Biography continuation · 1 October 2026

Existing [Fakir Mohan Senapati](fakir-mohan-senapati.md), [Gopinath Mohanty](gopinath-mohanty.md) and [Sitakant Mahapatra](sitakant-mahapatra.md) entries now connect life, places, selected work and reading routes. Together with the earlier women-writer batch, eight profiles have been deepened; this is a project coverage count, not eight complete biographies or a canon of Odisha literature.

## Performing-arts checkpoint · 1 October 2026

Four profiles and four credited theatre episodes connect the Mohapatras and Panigrahis with dance, stage work and music. Institutional recognition and archival presence are retained with their source limits. The programme still needs broader practitioner coverage, twelve credited works/performances and lawful listening/viewing routes; this batch is not its completion.

## Music listening checkpoint · 1 October 2026

Added Sunanda Patnaik, expanded Prafulla Kar and attached seven recording-specific records. Label and distribution routes identify where readers can seek the music; no audio was downloaded or playback verified. The 2012 OSA report gives a concrete diaspora link for both artists. Film, upload, compilation and recording dates remain distinct. Six selected practitioners and twelve performing-arts work records now exist, but the count includes a soundtrack container and does not establish twelve independent recordings; RES-027 remains in progress.

## Performing-arts milestone · 1 October 2026

The bounded RES-027 set now covers **six practitioners and twelve independently scoped works or performances**: four documented stage episodes and eight catalogue recordings. The Mamata soundtrack container is excluded from this count. Two label videos passed a muted-player progression check in the current session. Historical stage records do not thereby acquire surviving video; remaining listening routes, original recording dates, identifiers, biography conflicts and media permissions retain their stated unknowns. This completes the first research set, not an exhaustive discography or editorial approval.

## Sporting achievements · 1 October 2026

[Eight athlete profiles across four sports](../people/sporting-achievements.md) connect official results with dated Odisha affiliations. Team medals, individual results, career caps, heat positions and chess scores retain their separate meanings. This research collection is not a statewide medal total.

## Science connections · 1 October 2026

[Science and documented contributions](../people/science-and-contributions.md) connects rice seed systems and public-health research with named contributors and credited teams. A contribution record, a patient sample and statewide economic or health outcomes have different scopes.

## Scientific heritage through time · 1 October 2026

[Utkal’s scientific heritage to the present](../people/science-and-contributions.md) now connects medieval astronomy, Parija’s botany and contemporary research. Named contributions and collective technical traditions have separate evidence requirements; earlier periods remain explicit research gaps.

## Mathematics and Odia science writing · 1 October 2026

[Tribikram Pati](../people/tribikram-pati.md) and [Gokulananda Mohapatra](../people/gokulananda-mohapatra.md) connect mathematical research, science education and Odia writing to credited works. Source conflicts remain visible; neither a journal venue nor an encyclopaedia establishes measured global popularity.

## Contemporary creative lives · 1 October 2026

[Contemporary creators](../people/contemporary-creators.md) connects Bibhu Mohapatra, Jatin Das, Jagannath Panda and Subroto Bagchi to five credited creations. Existing Pratibha Ray and Sudarsan Pattnaik profiles are reused. Dated recognition, artistic circulation and economic outcomes remain distinct.

## Women across creative fields · 1 October2026

The [contemporary creators collection](../people/contemporary-creators.md) now includes Nandita Das, Susmita Bagchi, Sona Mohapatra and Sujata Mohapatra. Five linked records distinguish films, a translated novel, a song recording and a performance occurrence. Existing Jatin Das, Pratibha Ray and Kelucharan Mohapatra pages are reused for related reading.

[Entrepreneurs and business leaders](../people/entrepreneurs-and-business-leaders.md) — selected people, companies, Odisha connections and documented professional recognition. Existing profiles and statewide statistics are reused.

[Public servants and lawmakers](../people/public-servants-and-lawmakers.md) — five selected lives connect Odisha with Constitution-making, Parliament, national administration and constitutional office. Roles, periods and institutional evidence remain separate.

[Utkal’s rulers and royal legacies](../people/rulers-and-royal-legacies.md) — five selected rulers linked to inscriptions, government centres and architectural patronage; political power, contribution and later remembrance remain distinct.

[Lalit Mohan Patnaik](../people/lalit-mohan-patnaik.md) connects Odisha education and institutional collaboration with computing research and a jointly credited publication. Dated recognition, author bibliography and original-paper review remain separate evidence steps.

[Sanghamitra Mohanty](../people/sanghamitra-mohanty.md) and [Susmita Mohanty](../people/susmita-mohanty.md) extend the science collection into computing and space design/policy. Follow their credited-work pages for original publisher records and research limits.

[Pala and its culture](../culture/pala.md) — performed poetry, credited artists, archive routes and dated gatherings.

[Dance, learning and religious traditions](../methods/culture-learning-programme.md) — seven connected research tasks, existing-record reuse and a source-backed first checkpoint.

## Mahima Dharma and a credited reading route

[Stuti Chintamani](../works/stuti-chintamani.md) now records named English editions and translators. [Mahima Dharma](../culture/mahima-dharma.md) connects them to Joranda, Khaliapali and attributed historical scholarship while reusing the existing Bhima Bhoi literary profile.

## Weaving lives: evidence before biographies

[Handloom maker credits](../handlooms/garments-and-markets.md) now preserve four named awardee connections. These are scoped credits, with no invented life histories or current business claims.

## Textile creators: stronger work-level credits

[Handloom research](../handlooms/garments-and-markets.md) now connects Swarnalata Meher, Debaki Meher and Sarat Kumar Patra with three illustrated directory examples. Existing identities and shared records are reused; these are not newly invented biographies or interviews.

# Prafulla Kar

The 2015 Akademi citation describes a vocalist, composer and lyricist whose music-direction work included **more than 70 Odia films**. Mamata (1975) is one credited film. This is an attributed citation-vintage count, with the full PDF fetch unavailable; a complete discography and rights-cleared listening links are still needed.

This is a sourced research nucleus. A fuller biography, Odia spelling review, credited portrait and work-by-work bibliography remain pending.

[Mamata — film music](../works/mamata-film-music.md) — Read a documented work alongside the person’s profile; this is a selected example, not a complete bibliography.

## From film score to individual songs

Kapilas Bhuyan’s [2010 feature hosted by PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=67399) dates Kar’s debut as a film music director to **Mamata (1975)**. The feature carries an author-views disclaimer. The OSA’s own 2012 report records a lifetime achievement award for his contribution across singing, direction, composition and lyrics.

These broad career roles must be checked again at song level. The selected records below separate Kar’s music direction from the voices and lyricists named by the label. A catalogue is a route into his work, not a complete discography or a sales measure.

**Unresolved date:** the indexed Akademi citation gives 10 November 1939, while Saregama’s artist biography gives 2 February 1939. The exact birth date remains withheld pending stronger evidence.

# Public servants and lawmakers

Odisha’s national public-life connections include Constitution-making, elected representation, public audit and administration. This first selection records specific roles and contributions; it is not a party-based selection or a ranking of political merit.

| Person | Read about | Odisha connection |
|---|---|---|
| [Biswanath Das](biswanath-das.md) | Constituent Assembly debate on provincial finances | Ganjam public life and Orissa representation |
| [Harekrushna Mahtab](harekrushna-mahtab.md) | Union government, Parliament and translated essays | Odisha origin and public life |
| [Droupadi Murmu](droupadi-murmu.md) | State legislative service to the Presidency | Uparbeda and Rairangpur |

Civil servants, elected lawmakers, ministers and constitutional office-holders are separate categories. Holding an office does not prove authorship of a law, and a recorded speech does not establish that its proposal was adopted. The [structured public-service register](../references/data/public-service.json) preserves periods, roles and source issues.

[Public finance audit](../statistics/public-finance-audit.md) provides context for audit institutions without assigning their findings to one individual. [Gaon Majlis in English](../works/gaon-majlis-english.md) connects public life with credited literary work.

Further profiles should add original bills, debate passages, committee reports, policy publications and documented recognition. Shaktikanta Das and Nandini Satpathy are research candidates; they are not yet included in this five-person collection. Original source access, edition details and unresolved chronology remain explicit.

body:
# Utkal’s rulers and royal legacies

Utkal’s royal history can be explored through surviving places, inscriptions and institutions. Start with five rulers whose documented legacies connect ancient Kalinga, the Eastern Gangas and the Suryavamsi Gajapatis.

| Ruler | Historical setting | Why include them? | Evidence route |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Kharavela](kharavela.md) | Ancient Kalinga; exact chronology disputed | Royal record of campaigns, welfare and Jain connections | Hathigumpha inscription and cave heritage |
| [Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva](anantavarman-chodaganga.md) | Eastern Ganga; twelfth-century temple association | Major royal patronage at Puri | Government attribution of Jagannath Temple |
| [Anangabhima Deva III](anangabhima-deva-iii.md) | Eastern Ganga; early thirteenth century | Cuttack as a centre of government | Historical discussion of Nagari plates and charters |
| [Narasimha Deva I](narasimha-deva-i.md) | Eastern Ganga; 1238–1264 in UNESCO account | Konark and its architectural legacy | UNESCO’s site history |
| [Kapilendra Deva](kapilendra-deva.md) | Suryavamsi Gajapati; fifteenth century | An inscriptional presence beyond today’s Odisha | Srisailam record dated 1460 by its editor |

**Power, contribution and remembrance are three different questions.** Inscriptions can reveal campaigns and royal claims; buildings and grants can document patronage; later traditions can show how a ruler was remembered. None of these alone measures popularity among all subjects.

[Konark Sun Temple](../places/konark.md) connects royal-period history with a surviving World Heritage monument. [Jagannath Temple, Puri](../places/jagannath-temple-puri.md) connects patronage with an existing religious-place record. These reuse the encyclopedia’s place pages rather than creating duplicate monuments.

Ancient Kalinga and historical Utkal had changing meanings and boundaries. This collection is not a claim that all these kingdoms had the borders of modern Odisha. No empire-area, revenue or trade-volume estimate has been created from royal titles.

The [structured ruler register](../references/data/rulers-and-dynasties.json) preserves evidence classes, date scope and unresolved issues. Next additions can cover Purushottama, Prataparudra, the Bhaumakara queens and the modern regional rulers associated with education and Odisha’s formation; each needs its own identity and evidence check.

Editorial opportunity: a connected “ruler → inscription or institution → place today” reading journey. It can make the history vivid without turning a legend into a dated event or assigning the work of many makers solely to their royal patron.

# Sanghamitra Mohanty

**Odia is also a language of computing research.** Sanghamitra Mohanty and Basanta Kumar Swain jointly authored a [2012 speech-processing chapter](../works/odia-speech-wiener-filter-2012.md). Its publisher lists her chapter affiliation as Utkal University, Bhubaneswar. She also coedited [Speech, Sound and Music Processing](../works/speech-sound-music-2012.md), whose editor affiliation names North Orissa University, Baripada. These are publication-era affiliations, not current employment claims. Both publisher records establish Odisha institutional connections without inferring birthplace or ethnicity.

This computing researcher is distinct from [Sanghamitra Pati](sanghamitra-pati.md), the public-health researcher. Career dates, award totals and claims of first invention await stronger biographical evidence. [Science and contributions](science-and-contributions.md) provides the wider timeline.

body:
# Sanghamitra Pati

**Public-health research with an Odisha base.** Sanghamitra Pati is first-listed author of a 2015 study of multiple chronic conditions among adult primary-care patients in Odisha, with four credited coauthors. [The paper](../works/odisha-multimorbidity-2015.md) records the patient-sample scope and access limitations.

Her RMRC biography lists the 2018 Samanta Chandra Sekhar Award in Life Sciences from Odisha Bigyan Academy; the issuing academy’s register remains to be checked. ICMR’s leadership directory, checked on 1 October 2026, lists her as Additional Director General and Director-in-charge (additional charge), NIHR Bhubaneswar. body:
# Utkal’s scientific heritage to the present

Explore people, ideas, instruments and institutions across time. The historical record needs both named contributors and collective knowledge traditions. Ancient Utkal, Kalinga and present-day Odisha are not interchangeable geographic boundaries; every profile must explain its connection.

| Period or milestone | Person | Contribution to explore |
|---|---|---|
| Before 1099 CE | Evidence gap in this batch | Manuscripts, navigation, medicine, materials and engineering need separate attribution research. |
| 1099 CE | [Śatānanda](satananda.md) | *Bhāsvatī*: calendar and astronomical computation. |
| Nineteenth century | Samanta Chandrasekhar / Pathani Samanta | *Siddhanta Darpana* and observational instruments; reuse the project’s canonical entry. |
| 1928 publication | [Prana Krushna Parija](prana-krushna-parija.md) | Plant-respiration research with credited collaborators. |
| 2009 paper; 2021 prize | [Bedangadas Mohanty](bedangadas-mohanty.md) | Nuclear and particle-physics research, including collaborative experiments. |
| 2015 paper | [Sanghamitra Pati](sanghamitra-pati.md) | Public-health research among Odisha primary-care patients. |
| 2017 preprint; 2023 appointment | [Ajit Kumar Mohanty](ajit-kumar-mohanty-physicist.md) | Nuclear-physics research and national scientific leadership. |
| 2023 award | [Swati Nayak](swati-nayak.md) | Rice seed systems and agricultural field research. |

These are dated starting points, not birth-date order, a ranking or proof of an uninterrupted thousand-year scientific institution. Samanta’s project-native narrative and structured record remain canonical; RES-029’s reuse pointers identify them. His conflicting birth dates remain unresolved.

The [structured timeline and research lanes](../references/data/science-heritage.json) preserve the gaps. Extend the work through medieval manuscripts, nineteenth-century observational practice, modern institution building and contemporary disciplines. Women scientists and researchers working outside Odisha remain within scope when their connection is documented.

[Maritime evidence](../history/maritime-evidence.md) offers related archaeological context; ports and trade objects alone do not identify an inventor or establish navigation techniques. Astrological prediction, religious tradition and empirical astronomical computation require separate descriptions.

[Related agriculture evidence](../statistics/agriculture.md) — Read seed-system contributions alongside agriculture statistics; a training event does not measure statewide adoption or income.

[Related health evidence](../statistics/health.md) — Read the patient-study contribution alongside health statistics; a clinic sample does not establish statewide prevalence.

## Manuscript evidence · 1 October 2026

[Scientific knowledge preserved in manuscripts](../history/scientific-manuscripts.md) connects this timeline to institutional catalogues, including Bhāsvatī copies outside Odisha and mathematics texts held in Bhubaneswar. Named attribution and original manuscripts remain separate checks.

## Mathematics and science in Odia · 1 October 2026

[Tribikram Pati](tribikram-pati.md) adds a jointly credited 1960 mathematics paper. [Gokulananda Mohapatra](gokulananda-mohapatra.md) connects science with Odia literature and encyclopaedic writing. Two new profiles extend the selected timeline to nine identities including project-native Samanta; this is a research count, not a statewide total. Birth-date, degree and award conflicts remain recorded; research, education and science communication are distinct contributions.

## Computing and engineering · 1 October 2026

[Lalit Mohan Patnaik](lalit-mohan-patnaik.md) adds computing to the selected timeline through a Sambalpur education connection, IIT Bhubaneswar collaboration, TWAS election and a jointly credited 1994 paper. The [genetic-algorithms work](../works/adaptive-genetic-algorithms-1994.md) connects recognition with a named publication; bibliography verification does not replace reading its methods. Ten selected identities now appear in this evolving timeline, including project-native Samanta; this is not a statewide count.

## Computing, language and space · 1 October 2026

[Sanghamitra Mohanty](sanghamitra-mohanty.md) links the [Odia speech chapter](../works/odia-speech-wiener-filter-2012.md) and [edited proceedings](../works/speech-sound-music-2012.md). [Susmita Mohanty](susmita-mohanty.md) links design, enterprise and public service through a [space-policy article](../works/newspace-india-inspace-2022.md). These reading routes connect people to credited work; role and publication dates remain visible.

The initial RES-029 deliverable now contains twelve selected identities, including the existing project-native Samanta entry. It spans documented historical astronomy, modern research and science communication while preserving ancient/early-medieval attribution gaps. This completes a bounded timeline, not all scientific history. Full texts, disputed dates and further personalities remain follow-up research; no person is credited with a collective tradition solely from regional association.

# Tribikram Pati

**1929–2008**, as reported in the NISER-hosted memorial. Pati’s mathematics can be explored through a specific collaborative paper: [On the absolute summability factors of infinite series I](../works/pati-summability-1960.md), published with Z. U. Ahmad in 1960. It studies conditions for handling infinite series through a class of summation methods.

His Odisha connection includes reported leadership of the Odisha Mathematical Society and Odisha Bigyana Academy and founding chairmanship of the Institute of Mathematics and Applications, Bhubaneswar. These details come from a faculty-hosted memorial and await the institutions’ own historical registers. Publication in an international journal supports documented scholarly circulation, not a global popularity ranking.

Degree chronology remains unresolved: the memorial reports D.Phil. 1953 and D.Sc. 1956; IndCat labels a 1956 summability thesis as PhD. Neither has been silently corrected. A doctoral register is the next source. Work on the Riemann hypothesis must not be described as a verified solution.

# Chilika

## Sourced knowledge

Chilika is a brackish-water lagoon on Odisha’s coast, where freshwater and marine environments meet. The Chilika Development Authority describes it as a habitat for migratory birds and a source of livelihoods for fishing communities.[^cda]

# Debrigarh and Hirakud

## Sourced knowledge

The wildlife brochure connects Debrigarh and the Hirakud landscape.[^wildlife]

## Community livelihoods: a dated reported figure

**More than 150 community members were engaged at Debrigarh**, according to the Hirakud Wildlife Division officer quoted in The New Indian Express on 20 August 2026.[^debrigarh-nie-20260820] This is a reported participation count. It does not establish permanent jobs, annual full-time employment, income gains or net new jobs.

The report places community engagement alongside new visitor infrastructure. This supplies a local case study linking nature-based activity and livelihoods; it does not measure whether infrastructure caused employment growth or whether conservation outcomes improved.

## What the supplied clipping adds

The user’s Times of India clipping reports approximately 150 villagers engaged at Debrigarh and about 85 families directly engaged in 2025–26. Its comparison names around 80 community members at Similipal and 70 villagers at Satkosia’s ecotourism facilities.[^debrigarh-toi-user-clipping]

The clipping’s publication date and original URL are unresolved. Families and workers are different denominators: no growth calculation joins 85 to 150. Its statewide highest-employment claim remains a research lead, because a complete, dated and consistently defined comparison has not been checked. The two press sources offer similar accounts; they may rely on the same official and are not two independent headcounts.

The [five structured observations](../references/data/debrigarh-livelihoods.json) retain dates, units, qualifiers and review states. The original clipping remains in local research storage, outside public packages.

## Story opportunity

Explain the work behind a nature experience: community participation in safari and hospitality operations, with named workers’ accounts and consent as a next research step. A possible editorial theme is “The people behind Debrigarh’s nature experiences.” Keep employment evidence separate from claims about household income or ecological improvement.

*Editorial proposal; audience response has not been measured.*

## Next research

Obtain the dated original article and a primary engagement record from the Hirakud Wildlife Division: roles, duration, pay, worker/family definitions and comparable prior periods. Research community perspectives and conservation indicators separately. Check nature-camp access before visitor recommendations; no wildlife-sighting promises. The supplied Google share link remains unresolved, and is not assumed to be the clipping’s source.

## Connections

[Related knowledge](../stories/western-odisha.md) · [Research standards](../about/research-method.md)

[^wildlife]: [The Quest for Odisha’s Wildlife](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/dam/tourism/odishatourismbrochures/TheQuestforOdisha%E2%80%99sWildlife.pdf)
- [Employment](../statistics/employment.md) — Compare this local reported engagement count with statewide survey definitions; the populations are not interchangeable.

- [Biodiversity](../statistics/biodiversity.md) — Read ecological evidence separately from employment; one does not establish improvement in the other.

- [Editorial journey: western Odisha deserves its own chapter](../stories/western-odisha.md) — Place the livelihood story within a wider regional reading journey.

Subject reading: [Places](../subjects/places.md), [nature](../subjects/nature.md), [economy and livelihoods](../subjects/economy.md), [people](../subjects/people.md).

[^debrigarh-nie-20260820]: [The New Indian Express, 20 August 2026](https://www.newindianexpress.com/amp/story/states/odisha/2026/Aug/20/odishas-debrigarh-wildlife-sanctuary-witness-rise-in-visitors-upgraded-infrastructure-gave-push-to-it), closing officer statement.

[^debrigarh-toi-user-clipping]: [User-supplied Times of India clipping: provenance and limitations](../sources/debrigarh-toi-user-clipping.md).

## Programme context · 1 October 2026

The [state ecotourism series](../statistics/ecotourism.md) provides primary programme-wide income, visitor and participation context from Wildlife Odisha 2025. It does not corroborate the local 150-person account or supply Debrigarh payroll. The division’s comparable accounts and role/duration/pay definitions remain the next research step.

## Historical baseline and national recognition · 1 October 2026

A JICA survey published in **February 2017** records revenue from Debrigarh’s eco-complex facilities of **₹6.3 lakh in FY2009–10** and **₹19.3 lakh in FY2015–16**. It describes five cottages and notes no EDC engagement at that time. This is an institutional history to investigate, not evidence that communities had no other role. The historical facility scope cannot be spliced into present safari, cruise or sanctuary-wide revenue. [JICA report, printed p.4-12](https://openjicareport.jica.go.jp/pdf/12284139_01.pdf).

The [Prime Minister’s address of 30 August 2026](https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/pms-address-in-the-137th-episode-of-mann-ki-baat/) names **Maithili Bhue of Dhodrokusum**, describing her involvement in Debrigarh ecotourism. It states that more than 60 women were involved in forest conservation, including wildlife protection, grassland work and some ecotourism. This establishes national recognition of an attributed community story; it is not 60 verified tourism jobs, a formal award or measured household-income growth.

## Why the recent revenue growth headline is on hold

The [New Indian Express, 5 April 2026](https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/odisha/2026/Apr/05/odishas-debrigarh-raises-ecotourism-bar-with-sightings-record-tourist-footfall-revenue) reports ₹6.02 crore for FY2025–26 and ₹5.01 crore for FY2024–25. [OrissaPOST, 5 April 2025](https://www.orissapost.com/community-led-ecotourism-generates-rs-5-11cr-revenue/) reports ₹5.11 crore for Debrigarh and Hirakud Wetland together in FY2024–25. A scope difference could explain this, but no component accounts were obtained; no growth rate is adopted.

The dated OrissaPOST account also reports 85 families in that earlier financial-year context. The user clipping’s 85 families remains separately recorded under 2025–26. These are not silently merged or treated as annual growth.

A Hirakud DFO annual report retrieved from the Central Zoo Authority concerns **Sambalpur Zoo**, so its revenue and staff figures are excluded from this sanctuary case. Current payroll, income distribution and reconciled component accounts remain open.

[Programme-wide ecotourism](../statistics/ecotourism.md) — Read the statewide programme separately; its totals do not establish Debrigarh’s share or household earnings.

body:
# Ekamra Kanan: botanical collections and plant research

**The distinction is the cactus collection.** RPRC’s [Cacti page](https://rprcbbsr.in/researchanddevelopment/conservation/cacti) reports **1,050 cactus species and varieties** and describes this as Asia’s largest cactus collection. That is an attributed institutional claim about a collection; it does not establish that Ekamra Kanan is Asia’s biggest park.

The same page reports approximately **200 cactus varieties/hybrids developed** through its research. Species, varieties and hybrids are different categories. The collection and development counts must not be added together or presented as 1,250 species. Their inventory dates are not supplied.

## A garden that became a research institution

RPRC’s [history](https://www.rprcbbsr.in/about-us/history) dates its establishment to **1985**, initially as a recreational garden and green space for Bhubaneswar. It describes a subsequent research role spanning plant conservation and resource use. Ekamra Kanan is its botanical garden in Nayapalli; it is separate from the State Botanical Garden adjoining Nandankanan.

## Other stories inside the garden

The [official garden description](https://www.rprcbbsr.in/facilities/botanicalgarden) reports 72 scented-flower species, 52 hibiscus varieties, around 1,000 rose varieties, 32 threatened-plant species and 54 tropical palm types. These are undated collection descriptions with different units, not additive statewide biodiversity totals.

**Jagannath Vatika**, established in 2015, is described as holding **125 plant species** associated with Jagannath rituals and festivals. Individual ritual uses need their own sources. The existing wild-edible-fruit research adds another connection between botany and Odisha’s everyday food knowledge.

## Why the ranking stays attributed

[Panchkula’s district administration](https://panchkula.nic.in/tourist-place/cactus-garden/) describes a different category: Asia’s largest outdoor landscaped garden of cacti and succulents, reporting over 2,500 species of those combined groups. That does not directly confirm or refute RPRC’s cactus-only collection claim. A defensible ranking needs the same date, botanical scope, counting method and comparison set.

No Asia-wide park-area comparison was found in the sources checked. Precise RPRC campus and public-garden boundaries also remain to be established.

## Practical information still needs reconciliation

The official garden page gives conflicting opening times in its introductory text and visitor section. We therefore keep current opening hours unset rather than turn either passage into itinerary advice. Its annual attendance statement has no reporting year, so it is not used as a dated visitor statistic. Media rights and current facility availability also need checks.

## Proposed story treatment

**Ekamra Kanan: Bhubaneswar’s living library of plants.** Lead with the attributed cactus collection, then follow flowers, sacred plants and wild fruits into research and daily life. The headline is an editorial proposal, not a comparative award.

[Structured evidence and claim checks](../references/data/ekamra-kanan.json).


[Koli fruits](../food/koli-fruits.md) — Connects RPRC’s plant-conservation setting to the already sourced local-fruit names; it is not proof of current harvest or serving availability.

[Nandankanan](nandankanan.md) — Connects two distinct institutions for nature learning around Bhubaneswar; their gardens, inventories and visitor figures remain separate.

body:
# Hirapur: a circle of goddesses

Hirapur in Khordha district offers a distinctive architectural encounter: an open-air circular sanctuary with inward-facing Yogini sculptures. IGNCA’s inventory also records a central mandapa and images of Bhairavas. These details connect goddess worship with Shaiva imagery. [Inventory, pp.1–3](https://ignca.gov.in/asi_reports/orkhurda040.pdf).

The inventory distinguishes **sandstone construction from black-chlorite interior images**. Its sixty wall niches and central group describe an arrangement, not a newly verified count of surviving objects. It records weathering of the outer sculptures, a reminder that conservation belongs in the heritage story too.

Dating remains attributed: the inventory argues for the early tenth century from architectural and sculptural style, whereas the saved Odisha Tourism account says ninth century and names Hiradevi. No foundation inscription was examined here to settle the difference. The inventory’s description of active worship has no stated survey date; current rituals, entry, hours and facilities remain unverified.

[Read the comparative evidence](../culture/tantric-traditions.md) — Connects the Hirapur inventory to the comparative Yogini account without treating stylistic dating as a foundation inscription.

## Story opportunity

## Next research

[Visitor index](../visitor-index/index.md)

[^visitor-jagannath]: [Shree Jagannath Temple](https://puri.odisha.gov.in/en/tourism/tourist-places/shree-jagannath-temple)

## Visitor evidence · 30 September 2026

Odisha Tourism lists free entry, parking and nearby belongings-deposit outlets. Its attraction page says 05:00–23:00, while its [religious-shrines directory](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/dot/visitors-information/religious-shrines.html) lists 06:00–17:00 for Sri Mandira. These disagree; neither becomes a confirmed darshan schedule. The [attraction guidance](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/discover/attractions/temples-monuments/jagannath-temple.html) also lists camera, wallet and electronic-device restrictions. Current SJTA eligibility, exceptions and arrangements remain unverified after its website failed to open.

The [area evidence register](../references/data/puri-craft-access.json) preserves both hour listings. Toilets, water, step-free access and the exact deposit operator are unknown. Read the [craft corridor](../visitor-index/areas/puri-crafts.md) for separately researched stops; this connection does not establish a route or walking distance.

[Related reading](../visitor-index/areas/puri-crafts.md) — Read separately evidenced regional stops and visitor gaps; no proximity or route inferred.

### Royal patronage

[Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva](../people/anantavarman-chodaganga.md) provides a sourced reading route into the temple’s twelfth-century royal association. Detailed construction phases and later additions remain separate research questions.

## Origins: three separate research questions · 1 October 2026

Nayagarh district’s [Kantilo Nilamadhab description](https://nayagarh.odisha.gov.in/en/tourism/tourist-places/kantilo-nilamadhab) documents a religious association with Jagannath and locates the shrine beside the Mahanadi. It does not establish a dated relocation from a village to Puri.

1. **Religious tradition:** locate and attribute versions of the Nilamadhava, Visvavasu, Vidyapati and Indradyumna narratives, including community perspectives. Narrative sequence is not an archaeological date.
2. **Historical evidence:** examine dated inscriptions, textual editions and archaeological research for the development of worship and institutions.
3. **The present temple:** extend the existing Chodaganga and Anangabhima records through construction phases, patronage and later additions.

“From village to temple” remains a research question, not a settled origin claim. The existing access-hours conflict stays unresolved; historical work does not refresh visitor information.

## Jagannath evidence checkpoint · 2 October 2026 UTC

The [origins timeline](../history/jagannath-origins.md) now separates the Nilamadhava narrative from four edited thirteenth-century inscriptions in the Patalesvara shrine. A 1225 grant supports food offerings; two later records have calendar conflicts. This advances historical evidence, not current access verification.

# Koraput: landscape, makers and everyday enterprise

Coffee, cloth and landscape give this regional story several starting points. The district overview identifies coffee, Kotpad textiles and nature tourism. Read them as distinct subjects with their own people, production methods and economic questions.[^koraput]

## Things grown and made

[Koraput coffee](../food/koraput-coffee.md) is a starting point for learning about growers, processing and the route to market. [Kalajeera rice](../food/koraput-kalajeera-rice.md) adds an ingredient story. Neither entry establishes current sales, export volumes or verified sellers.

[Kotpad textiles](../handlooms/kotpad.md) connect Mirgan weaving traditions with aul-root dyes and earthy colours in the saved institutional reference. Maker attribution and community review should accompany a featured piece; “natural dye” alone does not establish organic certification.[^kotpad-textiles]

## A financial snapshot

**7,201.91 INR crore** — Bank advances utilised. 2026-06-30; Koraput district, Odisha.[^macro-slbc-jun2026]

This is a stock of bank advances utilised, not district output or household income. The linked banking page keeps deposits and both dated credit–deposit ratios together.

## The homestay opportunity

**60 homestay units** — Cycle-1 target. Cycle 1, reported 19 May 2026; Koraput cluster.[^homestay-cycle1-may2026]

This is a press-reported **Koraput cluster target**, not 60 open stays or a complete district inventory. The official allocation PDF remains unavailable. Host income, bookings, incentives paid and links to local food or weaving enterprises are still to be documented.

## Everyday life belongs in this profile

Education, health, transport, digital access and local work need district-specific evidence. Statewide figures in Life in Odisha are useful context; they cannot be assigned to Koraput. The district population pages timed out during the 30 September check, so this profile adds no newly verified population number.

## Next people and places to document

Build attributed profiles of willing growers, weavers, food producers and hosts, recording their village, work, product and verified contact channel with consent. Research seasonal access and actual commercial relationships before presenting a buying or visiting route. No current venue availability is established here.

# Langudi Hill and the Pushpagiri identification

**Langudi is a distinct Buddhist archaeological site in Jajpur.** Its proposed identification with Xuanzang’s Pushpagiri belongs to the history of scholarship as well as to modern interpretation.

The ASI Udayagiri report summarises B.N. Mukherjee’s readings of fragmentary Langudi inscriptions and D.R. Pradhan’s identification. The same author, Bimal Bandyopadhyay, records reservations after his 1999 visit and calls for further examination. [ASI 2007, pp.13–17](https://asi.nic.in/admin/publications/ePublicationReportsDetails/download/47). The saved Jajpur exhibition presents the identification affirmatively; retain that attribution rather than claiming universal agreement.

This checkpoint has not inspected the original 1997/1998 Langudi inscription articles, their full plates or all later research. It does not settle the site’s foundation date or establish a single university incorporating Ratnagiri, Lalitgiri and Udayagiri. Current access, facilities and media permissions remain unverified.

[Related reading](../history/buddhist-learning.md) — Places the proposed identification beside the traveller passage and independently named monasteries.

# Nandankanan: wildlife, conservation and a public institution

**39.35 lakh visits in 2024–25.** Nandankanan connects a popular day out near Bhubaneswar with breeding programmes, veterinary research, wetland habitats and wildlife education. Its reported revenue was **₹25.55 crore** that financial year, rounded from ₹2,554.79 lakh. Visits are not unique people; receipts are not profit or wider economic impact. [Annual report, printed p.72](https://nandankanan.org/images/documents/annual-report-2024-25.pdf).

## What changed

Against 2023–24, reported visits rose **0.4%**, while nominal revenue rose **18.1%**. Attendance was broadly steady. The report does not establish the cause of the revenue change, and these figures do not measure conservation quality. The structured register retains the full five-year table and calculation inputs.

## Conservation and history

Opened on **29 December 1960**, the institution’s account records captive gharial breeding and three white cubs born to normally coloured tiger parents in **1980**. Its claim to the world’s first captive gharial breeding remains explicitly attributed. It is not a claim to the first white tiger anywhere. [Annual report, history and preface](https://nandankanan.org/images/documents/annual-report-2024-25.pdf).

The [tiger programme page](https://www.nandankanan.org/conservation-breeding-of-tiger.php) dates participation in conservation breeding to 2009 and records a pseudomelanistic cub born on 28 July 2014. These are colour forms of tigers, not additional species. Breeding for a rare appearance is not itself evidence of a healthier wild population.

The annual report records **35 wild gharial hatchlings at Satkosia on 24 May 2024**. The [2025 highlights](https://nandankanan.org/images/documents/HIGHLIGHTS-2025.pdf) separately report **seven gharials released into the Mahanadi** and **14 hatchlings in the zoo’s pool**. Keep wild breeding, captive births and releases separate. The [recovery-project account](https://nandankanan.org/mobile/page.php?pid=gharial-breeding-at-nandankanan) also records entanglement, injury and mortality threats; post-release survival remains a research gap.

## A dated animal collection

The 2025 highlights report **4,110 animals representing 177 species as of 25 December 2025**. These are housed animals and the publisher’s species count, not a census of Odisha wildlife. The brochure calls the collection India’s largest; a like-for-like national inventory comparison is still needed before adopting that ranking.

Its **38.56 lakh visits and ₹23.37 crore revenue as of 25 December 2025** are partial-calendar-year figures. They must not be substituted for the financial-year series or used to claim an annual decline. The report also describes schools programmes and the conservation research centre, giving education and science their own place in this entry.

## Habitats and limits

The annual report places the zoo alongside Kanjia Lake and the State Botanical Garden within the sanctuary landscape. It also records animal deaths, including Nandan and Sara, alongside breeding achievements. A collection-size headline is not a welfare assessment.

The annual report’s preface says animal exchanges introduced 94 animals from 27 species; the website’s Director’s Desk says 30 species. This subtotal is held for reconciliation. All saved publications come from the same institution and are not independent confirmation.

## Proposed story

**Nandankanan: where a day out meets conservation.** A future feature can follow keepers, researchers, visitors and the gharial programme into connected stories. Images need rights clearance; interviews, current ticket prices, operating availability and accessibility checks are still pending.

[Evidence register](../references/data/nandankanan.json) retains periods, units, calculations and unresolved claims.


[Satkosia](satkosia.md) — Connects the zoo’s gharial work with the documented Satkosia wild-breeding setting; it does not establish survival of released individuals.

[Biodiversity](../statistics/biodiversity.md) — Connects captive inventories with biodiversity measurement while keeping them distinct from wild-population surveys.

# Ranipur-Jharial: Yoginis around a dancing Shiva

In Balangir district, Ranipur-Jharial’s circular Yogini temple brings the surrounding images into relation with a central dancing Shiva. IGNCA records an eight-armed Nataraja in a pillared mandapa, with Ganesa and Nandi on the pedestal. [Inventory, p.3](https://ignca.gov.in/asi_reports/orbolangir001.pdf).

The inventory gives an **external diameter of 16.60 metres** and an internal diameter of 13.60 metres. These are source measurements of this temple, not a national ranking. It attributes construction to the early tenth century within a broader ninth–tenth-century range and Somavamsi context. An individual ancient patron is not established; ASI’s appearance under “patron” describes modern care.

Its image inventory needs reconciliation: a stated total of 65 niches is divided into 48 with well-preserved images, 11 with damaged images or stones, and seven empty—categories summing to 66. Utkal therefore withholds a headline surviving-sculpture total. The report’s non-living label, conservation condition and granite identification remain dated-source claims with an unknown survey date; present worship and stone identification need further checking.

[Read the comparative evidence](../culture/tantric-traditions.md) — Connects the Ranipur-Jharial inventory to the comparative Yogini account while retaining its unresolved image count.

# Sambalpur–Bargarh: cloth, communities and regional enterprise

This is a reading collection across **two distinct districts**. Bargarh separated from Sambalpur in 1993; their current district statistics should retain separate labels. The Sambalpur administration identifies textiles among its defining activities, while the handloom department lists cotton tie-dye, silk and home furnishings at Bargarh.[^regional-sambalpur-overview][^weaving-centres]

## Two places, two statistical profiles

| Historical baseline | Sambalpur district | Bargarh district |
|---|---:|---:|
| Population, Census 2011 | 1,041,099 | 1,481,255 |

These are district-government reproductions of the 2011 Census, not 2026 population estimates.[^regional-sambalpur-overview][^regional-bargarh-demography] Bargarh’s table separately records 1,331,145 rural residents and 150,110 urban residents. The rural and urban counts sum to its district total. Literacy percentages are excluded here pending consistent denominator checks.[^regional-bargarh-demography]

## The fabric and the maker

[Sambalpuri Bandha](../handlooms/sambalpuri-bandha.md) and [Bargarh weaving](../handlooms/bargarh.md) provide complementary routes into textile history, technique and contemporary work. A textile’s regional name does not locate every workshop within Sambalpur district. Document each featured maker’s actual location and attribution. Current production, wages, sales and export series remain research gaps.

## Finance with the changes left visible

| Banking measure | Sambalpur district | Bargarh district |
|---|---:|---:|
| Deposits, 30 June 2026 | ₹42,139.41 crore | ₹11,768.67 crore |
| Advances utilised, 30 June 2026 | ₹25,781.51 crore | ₹9,484.63 crore |
| Credit–deposit ratio, 30 June 2025 | 95.19% | 74.41% |
| Credit–deposit ratio, 30 June 2026 | 61.18% | 80.59% |

The ratios move in different directions. A ratio alone does not establish whether lending rose or fell: both its numerator and denominator matter. Deposits and advances are banking stocks, not district GDP, investment received or maker income.[^macro-slbc-jun2026]

## Community work and landscape

**More than 150 community members** — Community ecotourism engagement. As reported 20 August 2026; reference date unspecified; Debrigarh Wildlife Sanctuary.[^debrigarh-nie-20260820]

The Debrigarh report is attributed press evidence of community participation. It does not establish permanent jobs, pay, net new employment or a measured conservation benefit. The [place record](debrigarh-hirakud.md) retains the undated clipping separately; families and workers cannot be compared as a growth series.

## Regional life to deepen

Add source-checked district education, health, agricultural production, work and service-quality measures. District institutional listings can guide research, but do not establish performance or current admissions. Locally reviewed festival, language and food coverage should credit named contributors.


[^regional-sambalpur-overview]: [About Sambalpur district](https://sambalpur.odisha.gov.in/en/about-district/about-us).

[^regional-bargarh-demography]: [Bargarh district demography](https://bargarh.odisha.gov.in/en/about--district/demography).

[^weaving-centres]: [Important handloom centres](https://handloom.odisha.gov.in/en/handloomtab/important-handloom-centers).

[^macro-slbc-jun2026]: [184th SLBC Odisha meeting agenda — June 2026 quarter](https://slbcorissa.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Total-Agenda-184th-SLBC-Meeting.compressed.pdf).

[^debrigarh-nie-20260820]: [Debrigarh infrastructure and community engagement, 20 August 2026](https://www.newindianexpress.com/amp/story/states/odisha/2026/Aug/20/odishas-debrigarh-wildlife-sanctuary-witness-rise-in-visitors-upgraded-infrastructure-gave-push-to-it).


## Connected reading

- [Life in Odisha](../collections/life-in-odisha.md) — Extend the regional story into education, health and everyday services.
- [Made in Odisha](../collections/made-in-odisha.md) — Connect textile traditions with maker attribution and livelihood research.

This is the first formal PRD version. Earlier conversation choices are reconstructed below as decision history, not invented prior PRD releases. Their order follows the discussion; exact message times, approvals and release dates are not invented. All occurred within the recorded 27 September 2026 planning sequence.

## Decisions leading to the baseline

| Order | Direction or proposal | Later disposition | Product consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Build a Git-backed Utkala · Odisha encyclopedia using existing content, photos and design work | Retained user objective | One durable public collection with website and Git contribution routes |
| 2 | Define audiences, information architecture and outcomes | Retained planning direction | Broad coverage with tourism/food/craft/story entrances and source inspection |
| 3 | Add KB-grounded conversational AI, internships, institutional relationships and analytics | Mixed scope | Analytics remains launch work; AI later deferred; internships and relationships remain programmes to arrange |
| 4 | Develop lineage/migration and global heritage connections | Retained future product scope | Evidence-qualified atlas; opt-in family records only after appropriate intake readiness |
| 5 | Consider object storage or a self-managed backend while avoiding complex cloud infrastructure | Superseded implementation proposals | Portable Git knowledge remained the core; no such provider was deployed |
| 6 | Consider Firebase and agree public read-only knowledge in Git, dynamic user data separately | Retained user direction | Spark for appropriate identity/private text features; public data does not depend on Firestore |
| 7 | Recommend Firebase Hosting, Blaze uploads/functions and Gemini | Partly superseded assistant proposal | Framework choice retained; hosting, upload method and paid feature scope changed below |
| 8 | Defer paid private backups and AI unless a suitable free alternative exists; use a custom domain with GitHub Pages | Retained explicit user direction | Static free hosting, search-first launch, no paid AI/backup launch requirement |
| 9 | Receive photo contributions by email or a free upload-to-email form and publish accepted photos manually through Git | Retained explicit user direction | No launch dependency on Firebase Storage or Cloud Functions; relay remains untested |
| 10 | Start with Spark and revisit Blaze for a specific justified need | User accepted this recommendation | No billing-enabled Firebase requirement for the launch design |
| 11 | Document stack, growth plan and diagrams in OKF | Completed documentation task | Technology concepts, current/future diagrams and architecture decisions are saved |
| 12 | Maintain a detailed PRD for history and references | Current documentation instruction | Versioned PRD, frozen baseline, requirements register and maintenance checks |

The initial $10–30/month assistant estimate applied to the broader AI/backup/managed-service design. It is historical context, not an approved launch budget. Current service target is $0 within free limits, excluding domain renewal and existing tools/labour. No pricing research is refreshed by this PRD update.

## Next change entry template

For a material change, append: version/date; added/changed/retired requirement IDs; previous and new behaviour; reason and evidence; explicit user/owner decision reference or “proposal”; effect on launch scope, cost, privacy and operations; open questions; related ADRs; snapshot paths/checksums; implementation/release reference when one exists. Never fabricate a commit, deployment or approval.

Keep prior entries intact. If an entry itself needs correction, append a dated correction explaining what was wrong. Use an erratum/new version for frozen baseline errors rather than editing history silently.

[Current PRD](prd.md) · [Maintenance procedure](prd-maintenance.md) · [Version register](../references/data/prd-version-register.json)

[The bounded batch](next-twenty.md) extends existing destination, language, literature, discovery and tour-book requirements. body:
# Maintaining the PRD and its historical record

## Authority and status

`product/prd.md` is the readable current document. `references/data/product-requirements.json` is its machine-readable requirements view. They describe one product baseline and must change together when requirement meaning changes. `product/versions/` and versioned requirements files preserve prior baselines. `references/data/prd-version-register.json` identifies the current version and checksums.

The initial v0.1.0 is a draft synthesis. It captures previously agreed decisions but does not claim formal approval of every acceptance detail. Keep lifecycle, approval, implementation, test outcome and public publication approval separate. Do not infer a human reviewer from an agent-generated document.

## Version rules

- Use a new **minor** version for meaningful scope, requirement, acceptance, policy or priority changes before a product release, such as 0.2.0.
- Use a new **patch** version for corrections or clarification that do not change intended behaviour, such as 0.1.1.
- Use 1.0.0 only when the owner explicitly designates an approved product baseline; a deployed website and a PRD version are related but different things.
- Give each requirement a permanent ID. Retire IDs explicitly; never reuse them for another purpose. Preserve their prior meaning in older snapshots.
- Record experiments as proposals; do not promote an experiment or paid feature to agreed launch scope without a decision.

## Update procedure

1. Read the current PRD, architecture decision register and latest user directions. Identify affected IDs and distinguish a correction from a scope change.
2. Prepare the changed requirements, acceptance criteria and consequences. Update narrative and structured register together. Record the decision basis honestly, including when it is still proposed.
3. Append a revision/history entry with rationale and affected IDs. Update related technical decisions when necessary; avoid allowing the PRD and architecture to prescribe conflicting launch behaviour.
4. Allocate a new version. Save a new readable snapshot and a corresponding versioned JSON requirements snapshot. Preserve all previous files unchanged. Fix relative links for the snapshot folder.
5. Calculate SHA-256 checksums, append the version registry entry and move its current pointer. Do not invent a Git tag; add a real revision/tag only after it exists.
6. Run `python3 outputs/odisha-kb/tools/validate_prd.py`, then the existing `reindex.py` and `validate.py` tools. Update the bundle log and checksum manifest.
7. Record acceptance-test results in release/test evidence, not by rewriting a preserved PRD. A result should reference requirement ID and PRD version, tester, date, outcome and evidence. Mark a requirement implemented only with actual implementation evidence.
8. When releasing a new edition, update summaries and the portable bundle according to the existing project procedure. A documentation update alone does not publish the website or change service billing.

## Preserving history

Snapshots are immutable by project convention. The validator detects changed snapshot hashes and cross-reference inconsistencies; it cannot prevent a person who changes both a file and its registered hash from rewriting history. Once Git is connected, reviewed changes and real version tags provide stronger history. Keep local copies in the meantime.

Do not overwrite current documents from old generation scripts. The scripts used to author the initial baseline are not an approved recurring publishing pipeline. Future work should edit the maintained files and append a new version deliberately.

The version register preserves requirements snapshots as well as the narrative. This matters because a historical PRD linked only to a changing current table would not preserve its original acceptance criteria.

## Traceability

User decision → architecture decision where relevant → requirement ID → acceptance criterion → implementation change → observed test evidence → release revision.

Not every requirement needs an ADR; product goals and programme requirements may trace directly to user direction. Each field must distinguish proposed, agreed, implemented and verified states. A provider pricing statement must carry its own check date when re-used for a purchase decision.

[Current PRD](prd.md) · [History](prd-history.md) · [Technology decisions](../technology/decisions.md)

This PRD describes what the product must achieve and how completion will be evaluated. Technical design records how it may be built. Earlier suggestions remain historical context; the latest user-agreed scope governs launch. Criteria marked `implementation_proposal` are design proposals, not separately approved user instructions. All feature acceptance tests remain unexecuted.

## 2. Problem and product vision

Knowledge about Odisha is spread across official sources, research, local accounts, photographs and diaspora memories. Our own work already spans a KB, brand concepts, a photo archive and multiple planning conversations. The product must turn this into a coherent, citable and maintainable public resource while allowing people without technical skills to improve it.

Help people **discover Odisha, understand it with context, and contribute to a trustworthy shared record**. Places, history, people, living arts, food and farming, nature, everyday life, the economy and governance each offer a way into the encyclopedia. Tourism is a featured collection connecting several of these subjects. Pride and modern opportunity should grow from supported knowledge, with difficult history, uncertainty and corrections retained.

The desired progression is curiosity → understanding → useful action → contribution. Readers may enter at any point. We do not need to prove a visitor journey to serve a student seeking a source.

## 3. Goals, outcomes and boundaries

Goals: make knowledge discoverable; preserve evidence and creator credit; accept public and Git contributions; improve representation over time; and support credible learning, research and cultural connection. Tourism demand, livelihoods and economic opportunity are longer-term ambitions, not outcomes that page views alone establish.

Launch does not include a booking marketplace, payment processing, a breaking-news operation, a complete statewide census, open public editing of canonical records, automatically accepted contributions, a definitive genealogy service, a podcast or AI chat. No partnership or internship is operational merely because it appears in this plan. Paid infrastructure upgrades and private backup services remain deferred under the agreed scope.

Launch language support must describe what has actually been reviewed; it does not promise a complete bilingual encyclopedia.

## 5. Information architecture and coverage

Proposed top-level navigation: **Subjects · Places · Odisha in Numbers · Stories · Contribute**. Food, handlooms and tourism remain featured collections within the shared subject structure. Keep search, language status, About, sources/editorial standards, credits, corrections, reuse terms and contact readily available. Global Connections can be reached through history, people and trade as it becomes ready. Programme information belongs under Contribute, with truthful availability and relationship status.

The [subject directory](../subjects/index.md) and [classification method](../methods/content-classification.md) define nine subject families underpinning these gateways: places/geography; history/heritage; people/languages/communities; arts/living traditions; food/farming; nature/environment; everyday life/human development; economy/livelihoods/infrastructure; governance/public life. These are coverage categories, not nine mandatory menu items or an obligation to publish empty sections.

Formats include encyclopedia entries, place profiles, person/practitioner profiles, stories/photo essays, oral histories, data explainers, recipes/process accounts, timelines, collections/journeys and individual archive items. Each should allow a quick understanding, deeper exploration and evidence inspection. Qualifications that change a claim remain beside the claim.

Geography, period, language, subject and evidence state are shared dimensions. Current boundaries must not be projected onto historical Odisha/Utkal/Kalinga automatically. One canonical item can appear in multiple gateways without duplicate content masters.

## 6. Launch scope and first complete slice

Launch with Bhubaneswar's Painted Streets as the end-to-end pilot, complemented by selected complete food and craft/place entries, plus proposed health/education and economy explainers with sources and contextual links. Those two non-tourism reading cases demonstrate breadth; they do not claim statewide coverage. A fixed page count is not the release gate. The pilot must prove reading, search, sources/credits, a guest contribution, editorial review, a Git change and publication.

The photo story preserves what the dated collection shows without inventing mural artists, exact locations or authoritative artwork titles. Invite evidence-backed identifications, clearly labelled memories and permitted photos. Existing assets and research are inputs; no blanket public-release permission is inferred from their presence in a local folder.

The launch architecture is Astro/TypeScript on GitHub Pages, a user-owned domain, public knowledge in Git and Firebase Spark for appropriate identity/private text features. Photos arrive through email or an activated/tested free relay; editors publish approved display copies manually through Git. Search replaces deferred chat. Target incremental service fees of $0 within free allowances; domain renewal, existing tools and labour are separate. This PRD does not authorise enabling billing.

## 7. Core journeys and operational states

**Discover and cite:** a reader searches or browses, opens an entry, understands its context, follows evidence, and shares/cites a stable identity. No account or analytics consent is required to read.

**Correct without Git:** a guest opens a correction form, supplies the claim/evidence and submits. The private record is created with a stable submission ID; failed saves remain visible. An editor requests detail, rejects with a private reason, or prepares a public-safe Git change. The outcome references the published revision when publication succeeds.

**Contribute photos:** a visitor selects files through the tested relay or emails them directly, including caption, credit and permission. The relay forwards to an inbox. The editor checks actual receipt and rights, prepares display copies and adds accepted material to Git. A relay confirmation, an email draft, receipt and publication are different states.

**Contribute through Git:** a contributor proposes public-safe files, automated checks run, an authorised editor reviews the content/media and the approved release is built. Public forks can propose changes; approved collaborators receive permissions, not exemption from review.

**Return as an editor:** an authenticated reviewer sees only permitted private records. Role assignment occurs through a maintainer-controlled process. Public site code or a hidden URL does not confer reviewer authority.

Editorial state model: received → triaged → needs information or accepted/rejected/withdrawn → published after a reviewed release. Preserve revision history when a published item is corrected or withdrawn; do not promise removal of previously downloaded or publicly versioned copies. Exact response-time promises remain unset until operating capacity is known.

## 9. Data and privacy requirements

The KB owns approved concepts, claims, sources, names, places, media metadata, rights/public credit and relationship records. Private working stores own contacts, raw submissions, consent, user preferences and permissions. Public data is readable in full if downloaded; a hidden UI field is not private storage.

Keep stable IDs, language, timestamps and source relationships. A source-check timestamp differs from editorial approval. A publication decision references the precise content/media revision. A derived data table retains its input definitions, period and calculation basis. Translation review is language-specific. Withdrawal/correction must update affected exports and search assets as well as visible pages.

Use only necessary private fields. Photo intake must not become an accidental family-identity collection. Living-family histories remain a future programme with an explicit purpose, consent and access design. Sensitive contacts and private lineage claims never become public just because their submission is useful to research.

## 10. Measurement and success

Establish a baseline after launch before setting growth targets. Proposed operating review cadence is monthly; this is a planning practice, not a newly scheduled automation.

| Outcome | Measure and definition | Evidence source | Interpretation limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Findability | Completion of named-entry, source and photo-credit tasks | Observed usability tasks | Traffic does not prove comprehension |
| Trust | Published entries with complete required sources/credits; correction turnaround | Publication metadata and private editorial queue | Automated checks do not prove historical truth |
| Contribution | Received, accepted and published counts; oldest pending age | Confirmed Firestore saves and editorial inbox records | Relay acceptance is not inbox receipt |
| Coverage | District × subject × language states and overdue reviews | KB coverage register | A missing entry does not imply a community lacks history |
| Usefulness | Source/citation actions and attributed reuse | Consented safe events; verified external citation links | Downloads are not endorsement |
| Sustainability | Manual review effort, failures and quota pressure | Aggregate operations records | Free service today is not guaranteed future capacity |

GA4 is a consented supporting signal; editorial outcomes use their own records. Private review and application pages are excluded. Disable automatic raw search/form collection. Do not collect sensitive data through custom event parameters or URLs.

## 11. Release acceptance

Launch acceptance requires all `launch` requirements to be tested or an explicit documented scope exception. A free relay is optional if the direct-email path works; photo contribution itself remains supported. A test case is not passed merely because its design is written here.

A reviewer should demonstrate: find the pilot story; identify a photo's credit/date; locate an original source; understand a statistical period/unit; submit a correction without GitHub; send a permitted photo through the selected path; publish one accepted contribution through Git; reject an unauthorised private read/write; decline analytics without losing functionality; and roll back a public release. Record actual results and responsible reviewers when this occurs.

The UI must state missing translation, unavailable submissions and evidence gaps honestly. No public release may contain confidential records or unapproved media. The domain, inbox, repository rules, Firebase permissions and GA4 property must be configured and verified for the features actually enabled. AI and private-backup restoration are not launch gates while those services are deferred.

## 12. Growth sequencing and upgrade gates

Follow the [technical growth roadmap](../technology/growth-roadmap.md). Begin with a useful collection and manual editorial flow. Expand editorial capacity and regional/language coverage before adding infrastructure merely for anticipated scale.

Revisit managed uploads and automation when lost attachments, submission limits or manual burden are measured. Revisit cited AI when search leaves recurring questions unanswered and a viable free integration or revised budget exists. Revisit private recovery when a suitable free export is established or operations require a recovery commitment. Preserve Git/OKF as the public knowledge source across upgrades.

The Heritage & Global Connections Atlas is the public umbrella; the Utkal Lineage & Migration Index is a subset. Investigate movement into and out of Odisha, languages, trade, belief/learning, living culture, objects abroad and contemporary diaspora, with evidence-qualified relationships. Do not treat similarity, commemoration, institutional membership or a surname as proof of lineage or continuous influence.

Internships should offer supervised, bounded research and learning, with local contributors and international students able to participate. Partner relationships should begin with concrete mutually useful work. No academic programme, organisation or cultural body is an agreed partner merely because it is a candidate. Outreach and recruitment require actual arrangements and explicit authorisation.

## 16. Basis and references

This is a synthesis of the user's conversation and the existing local planning/OKF material, not new independent research or a newly verified pricing quote. The product/audience, information architecture, atlas, internship and analytics proposals were consulted from the Odisha Tourism planning workspace. Current launch decisions supersede earlier alternatives.

Durable reference points: [community encyclopedia](../about/community-encyclopedia.md), [tourism-first audience strategy](../about/tourism-first-strategy.md), [research method](../about/research-method.md), [website readiness](../about/website-readiness.md), [statistics storytelling](../about/statistics-storytelling.md), [architecture decisions](../technology/decisions.md) and [growth roadmap](../technology/growth-roadmap.md).

## Repository integration · 1 October 2026

This imported research describes the source workspace at its recorded dates. Utkal Project already has a repository and a published preview; current authority, implementation and release status are held in [project records](../../records/index.md) and [the operating dashboard](../../registers/DASHBOARD.md). This sync adds research for review; it does not deploy these additions or replace implemented website addenda. The scheduled research queue continues in its existing workspace pending a separate canonical-workflow handover.


## Name correction · 1 October 2026

The user confirmed **Utkal**, correcting earlier Utkala wording. Version 0.2.1 updates the name only; requirement IDs, behaviour and approval states remain unchanged. Earlier snapshots retain their original text.
