body:
# Forest products: what the market numbers measure

**OFDC's kendu-leaf realised sales were ₹533.58 crore in FY2023–24**, down **6.39%** from ₹570 crore in FY2022–23. The 2025 forestry report's series is:

| Financial year | Realised sales, ₹crore |
| --- | ---: |
| 2019–20 | 399.09* |
| 2020–21 | 460.84 |
| 2021–22 | 591.77 |
| 2022–23 | 570.00 |
| 2023–24 | 533.58 |

Quantities sold include arrear stock. These nominal sales are neither collectors' net income nor the total forest-food market. **Kendu leaves are a non-food product.** Source: [Odisha Forestry Sector2025, printed p.159](https://odishaforest.in/admin/data/documents/publication_file_1151142053.pdf).

*The undated [OFDC webpage](https://www.odishafdc.com/kenduleaf.php) reports ₹399.14 crore and2.621 lakh quintals for2019–20, against ₹399.09 crore and2.625 lakh quintals in the2025 report. Both competing observations are held for reconciliation; no endpoint growth calculation uses them. The report's separate crop-year series is also not interchangeable with this fiscal-year table.

The same report describes **15 tonnes/year installed honey-processing capacity at Jashipur, Mayurbhanj** (printed p.161). This is capacity, not verified production, utilisation or wild-honey procurement.

[Canonical observations](../references/data/statistics-atlas.json) preserve these boundaries. [Market research](../economy/forest-products.md) explains what remains missing. No statewide forest-food market-size estimate is currently supported here.

## Food-processing research capability

OUAT reports a developed mahua candy/nectar unit rated10 kg per batch in its2020–21 report (printed p.23). [Source](https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/annual_report_2020-21_3.pdf). This is a research-unit specification, not an operating-factory census, annual output or commercial success. The observation is saved separately from OFDC honey capacity.

## Worker welfare: preserve the payment year and scope

The 2025 report records **₹250.75 crore distributed during 2023 for crop year 2022**, to more than eight lakh beneficiaries. It separately records **₹108.60 crore of bonuses and incentives during 2024 for crop year 2023**, to about nine lakh beneficiaries. The descriptions cover different benefit scopes; do not calculate a like-for-like decline or average worker earnings from them. [Printed p.150](https://odishaforest.in/admin/data/documents/publication_file_1151142053.pdf).

The [live welfare portal](https://kenduleaves.odisha.gov.in/welfare-measures), updated 9 September 2026, now displays ₹250.39 crore for year 2022, ₹116.07 crore for 2023 and ₹100.69 crore for 2024. Its year basis is unspecified. The older search-indexed snapshot contains different values again. These are held as a scope/vintage conflict, not silently substituted into the older report.

## A separately labelled grant table

| Financial year | Reported grant records | Total amount, ₹crore |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2023–24 | 587 | 11.235 |
| 2024–25 | 1,216 | 24.060 |
| 2025–26 | 1,235 | 24.635 |
| 2026–27, partial; cutoff unstated | 257 | 5.130 |

Source: [Compassionate Grant table](https://kenduleaves.odisha.gov.in/welfare-measures), read 1 October 2026. Amounts above convert the original rupees by dividing by 10,000,000. These death/permanent-disability welfare records must not be presented as distinct people, all worker benefits or household income. A higher grant total is not inherently a better wellbeing outcome. Partial 2026–27 must not be compared with complete years.

## An additional original vintage for the sales discrepancy

OFDC's 2020–21 annual report gives **262,581 quintals** in the FY2019–20 comparative sales column (printed p.17), equivalent to 2.62581 lakh quintals. The page was visually checked. This supports an additional precise historical observation but does not reconcile the existing 2.625/2.621 lakh totals or ₹399.09/₹399.14 crore sales values. Keep the original conflict open. [Annual report](https://www.odishafdc.com/annual_report/Annual_Report_2021.pdf).

## Van Dhan: a dated national comparison · 2 October 2026 UTC

The [11 December 2023 parliamentary reply](https://sansad.in/getFile/loksabhaquestions/annex/1714/AU1179.pdf?source=pqals) reports **₹10.7201 crore** in cumulative Odisha Van Dhan sales, **170 sanctioned centres** and **50,094 beneficiaries**. Odisha's reported sales are the highest of the annexure's 28 state/UT rows and about **26.1%** of its ₹41.0295 crore total. These are programme figures, including MFP and non-MFP activities; they are neither annual sales nor the whole forest economy. The exact common reporting cutoff is unstated.

The annexure was visually checked. A newer departmental report was located but could not be retrieved; its indexed figures have not been substituted. No growth calculation connects incompatible reporting snapshots. [Readable story](../stories/van-dhan-enterprises.md).

## Kendu accounts: where the sale proceeds are allocated

OFDC's FY2020–21 accounts report **₹460.8417021 crore** realised sales in Note26(b), covering receipts from 2016–2020 crops. The allocation reconciles exactly in original rupees:

| Accounting component | ₹crore, rounded | Payment status |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Working-fund advance to Forest Department | 270.03 | Released to department |
| Selling commission | 41.20 | Commission allocation |
| Additional financing commission | 3.20 | Commission allocation |
| Royalty/KLDF | 146.41 | Payable to department |
| Forest development tax | 0.00 | Payable category |

[Annual report, printed p.83 / PDF p.84](https://www.odishafdc.com/annual_report/Annual_Report_2021.pdf), visually checked. Exact values are retained in the structured register. # Forests

ISFR 2023 reports 52,433.56 square kilometres of forest cover and 6,163.45 square kilometres of tree cover in Odisha. Their combined area is 58,597.01 square kilometres. Read the assessment date and mapping definitions alongside the totals.[^nature-forest-pib]

## What these measures explain

# Health

NFHS-6 records 82.7% of Odisha households with at least one usual member covered by health insurance or a financing scheme, compared with 47.9% in its NFHS-5 comparison column. The Odisha fieldwork was July–November 2024; this is not a 2026 coverage survey. It does not establish coverage of every household member.[^people-nfhs6]

## What these measures explain

How do households access financial protection and maternal and child services? Coverage and utilisation can be described without treating them as proof of care quality or protection from every expense.

## Selected facts to explore

- **Households with health insurance/financing coverage: 47.9 percent of households** — NFHS-5 (2019–21), as reproduced in NFHS-6 release, Odisha.[^people-nfhs6]
- **Households with health insurance/financing coverage: 82.7 percent of households** — NFHS-6 (2023–24); Odisha fieldwork 18 July–28 November 2024, Odisha.[^people-nfhs6]

body:
# Odisha’s homestay opportunity

Odisha is building a public support system for family-hosted stays. The strongest evidence today concerns the scheme, its funding envelope and planned expansion. A historical marketplace report also suggests more properties were being advertised, while actual demand, host income and operating-unit growth remain unmeasured in this collection.

## Three figures to understand

| Figure | Meaning | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **₹50 crore** | Multi-year budget earmark, FY2025–26 to FY2028–29; not expenditure | 2025 Gazette, clause 3.3[^homestay-scheme2025] |
| **450 new homestays** | Overall scheme target; not completed units | 2025 Gazette, section 6[^homestay-scheme2025] |
| **380 homestays** | Reported Cycle-1 target in May 2026; primary allocation PDF still needed | Departmental figures reported by TOI[^homestay-cycle1-may2026] |

The first-cycle report describes 61 Gram Panchayats across 19 districts and 19 clusters, including targets of 60 in Koraput and 50 in Kandhamal. These are selected examples, not a complete district allocation list. They must not be added to the statewide programme target.[^homestay-cycle1-may2026]

## Is popularity increasing?

A January 2025 newspaper report describes roughly 50 properties advertised as homestays in 2017 and over 350 by its publication date. It also counted 270 Airbnb listings, including apartments, villas and other property types. This is a sign of a broader marketed offering, with unclear de-duplication and consistent definitions; it is not a measured statewide booking-growth series.[^homestay-market-jan2025]

The same report describes approximately 100 properties with 250 rooms identified around Bhubaneswar for Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas. That event inventory is separate from permanent registered supply.[^homestay-market-jan2025]

A parliamentary reply of 11 August 2025 lists **14 Odisha rural homestays on NIDHI**, a voluntary national registry. That narrow count neither disproves the marketplace figures nor measures all homestays. The reply expressly says NIDHI does not record tourism or occupancy days.[^homestay-nidhi2025]

## What would demonstrate sustained growth?

Follow the same defined group through applications, approval, construction, commercial operation and annual compliance. Then measure rooms available, room-nights sold, occupancy and host earnings. Keep closures and cancellations. Our [monitoring record](../references/data/homestay-research.json) leaves unavailable outcomes unknown rather than zero.

A useful story now is **“Odisha is investing in family-hosted tourism.”** Claims of an occupancy boom, rising household incomes or a successful 450-property rollout need further evidence.

## Read this in context

Subject: [Economy, livelihoods and infrastructure](../subjects/economy.md). Also part of [Places](../subjects/places.md), [People](../subjects/people.md) and [Governance](../subjects/governance.md).

- [Government support and policy history](../economy/homestay-support.md) — Separate the scheme’s incentives and later amendments from outcomes.
- [Accommodation](accommodation.md) — Hotel inventories and homestay registers describe different accommodation categories.
- [Debrigarh and Hirakud](../places/debrigarh-hirakud.md) — Compare a local community-work case without treating nature camps as registered homestays.

## Evidence and unresolved points

The original scheme uses **1,800 rooms** in section 6(a) and **1,800 beds** in section 7.2(a). Both records are held as a conflict; neither becomes our capacity headline. Later amendment text and the full Cycle-1 allocation remain retrieval priorities. No current application window or property availability is established here.

Definitions, evidence status and publication-readiness fields remain in the [statistical atlas](../references/data/statistics-atlas.json). Policy thresholds are not achieved results. No human editorial review is claimed.

[^homestay-cycle1-may2026]: [From Deomali to Daringbadi, homestays get a push](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bhubaneswar/from-deomali-to-daringbadi-homestays-get-a-push/articleshow/131184349.cms).

[^homestay-market-jan2025]: [Homestay count grows manifold in Odisha but local experience missing](https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/odisha/2025/Jan/04/homestay-count-grows-manifold-in-odisha-but-local-experience-missing).

[^homestay-nidhi2025]: [One India, One Registration Initiative under NIDHI Portal](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2155162&lang=2&reg=48).

## Portal geography: a new dated snapshot · 1 October 2026

**61 Gram Panchayats, grouped into 19 clusters across 16 districts**, appear in the public Go Homestay area list captured today. These are calculated counts of distinct publisher IDs in a place list, not homestays built or open. The [saved table](../references/data/homestay-portal-areas-20261001.json) also preserves destination and block relationships.

The earlier May report above says 19 districts. Keep it as a historical secondary claim: the current portal has multiple clusters within some districts. Without the original allocation and amendment texts, this difference cannot establish a reduction, a reporting correction or definitive legal coverage.

Rayagada’s portal rows include both Kulusing and Puttasing, despite the reported replacement amendment. The [policy record](../economy/homestay-support.md) holds this discrepancy. Current eligibility and booking recommendations remain unverified.

[Official public area data](https://gohomestay.odisha.gov.in/api/allowAll/get-notified-gp-list). This is a geography story with a dated scope, not evidence of occupancy, revenue or host-income growth.

## Operating evidence checkpoint · 1 October 2026

World Tourism Day coverage supplies a new lead but conflicting quantities: [Odisha Connect](https://odishaconnect.com/odisha-celebrates-world-tourism-day-2026-with-digital-innovation-and-community-led-tourism/) reports 176 provisional-registration beneficiaries in an indexed passage; [OdishaBytes](https://odishabytes.com/odisha-signs-pacts-to-promote-homestay-heritage-adventure-tourism/amp/) says 17 in its directly read closing paragraph. The event is 27 September 2026. Both counts are held pending an original departmental release/register, outside the headline statistics. The reports may draw on the same event announcement.

OdishaBytes also reports an SBI financing MoU. Its signed terms, loan approvals and disbursements were not obtained. An agreement is not realised lending. No active-property census, completed compliance returns, occupancy or host-income data was recovered in this bounded search. Unknown remains unknown.

[Community ecotourism evidence](../statistics/ecotourism.md) now supplies a separately scoped programme income/visitor series; it does not fill homestay operating gaps.

# Mining: national contribution and local development

**Odisha accounted for 43.7% of India’s mineral-production value in IBM’s 2024–25 highlights, excluding fuel, atomic and minor minerals.** The same vintage reports Odisha’s shares of iron-ore and bauxite output as **55%** and **72.7%**. These are different measures; they must not be added or described as a share of all mining including coal.

IBM reports **3.026 million tonnes of chromite**, all from Odisha, with output **down 3.9%** from the preceding year. Preserve that decline alongside the national contribution. These March 2025-vintage figures remain subject to revision. [IBM, printed pp. viii–ix](https://www.ibm.gov.in/writereaddata/files/1748864652683d8e8cdc8f1MSMP_MARCH25FINAL.pdf).

**Mining-area funds need an outcomes story.** CAG records **₹26,602.66 crore in leaseholder contributions** across Odisha’s 30 DMFs during 2015–16 to 2023–24. In its six sampled DMFs, **₹10,092.53 crore** had been spent against **₹20,947.52 crore sanctioned** by March 2024—**48.18%** of sanctions. The sample is Dhenkanal, Jajpur, Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj, Nabarangpur and Sundargarh. These sampled expenditure figures are not statewide utilisation rates or measures of working services. **Unresolved source conflict:** Table 4.1 reports ₹10,104.28 crore expenditure instead of Table 5.1’s ₹10,092.53 crore. The retained expenditure and derived 48.18% observations are held pending clarification; see the [cross-table comparison](../economy/dmf-community-outcomes.md#the-report-contains-conflicting-totals). [CAG Report 7 of 2026, executive summary pp. ix–x](https://cag.gov.in/webroot/uploads/download_audit_report/2026/Report-No.-7-of-the-year-2026_PMKKKY-06aba7c29ed78b2.53467972.pdf).

## Evidence boundaries

The IBM value comparison uses nominal reported production values, not real GSVA or government revenue. Resource stocks, production, dispatch, processing, sales and tax receipts need separate series. The CAG report was listed on 28 September 2026 but covers an earlier audit period; it is not a September 2026 balance.

[Canonical observations](../references/data/statistics-atlas.json) own the numeric records. [Mining coverage](../economy/mining.md) explains the next questions. New data will retain revision history and resolve older imported comparisons rather than silently replace them.

## Coal series checkpoint · 1 October 2026

[Coal production and resources](coal-production.md) adds fuel-mineral evidence alongside the IBM non-fuel figures. These coverage scopes must remain separate.

## Ore reconciliation checkpoint · 1 October2026

[Ore production](ore-production.md) adds eleven-year state observation coverage and three-year IBM comparison for four ores, including retained source differences.

## Baphlimali returns · 2 October2026 UTC

[Baphlimali’s mine-level return](../economy/bauxite-mine-identities.md) adds FY2024–25 output and DMF payment evidence. A mine’s payment is not district spending or a statewide total.

## Mining and community services · 2026-10-02

[Receipts, six DMFs and four case bundles](../economy/dmf-community-outcomes.md) adds actual/BE/RE scope, Tables5.1–5.2 and selected implementation findings. The existing48.18% uses sanctions;76.69% uses releases. Neither is a statewide benefit measure. All30DMF contributions and six-DMF collections including interest have different scopes.

body:
# Ore production: trends, places and source differences

**Odisha’s bauxite output nearly doubled over ten years in the state Directorate series:** 9.192 million tonnes in 2014–15 became 17.934 million tonnes in 2024–25, a calculated **95.1% increase**. This is ore production, not aluminium output. [State table](https://www.odishaminerals.gov.in/StatisticsReport/DespatchProductionReport).

The evidence now keeps production and despatch separately for five minerals across eleven annual observations. It also retains declines: chromite falls from 3.930 million tonnes in 2019–20 to 3.187 million tonnes in 2024–25 in that state capture, while manganese slips from 0.659 to 0.618 million tonnes in its final year. These attributed series do not settle differences with IBM.

## Where the sources disagree

| 2023–24 production, million tonnes | State Directorate | IBM Yearbook 2024, provisional |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Iron ore | 169.034 | 148.959 |
| Bauxite | 17.539 | 17.591967 |
| Chromite | 3.160 | 3.147954 |
| Manganese ore | 0.659 | 0.650856 |

The cause is unverified. Do not combine one agency’s Odisha numerator with another’s India denominator. Disputed observations are held for reconciliation. Even the two state website routes differ for 2019–20 iron ore: 146.016 versus 142.159; the existing five-year comparison remains a historical imported claim requiring review.

## Put mineral evidence back in its place

IBM’s 2023–24 bauxite producer table links NALCO and OMC to Koraput, and Utkal Alumina to Rayagada. These are mine-location districts, not office addresses or exact lease identities. Its chromite tables preserve Jajpur and Kendujhar quantities and mark Dhenkanal as labour-only reporting; no output is inferred from a reporting-mine count.

Resource tables are dated **1 April 2020** and separate reserves from remaining resources. For bauxite, 409.740 million tonnes are classified as reserves within 2,057.024 million tonnes total resources; for haematite iron ore the corresponding quantities are 2,798.749 and 9,409.331 million tonnes. Historical inventory does not become current mineable supply. [IBM Yearbook 2024](https://www.ibm.gov.in/writereaddata/files/177426215469c1178a48453IMYB_2024_EBookFinal.pdf).

[Structured mining evidence](../references/data/mining-programme.json) — all series, units, original values, source locators and held comparisons.

[Mining: minerals, industry and people](../economy/mining.md) — Connects ore quantities and district evidence to separate processing, revenue and livelihood research.

# Odisha’s textile and apparel export story

**₹757.33 crore in 2024–25**, up **6.9%** from ₹708.13 crore in 2023–24. This Ministry of Textiles series includes handicrafts alongside textiles and apparel.

![Five annual export values; fall in 2022–23 and recovery thereafter](../references/charts/textile-exports-2020-2025.svg)

Across these five annual observations, export value rose from ₹211.67 crore in 2020–21. The endpoints are four years apart; the first is the pandemic fiscal year. Growth was uneven, with a decline from ₹641.05 crore in 2021–22 to ₹528.39 crore in 2022–23. These are nominal rupees, not inflation-adjusted output.

## Evidence view

| Full financial year | INR crore |
|---|---:|
| 2020–21 | 211.6730 |
| 2021–22 | 641.0501 |
| 2022–23 | 528.3892 |
| 2023–24 | 708.1322 |
| 2024–25 | 757.3289 |

Source: Ministry of Textiles, 24 March 2026, DGCI&S table, Odisha row. Original values are INR lakh; divide by 100 for crore. This dated release is not claimed to be the latest available. It does not tell us which garment, named weave, factory or destination generated the sales. The Economic Survey’s narrower textile grouping must remain separate until definitions are reconciled.

| Total tourist visits | 11,052,211 visits | 2024; Odisha | reported-source-conflict; hold_conflict[^connect-tourism2024] |
| Foreign tourist visits — conflicting central release | 87,854 visits | 2024; Odisha | reported-source-conflict; hold_conflict[^connect-tourismconflict] |

## Interpretation limits

- Visits, not unique people; calendar year.
- Visits, not unique people; calendar year. State bulletin foreign count conflicts with Ministry of Tourism February 2026 table (87,854); do not silently replace or blend series.
- Conflicts with state Statistical Bulletin 2024 value 53,392. Hold foreign-growth headline until reconciliation.

The [structured atlas](../references/data/statistics-atlas.json) retains indicator IDs, exact source locators and definitions. [Coverage and gaps](coverage.md) · [Atlas home](index.md).

## Reconciliation checkpoint · 30 September 2026

The Ministry's [8 December 2025 release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2200323&lang=1&reg=6), Annexure I, reports **87,854 foreign tourist visits in 2024** and **45,173 in 2023** for Odisha. The higher 2024 count therefore appears in an earlier central release as well as the saved February 2026 table. This is corroboration within government reporting, not an independent enumeration.

The state bulletin's saved **53,392** remains unresolved. No correction or definition bridge was found. Keep foreign-growth and affected total-visit headlines on hold. The ministry explicitly separates state visits from international arrivals; neither is a count of unique travellers to Odisha. Follow the annexure's 2020–2024 columns despite a wider period mentioned in surrounding prose.

[Reconciliation evidence](../references/data/tourism-series-reconciliation.json) preserves the checks and failures. [Tourism comparison](../economy/comparison-09-tourism.md) shows why a conflicting component also affects the total; [source recovery](../methods/source-reliability.md) records the remaining document work.

## Community-managed programme evidence

[Ecotourism](ecotourism.md) now has a dated primary income/visitor series. Its narrower programme scope must not be added to statewide tourist-visit totals.

# Women And Inclusion

Among women aged 15–49, reported internet ever-use rises from 24.9% to 51.8% between the survey columns reproduced in NFHS-6. The later Odisha fieldwork took place in July–November 2024. Ever-use is not daily access or a measure of digital skill.[^people-nfhs6]

## What these measures explain

How do women’s access and participation change across survey rounds? Banking, schooling and internet use offer distinct views; keep age range and survey vintage beside each figure.

These are editorial reading connections, not assertions of causation, proximity or a verified supply chain.

title: A name in clay across Odisha’s Buddhist circuit
description: A reader journey through excavated names, relic caskets and traveller testimony, keeping three Buddhist sites distinct.

sources.title: Excavations at Udayagiri-2 (1997–2000), Memoirs of the Archaeological Survey of India No.100
The Great Tang Dynasty Record of the Western Regions

body:
# A name in clay across Odisha’s Buddhist circuit

A monastery can return to us through a few letters.

At Udayagiri-2, excavated clay seals and sealings helped researchers identify **Simhaprastha Mahavihara**. Among the published readings is a fragment carrying part of that name. The archaeological report preserves its accession number, the reading and the uncertainty around damaged lettering. A place that might first appear as walls and foundations becomes a named institution, remembered through something small enough to overlook.

That is a rewarding way to approach Odisha’s Buddhist circuit: let one detail hold your attention before widening the view. [Ratnagiri](../places/ratnagiri.md), [Udayagiri](../places/udayagiri-buddhist.md) and [Lalitgiri](../places/lalitgiri.md) offer related histories, but each deserves its own questions. You do not have to recognise every figure or understand every period to begin looking closely.

## Let the name lead you

The ASI report on the 1997–2000 excavations, by **Bimal Bandyopadhyay**, credits the inscription readings to **Snigdha Tripathy**. It distinguishes Simhaprastha at Udayagiri-2 from **Madhavapura Mahavihara**, identified through seals in an earlier excavated area at Udayagiri.

Two names within the same archaeological site are already a reason to slow down. Ask how a particular structure, object or inscription acquired its identification. A guide or museum label may be able to connect what you see with the evidence behind the name. A question left open is also worth remembering; it can lead you back to a book after the visit.

Keep the destination clear when arranging transport. This Buddhist Udayagiri in the Jajpur circuit is distinct from the Jain Udayagiri–Khandagiri caves near Bhubaneswar. A familiar place name is not always a sufficient address.

## Three places and different ways of looking

For **Ratnagiri**, begin with the work of discovery. The Udayagiri report recalls **D. Mitra’s excavations at Ratnagiri between 1958 and 1961**. That research history gives another dimension to a visit: someone had to expose, record and interpret the remains before they could become the heritage landscape a visitor encounters.

Choose a detail that interests you, then look for its context. Where was the object found? Does the label give a date, an interpretation or both? If photography is permitted, a picture of the label alongside the object can preserve a connection that a dramatic close-up alone would lose.

At **Lalitgiri**, the containers around a relic offer a different point of attention. A Ministry of Culture briefing issued in December 2018 describes three khondalite stone caskets recovered from a stupa during the 1985 excavations. Two held further caskets of steatite, silver and gold, with charred bone relics inside. The same briefing describes the new site museum as a place for displaying and protecting excavated antiquities.

The sequence of materials invites a patient look: stone, another stone container, silver, gold. What did enclosing and protecting something mean to the people who placed it there? Let interpretation accompany that question. The account establishes a reported find; it does not establish whose remains the relics are. Religious significance can be discussed respectfully without attaching a certainty the evidence has not supplied.

Museum arrangements and individual displays can change. Check access before setting out, particularly if the caskets or a specific object are the reason for your visit.

## Read a traveller beside the archaeology

There is another kind of journey in **Xuanzang’s account**, available in English through **Li Rongxi’s translation**. In its description of Uḍa, the text places an interest in learning alongside more than a hundred monasteries and over ten thousand monks. It then introduces Pushpagiri monastery and reports spiritual signs associated with its stupa.

Read those passages with their different purposes in mind. The numbers refer to the wider historical country, not to a student register for Pushpagiri. The spiritual signs belong to the traveller’s religious account. Neither passage identifies Simhaprastha merely because both belong in a story about the region.

Our [Buddhist learning collection](../history/buddhist-learning.md) follows these connections and the debated identification of Pushpagiri. A modern circuit makes it easier to discover several places; it does not turn them into one ancient university. The more carefully we keep their identities, the more interesting the connections become.

## Make room for one good explanation

Before choosing a route, decide what you most want to understand: a monastery’s name, a sculpture, the care of relics or the history of excavation. Choose one main site and allow time for its museum or interpretation if available. Add another only after checking transport, current opening arrangements, walking conditions and your return time. This story is a reading companion, not a tested one-day itinerary.

Ask a qualified guide to explain one object or structure in detail. Establish the appointment and fee beforehand; confirm any language or mobility needs. Keep a respectful distance from remains, follow site instructions and ask about photography. If an explanation includes local belief, record it as that person’s account, with permission to credit them.

The photograph you keep might show a broad view. The memory beside it could be much smaller: a material, a name, or the moment a few damaged letters made a place feel particular.

## Sources and reading notes

- [Bimal Bandyopadhyay, *Excavations at Udayagiri-2 (1997–2000)*, ASI, 2007](https://asi.nic.in/admin/publications/ePublicationReportsDetails/download/47). Preface and printed pp.1,123,141 checked in the original PDF on 10 October 2026. Inscription readings are Tripathy’s published interpretations, not a new decipherment by this project. No report image is reproduced.
- [Ministry of Culture briefing, 20 December 2018](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=186679). Historical account of the Lalitgiri caskets and museum prepared before its announced inauguration. It is not a current inventory, opening-hours notice or proof of the relics’ personal identity.
- [*The Great Tang Dynasty Record of the Western Regions*, translated by Li Rongxi, 1996](https://bdkamerica.org/download/1865), Fascicle X, printed pp.269–270. Passage and regional scope rechecked on 10 October. Figures and religious accounts remain attributed to this text; no modern census, enrolment or measured phenomenon is inferred.

[Related reading](../history/buddhist-learning.md) — Provides the chronology and separates excavation from literary testimony.

## Editorial development note

This expands the existing circuit concept, retaining its earlier direction, “Let the stone tell the story.” The original outline and source-backed opening remain in Git history. For an illustrated edition, pair a verified site view with an accurately captioned inscription or object detail only after checking access and image rights. Do not generate legible ancient lettering or a relic image and present it as documentary evidence.

The saved tourism brochure and two older tourism-page addresses returned 404 during this review. Historical claims above use the recovered original reports and museum briefing; current visiting arrangements remain unconfirmed. Archaeologist or community review, guide arrangements and an illustrated website edition are future work. No demand estimate, field visit, appointment or website publication is claimed by this article draft.

title: Editorial journey: coast, food and making
description: A coastal reading journey connecting Konark, Raghurajpur and Pipili through the ways stone and cloth carry stories.
body:
# Editorial journey: coast, food and making

**Follow the coast. Stay for the stories.**

A wheel, a painted scene, a seam. Three details can change the way you look at a journey through coastal Odisha. Each asks a different question of its material: how can stone suggest movement, how can a picture unfold, how can separate pieces of cloth become a whole?

Begin with those questions and a familiar sightseeing list becomes more personal. You might come home remembering the edge of a pattern as clearly as the outline of a monument.

## Start with a wheel

At [Konark](../places/konark.md), the Sun Temple takes the form of Surya’s chariot. UNESCO places it in the thirteenth-century reign of Narasimha Deva I and describes twelve pairs of carved wheels. Its account also draws attention to musicians and dancers among the sculptural reliefs.

Try looking at one wheel before trying to take in the entire building. Follow its rim and spokes with your eyes. Then look again from farther away. The detail and the whole offer different pleasures: a surface to examine, and a chariot to imagine moving.

Carry that attention towards one carved figure. What can you see in its posture? What would you want a knowledgeable guide to explain? Observation can begin a conversation without requiring you to guess the figure’s identity or turn your guess into history.

The reward is a different kind of photograph: one you can introduce with a detail you actually noticed. Keep to permitted viewing areas and leave the stone untouched.

## Let a picture take its time

At [Raghurajpur](../culture/raghurajpur-pattachitra.md), change the scale of your attention. Sucharita Sahoo’s 2014 PIB feature describes Pattachitra made on a canvas prepared from layers of cloth, with religious narratives and Jagannath-related subjects. The same account connects the village with Gotipua performance. These are cultural introductions from a dated feature, not a schedule of activities awaiting today’s visitor.

If an artist welcomes a conversation, ask where to begin reading one painting. Follow the part they choose: a gesture, a sequence, a border. Let their explanation guide you past the first impression of colour. A picture can reward the time you would normally give to a short story.

Our [painting and performance narrative](narratives/raghurajpur-painting-and-performance.md) follows this connection further through the documented life of Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra. Keep that deeper reading beside the visit rather than trying to fit every cultural subject into one stop. An artist’s working day and a troupe’s performance need separate arrangements.

## Turn the cloth over

In [Pipili](../culture/pipili-applique.md), look at how a pattern is assembled. The NID-authored process account on D’source describes coloured fabric cut and joined, with embroidery, mirrors and borders. Its lampshade example follows a cardboard stencil through repeated cloth pieces, machine stitching and a supporting ring.

Here is a useful question to take along: which decisions remain in the maker’s hands when a sewing machine enters the process? A tool does not choose a design or explain why a particular edge works. If a maker is willing to show you an unfinished piece, the construction may be as interesting as the finished surface.

Ask before handling or turning anything over. If you buy a piece, keep its maker’s name, materials and care instructions with the receipt. A well-introduced object brings more of the encounter home. The [Pipili story](narratives/pipili-cloth-and-ceremony.md) adds ceremonial context and questions for a workshop conversation.

Stone carved, cloth painted, cloth joined: this is a way of looking across three places. It is not a claim that their makers share one lineage, or that their traditions have stood still.

## Leave space around the encounters

[Puri](../places/puri.md) and [Chandrabhaga](../places/chandrabhaga.md) remain part of this coastal reading path. Let landscape, rest and a meal give the cultural stops room to breathe. [Mahaprasad](../food/mahaprasad.md) offers a food-and-hospitality chapter where appropriate access and context are established; temple entry must never be assumed. The [Taste Odisha story](taste-odisha.md) offers another way into food through cooks and preparation, with a meal planned around what is actually available.

Choose a focus before choosing how much to fit in. For a first visit, one monument and one agreed craft encounter might give you more to remember than a hurried attempt to see every stop. On a return journey, choose a single process you would like to understand better.

This is a narrative sequence, not a timed or confirmed route. Before making a visitor itinerary, establish the starting point, realistic travel durations, current opening and entry rules, hosts, seasonal conditions and suitable alternatives. Confirm access needs, rest stops and any demonstration fee. Ask permission for photographs and respect a maker’s decision to keep work or family spaces private.

A good question to carry home is simple: what did someone help you notice that you would otherwise have walked past?

<details>
<summary>Sources, credits and development notes</summary>

- [UNESCO Sun Temple, Konârak](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/246): description and Outstanding Universal Value passages inspected 10 October 2026; chariot, period, patron, wheels and sculptural subjects. Horse count omitted because the page’s sections disagree. Our observation prompts are original editorial suggestions.
- [The land of artisans: Raghurajpur](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=104817), Sucharita Sahoo, 11 April 2014: prepared cloth, narrative subjects and Gotipua context. No household count, livelihood outcome or current availability inferred. The district tourism endpoint timed out during this review; it supplies no new claims here.
- [Traditional Applique Work: Making Process](https://www.dsource.in/resource/traditional-pipli-applique-work-pipli-orissa/making-process), Prof. Bibhudutta Baral, Divyadarshan C. S. and Manasa K H, NID Bengaluru: process passage inspected 10 October 2026, consistent with our earlier saved narrative. The retrieved page also contains unrelated spam links; only its attributed craft passage is used. Market and employment claims are excluded.

Creative direction: **Ahimanikya Satapathy**. Research and original draft: current AI assistant. Source authors retain their credits. No field visit, interview, independent human review or participant relationship is claimed.

The earlier outline remains in Git revision `bb6998a8`. Its coastal anchors, food chapter, domestic and international audience directions, and unfinished itinerary and photography-permission work are preserved here. Future illustrated treatment should pair a permitted monument detail with credited process photographs agreed with their makers; no source photographs have been copied. International presentation should explain unfamiliar terms, while a domestic return-visit feature can follow one craft or food detail more closely. The existing research and visitor records own the facts and access questions; this article connects them rather than creating another destination catalogue.

</details>

body:
# Forest work: understanding the support behind the trade

A market story often starts with what was sold. A support story asks a different question: what happens when someone needs help? Both belong beside the work, but they should not be folded into one triumphant number.

Odisha’s Kendu Leaf Organisation records compassionate grants associated with death or permanent disability. That is a serious human context for a financial table. Read it with care: the amount tells us about a specific recorded category of assistance, not the quality of a person’s life or the full experience of a family.

## Read the total through its parts

In the FY2025–26 row, the page lists **1,132 records and ₹225,950,000** for pluckers and binders, and **103 records and ₹20,400,000** for seasonal staff. The count and amount add to the reported total retained below. The page’s “Nos” column does not establish a deduplicated count of people or households. [Compassionate Grant table](https://kenduleaves.odisha.gov.in/welfare-measures).

A count answers how many entries the table records. An amount answers how much it records for that category. Dividing one by the other would produce an arithmetic average per record, not a standard entitlement, a typical wage or the amount every family received. We do not use that shortcut to tell someone’s story.

## The dated support evidence

**₹24.635 crore in compassionate grants is recorded for FY2025–26** on Odisha's Kendu Leaf Organisation welfare page. The accompanying total is **1,235 grant records** across pluckers/binders and seasonal staff. [Official table](https://kenduleaves.odisha.gov.in/welfare-measures).

This is one specific form of support associated with death or permanent disability. It is not the whole welfare budget, the trade's sales value or the earnings of a typical collector. The page was read on 1 October 2026 and displays a 9 September update; individual payments have not been independently audited here.

| Follow the money | What the measure tells us |
| --- | --- |
| Sale proceeds | Value of marketed leaves |
| Wages and collection payments | Payment for work or leaf supply |
| Bonuses and incentives | Separate programme benefits |
| Compassionate grants | Support under a specific welfare category |

These rows are categories to distinguish, not an additive flow diagram. A larger compassionate-grant amount does not by itself show improved wellbeing. The [evidence view](../statistics/forest-products.md) retains prior years, the incomplete current year and unresolved totals elsewhere. An effective story should credit the people and explain the programme without confusing assistance with prosperity.

[Related reading](../statistics/forest-products.md) — Explains how payment categories differ; does not infer typical earnings or improved wellbeing from a grant total.

[The sale-proceeds allocation](../statistics/forest-products.md) now shows why advances, commissions and payable balances must remain separate from verified worker receipts. [Van Dhan enterprise reporting](van-dhan-enterprises.md) provides a different programme measure, with its historical date visible.

## Follow a record towards an actual receipt

A fuller account would follow a permitted case through its stages. Application, decision and receipt answer different questions. None should silently stand in for the next.

| Reporting question | Evidence to seek, with permission | What remains unproven |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Was support requested? | Dated application or acknowledgment, with unnecessary personal information excluded | A request does not establish eligibility or approval |
| What decision was made? | Applicable dated decision and the category it covers | Approval does not prove money reached the recipient |
| What was received, and when? | A privacy-protected payment record and the willing recipient’s account | An aggregate transfer does not establish each individual receipt |
| What did the support change? | The person’s permitted account, its timing and other relevant circumstances | One account cannot measure programme-wide wellbeing or establish causation |

These are reporting questions, not a claim that Utkal has inspected private files or interviewed a recipient. People can share an experience without sharing a diagnosis, bank information or the details of a bereavement. Permission to speak, to be named and to use a portrait are separate choices. Keep the person’s own words distinct from the department’s aggregate figures.

The [Kendu patra introduction](../economy/kendu-patra.md) opens the work-and-trade context. The [forest-enterprise story](van-dhan-enterprises.md) follows a different programme. Read them together without implying that their totals refer to the same recipients, financial years or payment categories.

## Let the visual explain the distinction

A later graphic should show four separate labelled cards: sale proceeds, work payments, bonuses and compassionate grants. Do not connect them with arrows that imply a verified money flow or add the figures into a household-income total. Pair the explanation with a verified, permitted image of actual work where useful; a photograph cannot prove benefit receipt. Avoid staged distress or a fictional beneficiary used to make the grant number emotional.

<details>
<summary>Evidence and editorial scope</summary>

The original welfare page was re-read on 11 October 2026. It still displayed the 9 September 2026 update and FY2025–26 counts/amounts retained here. Category addition and the rupee-to-crore conversion were recalculated. The separate welfare-expenditure table has an unspecified year basis; the partial2026–27 grant row has an unstated cutoff. Neither is substituted into this full-year story. Earlier draft, source identity, canonical observations and unresolved sales/payment issues remain preserved. This is not current eligibility guidance, a payment audit or independent wellbeing evaluation. Same-assistant editorial review is not human or participant review. No website or search selection changes.

</details>

title: Growing Odisha: numbers with a human setting
description: A reader story connecting fisheries, port activity and construction measures with the livelihood questions that deserve their own evidence.
body:
# Growing Odisha: numbers with a human setting

**See what is taking shape.**

What would make Odisha’s growth feel real to you? A steadier order book? More reliable work? A business that can reach its buyers without losing time or money along the way?

Those are personal questions. A state-level number cannot answer them alone, but it can point towards an activity worth understanding. Start with three different measures: fish produced, cargo handled and value added by construction. Each opens a door. The next part of the story asks who is on the other side.

## Follow the fish beyond the total

The Odisha Economic Survey 2025–26 reports fish production rising from **469.5 thousand tonnes in 2014–15 to 1,191.8 thousand tonnes in 2024–25**. That is a calculated **153.8% increase** over ten years. The [original comparison](../economy/comparison-01-fisheries.md) preserves this interval.

A later Department of Fisheries release, dated **9 July 2026**, reports **12.70 lakh tonnes for 2025–26**. Of that year’s reported components, freshwater accounts for 8.27 lakh tonnes. The sea is only one part of the production picture. The [fisheries record](../statistics/fisheries.md) keeps the newer release and its rounded components separate from the earlier survey table.

Now ask what a larger harvest means for someone trying to earn a living from it. What price did they receive? What did feed, fuel, ice or transport cost in their particular operation? Was there a buyer when the product was ready? These are questions for future reporting, not answers supplied by the production total.

A good feature could follow one consignment with a willing producer and document the steps between production and payment. That would give the reader a human setting for the statistic while leaving room for an experience that differs from the statewide trend. No such participant account has yet been collected for this article.

## A port measures movement

**Paradip handled 156.45 million tonnes of cargo in FY2025–26**, according to the Port Authority’s 1 April 2026 release. A 2017 Shipping Ministry reply records **76.39 million tonnes for FY2015–16**. The endpoint comparison is a calculated **104.8% increase**—more than twice the cargo over a decade.

One detail changes how that headline should be read. The port reports **65.81 million tonnes of coastal cargo**, representing **42.06%** of its FY2025–26 total. Its activity includes domestic coastal movement as well as overseas trade and serves a wider hinterland. These tonnes cannot all be described as Odisha-made exports. Our [Paradip evidence record](../trade/paradip-throughput.md) keeps that distinction visible.

For an entrepreneur, the useful next question may concern the journey to the ship: which service is needed, who supplies it, and where does a delay occur? For someone living near a transport corridor, the questions may concern access, working conditions or environmental effects. Cargo throughput provides a scale for that inquiry; it does not settle any of those experiences.

The port’s published expansion plans belong in a different part of the story. An expected completion date remains a plan until there is evidence that the facility is operating. A photograph of construction would not close that gap by itself.

## Keep the dip in the picture

Odisha’s construction **real gross state value added rose 62.2% between FY2019–20 and FY2024–25**, calculated from the survey’s constant-2011–12-price series. It fell in FY2020–21 before rising. Here is the full six-year interval, in **₹ crore**:

| Financial year | Construction real value added |
| --- | ---: |
| 2019–20 | 25,976.11 |
| 2020–21 | 23,648.15 |
| 2021–22 | 29,950.62 |
| 2022–23 | 32,934.07 |
| 2023–24 · second revised estimate | 38,465.22 |
| 2024–25 · first revised estimate | 42,144.69 |

The survey table is in ₹ lakh; the values above divide by 100. This measures economic value added after allowing for price changes. It is not a count of jobs or a total of public infrastructure spending. The [construction record](../economy/construction.md) retains the series and method.

Keeping the dip matters to the story. Two endpoints can describe an increase while concealing the uneven journey between them. Someone whose work depends on that activity may remember the difficult year as clearly as the later recovery. Finding out how requires listening, rather than assigning a memory to an unnamed worker.

## Bring the question back to people

These three measures are useful together because they ask us to look in different ways. They have different units, periods and coverage, so their growth rates must not be added into a single score. The [GDP story](../economy/gdp-story.md) provides a separate introduction to the economy’s overall scale.

For the next reported feature, choose one activity and one question that a participant wants to explain. Keep permission, attribution and the period of their account with the evidence. Then ask whether the wider number helps the reader understand that account—or whether it needs to stay in the background.

Odisha’s development deserves both kinds of attention: the scale visible in a table and the detail that becomes clear only when someone tells you how their work has changed. The ambition of *Growing Odisha* is to bring them together without making either speak for the other.

<details>
<summary>Sources, method and development notes</summary>

- [Odisha Economic Survey 2025–26](https://assembly.odisha.gov.in/WriteReadData/News/OES%202026%20WEB%20UPLOAD.pdf), Table 4.1, printed p.393/PDF p.440; Table 1.4 continuation, printed p.372/PDF p.419. Both pages rendered and inspected on 10 October 2026. Existing source identities `comparison-1-1` and `sector-survey` refer to the same publication.
- [Department of Fisheries release, 9 July 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2282817&lang=2&reg=48), Background section: later production and freshwater component. Existing ID `weekly-fisheries-jul2026`. No causal claim about its announced fishing mission is adopted.
- [Increasing efficiency of Major Ports, 18 December 2017](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1513070): Paradip row, FY2015–16 column. Existing ID `maritime-paradip-2016`.
- [Paradip Port Authority, 1 April 2026](https://paradipport.gov.in/all_news/paradip-port-registers-historic-high-cargo-handling-in-fy-25-26-best-ever-in-its-history/): annual cargo and coastal-cargo passages. Existing ID `maritime-paradip-2026`. Planned projects are not treated as completed. Web passages rechecked 10 October 2026.

Endpoint changes use `(end / start − 1) × 100`, rounded to one decimal place. They describe the stated periods, not uninterrupted annual growth. The existing [growth methodology](../methods/growth-calculations.md) and [industry data](../references/data/industry-growth-data.json) remain the calculation references. This story does not introduce a new economic dataset or claim a comprehensive update of all series.

Creative direction: **Ahimanikya Satapathy**. Source review and original draft: current AI assistant. No interview, field visit, independent human review or measured audience response is claimed.

The earlier campaign outline is preserved in Git revision `807c8e78`. Its three feature subjects and campaign line remain. For a future poster, use one measure with its period and source; for construction, retain all six annual points in a labelled chart. A short video can introduce the number once and spend its remaining time explaining the activity through a consenting participant. Planned investments belong in a separately labelled sequence distinguishing approval, groundbreaking and commercial operation. No images or participant footage are supplied or cleared in this draft.

</details>

body:
# Seventy years, from loom to market

**A textile has two journeys: the pattern becoming cloth, and the cloth finding someone who will wear it. Look closely enough, and a third journey appears—the maker’s name travelling with the work.**

Start with a border. Follow a line until it becomes a shape, then look back at the larger field of colour. The first impression may be delight; the next can be curiosity. Where did this pattern begin? In the yarn before weaving, in additional threads worked into the fabric, or in a combination of decisions?

These questions give an encounter with Odisha’s handlooms somewhere to go. You can enjoy a saree without knowing how it was made. Learning one detail, though, gives your eye a reason to return.

## Where the pattern enters

The India Handloom Brand description of [Khandua](../handlooms/khandua.md) follows groups of weft yarn through tying and dyeing before they enter the weave. Parts of the design are prepared in yarn: the finished fabric brings that preparation into view.

Its [Bomkai](../handlooms/bomkai.md) sheet describes additional warp threads in the border and additional weft threads in the body and pallu. The pallu is the saree’s decorated end. Here, a useful question is how those threads build the detail you are looking at.

These are attributed descriptions, not a test that can certify every piece in a shop. Ask someone knowledgeable to explain the particular cloth. If they point out a structure you had missed, pause with it. A tiny detail can change the way you see the whole surface.

## A name beside the cloth

An official Odisha weaver directory credits **Swarnalata Meher** with a silk-cotton Bapta saree described as a Mahalaxmi Gayatri composition. Its profile specifies silk warp, cotton weft and single ikat. On the following page, **Debaki Meher** is credited with a cotton Dasa Phulia saree combining weft ikat, additional border and end-panel threads, and calligraphy in the pallu.

The names matter. “Odisha handloom” offers a broad introduction; an identified work lets the story become more particular. A written composition becomes something to read as well as wear. Before translating its words or interpreting its religious meaning, ask for a reliable explanation of that specific piece.

The directory profiles are records of illustrated works. They do not tell us that these pieces are for sale today, identify the maker of another similar saree, or establish a current workshop appointment. They give us a better habit: ask whose work we are looking at, and preserve the answer when it is supported.

## The journey beyond the loom

In an account dated 14 May 2026, Boyanika describes its establishment in 1956 and its seventy-year milestone in May 2026. The institution presents retail, online sales and exhibitions as routes between weaving and customers. That is its own account of a market role, not an independent measurement of what each weaver earned.

For a reader, it opens a useful second set of questions. Who made the cloth? Who brought it to market? Who is selling this particular piece? Those roles may connect, but a retail label alone does not answer all three.

The earlier [market research](../handlooms/garments-and-markets.md) keeps product descriptions, cooperative associations and financial evidence separate. A named institution can help you begin an enquiry. Its anniversary cannot substitute for the story of a particular maker or transaction.

## Bring a question home

At a shop, ask for the textile name, fibre description, maker or production-group credit where documented, care instructions and a receipt. If an answer is unknown, let it remain a question. Do not turn a confident sales description into a verified biography.

A workshop encounter needs a separate arrangement. Confirm whether a visit or demonstration is welcome, what time and fee are agreed, and whether photography is permitted. A purchase is not permission to photograph a person, copy a design or interrupt work.

For your notebook, choose one detail: a border, a line of lettering, or the meeting of two colours. Record what you noticed, what was explained, and who should receive credit. You may carry home a textile; you can also carry home a more attentive way of looking.

## Sources and context

- [Boyanika’s institutional account, 14 May 2026](https://boyanika.com/boyanika-wear-your-heritage/). Re-read 10 October; its livelihood and growth language is not adopted as measured impact.
- India Handloom Brand: [Khandua](https://www.indiahandloombrand.gov.in/pages/downloadFile/khandua-saree.pdf) and [Bomkai](https://www.indiahandloombrand.gov.in/pages/downloadFile/bomkai-saree.pdf), technique sections, page 1. Product descriptions do not authenticate an individual purchase.
- [Official Odisha weaver directory](https://handlooms.nic.in/assets/img/Weavers%20Database/Odisha637322660372253324.pdf), PDF pages 10–11. Undated directory; named creation profiles, not current availability. Text and page images inspected 10 October. No directory image is reproduced here.

Editorial direction: Ahimanikya Satapathy. Developed with AI assistance from existing research and rechecked sources; no interview or field visit claimed. [Claim and reuse review](../../records/loom-market-story-review-2026-10-10.json).

<details>
<summary>Editorial development and future images</summary>

This develops the 2 October story seed in place; the earlier wording remains in Git history. Retain its visual ideas for a later illustrated edition: a dated institutional timeline, textile details showing where patterns enter, and a close view of lettering with a named creator’s explanation. The earlier Sarat Kumar Patra example remains in the [structured research](../references/data/handloom-markets.json); its documented piece must not be relabelled Khandua without evidence.

Obtain licensed or commissioned images and the necessary maker permissions. No rights are inferred from the PDFs. Keep any making-duration figure tied to its illustrated work and source wording; do not infer typical lead times, wages or productivity. This remains a KB article draft, outside the website publication and search selection.

</details>

body:
# Institution building, measured one stage at a time

An education story begins with a possibility: someone gets the chance to study, and a different future becomes imaginable. How do we tell that story without making the possibility stand in for the result? Follow three separate questions—what institution is being described, what resources it reports, and what students experience.

KISS Deemed to be University provides a dated case for that approach. Its records give us something concrete to read. They also show why an institution’s scale and a student’s outcome need different evidence.

## First, know which institution is in the frame

The **25 August 2017 notification** explicitly distinguishes the proposed deemed university from the school run by KISS. Its school de-linking condition and stated compliance appear on page 2. That is a historical legal stage, not a current programme-approval check. University accounts and university student rows should not be turned into combined figures for the school, Foundation or KIIT. [Notification, p.2](https://university.kiss.ac.in/docs/IIQA/KISS-DU-NOTIFICATION-DT-25.08.2017.pdf).

This boundary makes the story more useful: a reader can follow a named institution instead of an impressive number whose population changes from sentence to sentence.

## What the accounts let us see

The university-labelled income and expenditure statement reports **₹25.20 crore in total expenses for FY2024–25**. Its prior-year comparative column reports **₹24.02 crore for FY2023–24**. The exact totals are ₹252,023,295 and ₹240,170,499; their change is about **4.94% in nominal rupees**. These are expense figures including depreciation and amortisation, not cash payments or a measured improvement in education. Signatures are visible on the statement; a separate audit opinion has not been established by this review. [Statement, p.2](https://university.kiss.ac.in/docs/Accounts/Balance_Sheets/KISSDU_FY_2024-25.pdf).

For a later illustration, two bars could show that financial scale, with the institution, financial years and nominal basis printed directly beside them. A larger bar would mean a larger reported expense total. It would not mean a larger change in students’ lives.

## A different lens: tuition support

The **2025 NIRF SDG submission** reports **948 students across two-year postgraduate programmes**, with full tuition reimbursement from institutional funds recorded for all 948. The row covers programme years together and supplies no explicit census day. It is a university submission about tuition support, not a current enrolment total, a promise to applicants or evidence that every living cost is covered. [Submission, p.1](https://university.kiss.ac.in/docs/NIRF/SDG_Institutions.pdf).

The human question is easy to understand: what does removing a tuition charge make possible for a student? The row gives a reason to ask that question. It does not supply the student’s answer, demonstrate learning gains or establish an employment outcome. No participant account has been collected for this draft.

Keep the support count beside the accounts as a separate panel. **Do not divide total university expenses by 948 to invent a cost per student:** the expense statement and that particular PG population do not establish a matching accounting scope and period.

## Three questions to carry into the next story

| Lens | What this case supplies | What a richer account still needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Institution | A historical university notification with a school boundary | Original founding-stage records and current programme information |
| Resources | A dated university-labelled expense statement | Separate audit opinion and reconciliation of held accounting questions |
| Access and experience | Institution-reported PG tuition support | Actual student perspectives, cohort outcomes and evidence over time |

These are reporting questions, not a new evaluation of the institution. With permission and suitable evidence, a future student account could explain a course, an aspiration or what changed after study. We cannot substitute an imagined voice for that work.

[Achyuta Samanta’s education-building record](../people/achyuta-samanta.md) connects separately attributed founder history, legal stages and the remaining research. It preserves conflicting founding-year accounts and financial-presentation questions rather than smoothing them into one origin story. [Bhubaneswar beyond the rank](odisha-university-evidence.md) offers another way to read education numbers, keeping ranks and graduate cohorts apart.

<details>
<summary>Evidence and editorial scope</summary>

Original FY2024–25 statement p.2, the 2017 notification p.2 and the NIRF2025 PG row p.1 were visually checked on 11 October 2026. Existing [learning research](../references/data/culture-learning.json) retains exact values, financial vintages and unresolved scope issues. This review does not reconcile earlier account notes or the income-component differences between presentations, or obtain original school/society registration, an independent audit opinion or participant research. No causal impact, current admissions assurance, combined institution total or per-student cost is claimed. This remains a KB editorial draft, with no independent human review or website publication.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Earlier research draft, preserved</summary>

**₹25.20 crore in reported university expenses, FY 2024–25.** KISS Deemed to be University’s signed statement gives a concrete financial scale for one part of Odisha’s education landscape.

The prior-year column is ₹24.02 crore: about 4.94% nominal growth. Expenses include depreciation; the figures are neither cash spending nor measured social impact. They cover the university, not the KISS school, Foundation or KIIT. [Statement, p.2](https://university.kiss.ac.in/docs/Accounts/Balance_Sheets/KISSDU_FY_2024-25.pdf).

The original university notification explicitly distinguishes the school. Keep that boundary visible when connecting institutions, money and students. [Notification, p.2](https://university.kiss.ac.in/docs/IIQA/KISS-DU-NOTIFICATION-DT-25.08.2017.pdf).

[Explore Achyuta Samanta’s journey](../people/achyuta-samanta.md) for parliamentary service, legal milestones and the unanswered outcome questions. Suggested visual: two labelled expense bars with the entity, financial years and nominal basis visible. Editorial draft; no human review or website publication claimed.

[Related reading](../people/achyuta-samanta.md) — Links a scoped institutional financial statement to founder history without equating spending with social impact.

## A second lens: access to postgraduate study

**948 postgraduate students with institution-funded full tuition reimbursement** are reported in KISS’s 2025 NIRF SDG submission. This covers two-year PG programmes across study years, with no explicit census day on the row. It is institution-reported tuition support, not proof of independently measured learning or employment impact. [Submission, p.1](https://university.kiss.ac.in/docs/NIRF/SDG_Institutions.pdf).

Use this as a separate access card alongside the financial story; do not divide expenses by this PG count to invent per-student costs. [Detailed outcomes and limitations](../people/achyuta-samanta.md).

## Preserve the accounts’ vintages

The FY2023–24 original and later comparative statement agree on the ₹24.02crore total but differ in the grants/other-income split. The total-based comparison above is unchanged; component-level growth stays on hold. The original file’s notes mix society/Delhi references and2021 balances with university headings, so further scope reconciliation is needed. [Original accounts, pp.2,11–12](https://university.kiss.ac.in/docs/Accounts/Balance_Sheets/KISSDU_FY_2023-24.pdf). [Exact comparison and founding-stage limits](../people/achyuta-samanta.md).

</details>

title: Koraput through a book a cup and a cloth
description: A reader journey connecting Koraput, Gopinath Mohanty, coffee, Kalajeera rice and Kotpad textiles.
body:
# Koraput through a book a cup and a cloth

Before choosing the photograph you want to bring home from Koraput, choose a question. It might begin with a novel: whose account of a place are you reading? It might begin with coffee: who grew what is in your cup? Or with a piece of cloth: how did that colour reach the thread?

These are three ways into a region whose landscape can be the beginning of a much longer interest. Koraput lies along the Eastern Ghats in southern Odisha. The district administration’s introduction brings hills, agriculture, coffee and Kotpad fabrics into the same account. Give those connections time. A view may draw you here; learning to notice the work within it can give you a reason to return.

## Begin with a book

[Gopinath Mohanty](../people/gopinath-mohanty.md) offers a literary doorway. His memorial biography connects his early administrative posting in Koraput with an interest in local languages and lives. Its introduction to [Paraja](../works/paraja.md) describes a struggle between people subjected to exploitation and those exercising power over them.

You can carry that question into your reading without turning every present-day encounter into an illustration of the novel. Who gets to explain what happens? What does the narrator let you hear? Keep your own response beside a passage in the edition you read. A fictional character, an author’s viewpoint and a living person’s account each deserve their own space.

For English readers, an Oxford-published bibliography identifies *Paraja: A Novel*, translated by **Bikram K. Das**, in a 1987 Oxford University Press edition. Keep the translator’s name with the title when you recommend it. Check the edition you obtain; the publication date of a later listing is not automatically the date of that translation.

This reading can begin well before the journey, in a library or at home. It can also continue afterwards, when a detail you overlooked acquires a different weight. The novel is an invitation to pay attention, not a substitute for hearing contemporary people describe their own lives.

## Follow an ingredient back

The district administration names Koraput Tribal Coffee among the region’s products. That gives you a starting point for a conversation over a cup. Ask which producer or farm supplied it and how it was processed, if the seller knows. Write down the answer as an attributed account. A regional name becomes more interesting when it leads to a particular person, organisation or growing place.

Rice opens another door. The Geographical Indications register lists **Koraput Kalajeera Rice**, application 814, as registered, with a certificate dated 2 January 2024. If you find it offered during your visit, ask what rice is being served and where it came from. Registration of a named product does not identify the grain in every bowl or packet.

Let a willing cook explain their preparation before supplying your own description of it. Ask how they like to eat it, what they call it, and whether they would like their account shared. Your notebook can hold an ingredient name and a person’s preferred credit as carefully as it holds a photograph. The [rice collection](../food/rice-varieties.md) gives further reading, including the distinction between Kalajeera and the improved selection Nua Kalajeera.

## Look closely at Kotpad

A textile can make the same journey from broad impression to particular knowledge. Our [Kotpad record](../handlooms/kotpad.md) draws on a government-hosted account associating Mirgan weavers with aul-root dyes and colours including red, maroon, brown and black. That is an introduction to a tradition. A particular piece still has its own fibre, maker and history.

Before a possible visit, follow the producer’s listing for **Biswanath Rath’s *Kotpad Weaving: The Story of a Race Against Time***. PSBT identifies it as a 2018 documentary, 29 minutes long, in Odia and English. Use its official listing to investigate viewing or screening options; the catalogue is not a promise of free streaming.

At a shop, start with one detail that attracts you. Ask about its material and maker, the process behind its colour, and how to care for it. If a workshop visit is possible, arrange it separately with a willing host. Agree the time and any fee, and ask before photographing people, work or designs. A person absorbed in making is working; leave room for their pace.

## Leave room in the journey

Use [Deomali](../places/deomali.md), [Koraput](../places/koraput.md), coffee, rice and Kotpad as interests to investigate, not a checklist to squeeze into a day. Choose one main purpose for an outing. Confirm the route, weather, access and a realistic return with a current local source before adding another stop.

Carry three spaces in your notes: something you noticed, something someone chose to explain, and something you still want to understand. Keep the name of the speaker with their permission. Ask which language they prefer for the conversation, and welcome an answer that changes your original idea.

You may return with a book to finish, a producer’s name to remember or a cloth whose details you now recognise. That is a good beginning for a second visit.

## Sources and further reading

- [Koraput district introduction](https://koraput.odisha.gov.in/en/about-district/about-us). Rechecked 10 October 2026 for regional setting, coffee and Kotpad associations. Its transport schedules and superlatives are not adopted here.
- [Gopinath Mohanty memorial life sketch](https://gopinathmohanty.in/life-sketch/) and [Paraja introduction](https://gopinathmohanty.in/literary-creations/immortal-novels/paraja/). Rechecked 10 October. The memorial’s description supplies the short thematic introduction; the reading questions are ours. No passage from the novel is reproduced or presented as a close reading.
- [Oxford bibliography in Jean Drèze’s *Sense and Solidarity*](https://academic.oup.com/book/35106/chapter/299186110), Mohanty 1987 entry. Rechecked for edition and translation credit; the 1987 title page was not inspected.
- [Koraput Kalajeera Rice registration entry](https://search.ipindia.gov.in/GIRPublicSearch/Application/Details/814). Rechecked 10 October for the named product, registration status and certificate date; no seller or packet authenticated.
- [Sustainability in the Handloom Traditions of India](https://handlooms.nic.in/assets/img/EBOOK/Sustainability%20in%20the%20Handloom%20Traditions%20of%20India.pdf), printed p.36. Reuses the project’s 1 October inspection of this bounded Kotpad section. A fresh web-reader request failed; no fresh PDF inspection is claimed.
- [PSBT film catalogue](https://psbt.org/films/kotpad-weaving-the-story-of-a-race-against-time/). Rechecked 10 October for filmmaker, year, duration and languages. The film itself was not reviewed and no footage is reproduced.

## Editorial development note

This expands the earlier landscape-to-making journey concept in place. Its proposed opening, “A landscape you can taste. A story you can take home,” remains part of that history in Git. The next illustrated edition should begin with an accurately identified landscape and connect it to a permitted detail of food or cloth. Reuse existing credited Koraput assets after checking their subject and rights; any new portrait or process photograph needs specific permission and context. No new image or imagined field encounter is supplied by this draft.

The original producer, cook and maker conversations remain future work with named, willing participants. Travel logistics, current availability and workshop access still require confirmation. Deomali’s unresolved elevation is not used as a headline claim. No interviews, community review or website publication are claimed here.
